Nitakusifu; kwa maana nimeumbwa kwa jinsi ya ajabu na ya kutisha; kazi zako ni za ajabu, na nafsi yangu yajua sana –Zaburi 139:14.

Tunaishi katika ulimwengu uliojaa bakteria na virusi. Inakadiriwa kuwa kuna bakteria trilioni 100 katika mwili wa wastani wa binadamu. Hii ni idadi kubwa sana kiasi kwamba siwezi kuielewa. Kwa kawaida, bakteria hawa hawana sumu hadi wanapokosa uwiano au kufika mahali ambapo hawakukusudiwa kuwa. Mungu ametuumba kwa namna ambayo miili yetu ina uwezo wa ajabu wa kujikinga na magonjwa.

Seli zinazotengeneza kingamwili na seli T huzunguka katika mikondo yetu ya damu kama walinzi, zikingojea seli za kigeni au sumu zitokee. Shughuli rahisi kama kupiga mswaki au kujikwaruza mkononi inaweza kuachia bakteria ndani ya mkondo wa damu. Kama si mifumo yetu ya kinga tuliyopewa na Mungu, bakteria hao wangeweza kujishikiza kwenye tishu mbalimbali na kusababisha maambukizi makubwa.

Ni muhimu tuelewe baadhi ya mambo kuhusu mfumo wetu wa kinga na kufikiria njia tunazoweza kuusaidia ufanye kazi vizuri zaidi.

Hapo Mwanzo

Baada ya kumaliza, …Mungu akaona kila kitu alichokifanya, na tazama, kilikuwa chema sana… –Mwanzo 1:31. Hii haimaanishi tu kwamba kilionekana kizuri, ingawa kilikuwa hivyo. Pia inamaanisha kwamba wakati huo Uumbaji wote ulikuwa ukifanya kazi kwa pamoja. Hakukuwa na bakteria waliosababisha magonjwa wala virusi hatari. Adamu na Hawa waliumbwa kikamilifu na hawakuhitaji viuavijasumu au probiotiki kupambana na maambukizi.

Kabla ya Anguko, hakukuwa na haja ya mfumo wa kinga kama tunavyouhitaji leo. Inawezekana sana kwamba mfumo wa kinga wa wakati huo ulifanya kazi zaidi kama mfumo wa kuondoa taka, ukiondoa seli zilizohitaji kusafishwa.

Baada ya Anguko, kila kitu kilikuwa tofauti. Bakteria na virusi vikaanza kuwa “viletavyo magonjwa” au visababishavyo magonjwa.

Sehemu za Mifumo Yetu ya Kinga

Watu wanapofikiria kuhusu mfumo wa kinga, mara nyingi hufikiria seli zinazotengeneza kingamwili. Hizi ni sehemu muhimu sana ya ulinzi wa miili yetu, lakini kuna sehemu nyingine nyingi pia.

a.

Mstari wetu wa kwanza wa ulinzi dhidi ya maambukizi mengi ni ngozi yetu. Kufunikwa kwa mwili wetu na ngozi nzima, iliyo na bakteria wenye afya juu ya uso wake, kunaweza kuzuia viumbe visivyo na afya kuingia kwenye tishu zilizo chini ya ngozi na hata kwenye mkondo wa damu.

Nimeona maambukizi mengi makubwa yaliyotokea baada ya matukio ambayo ngozi ilipasuka. Kitu chochote kuanzia kukanyaga msumari hadi kuumwa na mbwa kinaweza kusababisha maambukizi.

b. Mfumo wa Limfu…

Tunapofikiria kuhusu mzunguko wa damu, jambo la kwanza linalotujia akilini ni mfumo wa damu wenye mishipa, ateri na moyo. Kuna mfumo mwingine, unaoitwa mfumo wa limfu, ambao una jukumu la kusafirisha seli za damu zinazopambana na maambukizi mwilini kote na kuondoa vitu vyenye sumu.

Kuna sehemu ndogo za kuchuja katika mfumo huu zinazoitwa nodi za limfu, ambazo huvimba zinapopambana na maambukizi. Mara nyingi mtu anapokuwa na maambukizi ya njia ya juu ya upumuaji, atagundua kwamba tezi za limfu kwenye shingo yake zimevimba. Hii ni ishara kwamba mfumo wa kinga unafanya kazi inayopaswa kufanya.

c. Uboho/Wengu…

Uboho hutengeneza seli zinazopambana na maambukizi. Nyingi ya seli hizi huhifadhiwa kwenye wengu, ambao hufanya kazi kama kichujio kikubwa cha damu. Mwili unapogundua aina yoyote ya maambukizi, seli hizi zinazopambana na maambukizi huachiliwa kwenye mkondo wa damu na kwenye mfumo wa limfu ili kupambana na bakteria au virusi vinavyosababisha maambukizi hayo.

Kwa hiyo, watu ambao hawana wengu wako katika hatari kubwa zaidi ya kupata aina fulani za maambukizi.

d. Seli za Kinga…

“Askari” wa mfumo wetu wa kinga ni seli nyeupe za damu, seli B (zinazotengeneza kingamwili) na seli T. Hizi ndizo seli zinazojibu kila uvamizi wa mwili wetu.

e. Mfumo wa Kichochezi…

Huu ni mfumo ambao watu wengi hawaufahamu sana. Mfumo huu unajumuisha ini, ambalo hutengeneza protini ndogo zinazosaidia seli za kinga kufanya kazi vizuri zaidi na kufanya kingamwili ziwe na ufanisi zaidi. Protini hizi huzunguka zikiwa katika hali isiyotenda kazi hadi kunapokuwa na ishara ya maambukizi; kisha vimeng’enya fulani huzifanya ziwe tayari kusaidia mwitikio wa kupambana na maambukizi.

Mambo Yanayodhuru Mifumo Yetu ya Kinga

Kuna mambo kadhaa yanayodhoofisha mifumo yetu ya kinga na kuifanya ishindwe kujibu maambukizi ipasavyo. Kwa kweli, mambo haya yote huchangia kudhoofisha ulinzi wa miili yetu.

  1. Mlo usiofaa
  2. Mienendo mibaya ya usingizi
  3. Baadhi ya dawa (hasa steroidi)
  4. Kisukari kisichodhibitiwa vizuri (au ugonjwa mwingine wowote unaodhoofisha mwili)

Isitoshe, viwango vya juu vya wasiwasi huachilia homoni za msongo mwilini, ambazo zinaweza kusababisha kinga dhaifu.

Kujaribu kuondoa mambo haya ni mwanzo, lakini tunapaswa pia kuhakikisha tunayabadilisha kwa mtindo wa maisha wenye afya. Mambo mengi yanayoimarisha mifumo yetu ya kinga ni dhahiri, lakini hilo halimaanishi kwamba tunafanya mambo hayo vizuri kila wakati. Huenda tumejenga mazoea yasiyo na afya au labda hatukuwahi kufundishwa baadhi ya uchaguzi wa mtindo wa maisha wenye afya.

Kula Vyakula Vinavyofaa

Hakuna chakula au juisi moja maalumu tunayoweza kutumia itakayotufikisha kwenye hali bora ya afya. Badala yake, tunahitaji mchanganyiko wa vyakula vyenye afya tunavyokula na vile visivyo na afya tunavyopunguza.

Jambo la kwanza ninalofikiria ninapozungumzia “vyakula vinavyofaa” ni vizuiaoksidishaji. Vizuiaoksidishaji ni kemikali zinazofunga molekuli hatari katika miili yetu zinazoitwa “radikali huru.” Radikali huru nyingi mno zinaweza kusababisha magonjwa ya kila aina, yakiwemo kisukari na saratani. Bila shaka, sehemu nyingine za miili yetu, kama vile mfumo wetu wa kinga, pia hazifanyi kazi vizuri katika hali hii.

Vyakula vyenye nitrati nyingi zilizoongezwa, kama vile nyama zilizohifadhiwa kwa kuponywa, huwa vinaongeza sana radikali hizi huru na vinapaswa kuepukwa.

Kula matunda na mboga nyingi husaidia sana kuongeza viwango vya vitamini mwilini kwa njia ya asili (hasa Vitamini C). Kula mafuta yenye afya (yale yenye asidi nyingi za mafuta za omega-3) na kuepuka yale yasiyo na afya (yale yenye mafuta mengi yaliyojaa) huenda pia kukaboresha uwezo wetu wa kupambana na maambukizi.

Pata Usingizi wa Kutosha (na Mzuri)

Tafiti zimechunguza hatari ya kupata mafua ya kawaida na kugundua kuwa watu waliolala kwa muda mfupi walikuwa na uwezekano mkubwa zaidi wa kupata mafua. Inaonekana kuwa kiwango cha chini ni takriban saa sita kwa watu wazima (huenda ikawa zaidi kwa vijana na watoto).1

Hili linaeleweka kwa kuwa miili yetu hupona zaidi tunapokuwa tumelala. Ukiamka bila kujisikia umepumzika, ni muhimu kujua sababu. Mambo kama kutolala kwa muda wa kutosha tu, usafi duni wa usingizi (kama vile kwenda kulala ukiwaza kuhusu mahangaiko, au kufanya kazi hadi karibu na wakati wa kulala), na tatizo la kukosa hewa wakati wa usingizi, yote yanaweza kusababisha usingizi usiourudishii mwili nguvu.

Mungu aliiumba miili yetu ikiwa na uhitaji wa kupumzika, na akaweka siku kwa kusudi hilo. Kama hakuna jingine, huu ndio ujumbe wa Siku ya Sabato (ona Kutoka 20:8-11).

Fikiria Kuhusu Probiotiki

Katika miaka ya 1800, watu kama Joseph Lister na Louis Pasteur waliendeleza nadharia ya vijidudu kuhusu magonjwa. Waliamini kuwa bakteria (wakati huo hawakuwa bado wanajua kuhusu virusi) ndio waliosababisha magonjwa mengi. Hili lilimwongoza Joseph Lister kuwa mwanzilishi wa utakasaji wa vifaa vya upasuaji.

Katika miaka iliyofuata, tumebaini kwamba si bakteria wote ni “wasababishao magonjwa.” Bakteria wengi kwenye ngozi yetu na katika njia yetu ya chakula ni bakteria wazuri. Bakteria hawa wazuri husaidia usagaji wa chakula na hutulinda dhidi ya bakteria wanaosababisha magonjwa (au wabaya) wanaoingia na kutuletea matatizo.

Probiotiki hupatikana kwenye mtindi na kefiri, na pia kwenye vyakula vingine vingi. Probiotiki pia zinaweza kutumiwa kama virutubisho kupitia kapsuli au matone.

Utafiti mmoja uliwapa watoto 326 probiotiki au placebo wakati wa msimu wa mafua. Watoto waliokuwa wakipokea probiotiki walikuwa na magonjwa ya njia ya upumuaji na homa chache zaidi kwa kiasi kikubwa katika kipindi hicho cha miezi sita.2

Watu wanaojumuisha vyakula hivi katika mlo wao na kutumia baadhi ya virutubisho vya probiotiki huwa na afya bora na mifumo imara zaidi ya kinga.

Punguza Ulaji wa Sukari

Tunajua kwamba unene kupita kiasi na kisukari kisichodhibitiwa huongeza hatari ya maambukizi, madogo na makubwa. Inaonekana kwamba sukari inapokuwa nyingi mno ikizunguka kwenye mkondo wa damu, huipa bakteria wabaya virutubishi wanavyohitaji ili kukua haraka, na husababisha mifumo ya kinga isifanye kazi vizuri.

Seli nyeupe za damu zinapozungukwa na sukari nyingi, uwezo wake wa kufanya “fagosaitosisi” (mchakato wa kumeza) hupungua, na uwezo wake wa kuzuia uvamizi wa bakteria au virusi wabaya pia hupungua.3

Huenda tukapata ugumu wa kuondoa sukari yote katika mlo wetu, lakini inaonekana kwamba kuipunguza kunaleta tofauti kubwa katika jinsi miili yetu inavyoweza kupambana na maambukizi.

Fanya Mazoezi Mara kwa Mara

Pengine ni wazi, lakini kusubiri hadi uhisi kana kwamba mafua yanakuja kisha kukimbilia nje ili kukimbia maili tatu huenda kusikusaidie. Kwa kweli, kunaweza kukufanya ujisikie vibaya zaidi unapokabiliana na mwili ambao haujazoea kufanya mazoezi na ambao pia unapambana na maambukizi.

Jambo la msingi hapa ni kiasi cha wastani. Viwango vya juu sana vya shughuli za kimwili, kama vile vya wanariadha wa mashindano wanaojiandaa kwa mbio au tukio kubwa, vinaonekana kuongeza hatari ya maambukizi. Hata hivyo, kufanya mazoezi kwa kiwango cha wastani kwa dakika 30 kwa siku, siku tano kwa wiki, ni ushauri mzuri wa kufuata ili tuweze kuutayarisha mwili wetu, tupate mioyo yenye afya pamoja na mifumo mingine yenye afya itakayotulinda dhidi ya wavamizi hao wa nje wasioonekana.

Punguza Msongo

“Mungu mpendwa…
Nijalie [neema] ya kukubali mambo nisiyoweza kuyabadilisha,
[na] ujasiri wa kubadilisha mambo [ninayoweza],
na [hekima] ya kutambua tofauti.”

Kuinuka kwa muda mrefu kwa viwango vya homoni za msongo kunadhuru miili yetu. Homoni za msongo huongeza shinikizo la damu na kasi ya mapigo ya moyo. Huongeza sukari ya damu na huwa zinaongeza miitikio ya uchochezi katika miili yetu.4

Kimsingi, homoni za msongo hufanya mambo yote yanayohitajika ndani ya mwili wako ili kukuandaa endapo hali itatokea na ukahitaji kukimbia hatari kubwa, kama vile dubu mkubwa wa grizzly anayekukimbilia. Hata hivyo, kiwango hiki cha juu cha homoni za msongo hakisaidii sana unapokabiliana na tatizo la afya la mtoto au ugumu wa kifedha wa familia.

Kila mmoja wetu amewahi kukabiliwa na wasiwasi. Hata hivyo, kuishi katika hali ya wasiwasi wa kudumu si jambo lenye afya, wala si hali ambayo Mungu anataka kuwaona watu wake wakiishi ndani yake. Kwa mtazamo wa Kikristo, lengo letu lazima liwe kumkabidhi Mungu mahangaiko haya. Huku mkimtwika yeye fadhaa zenu zote, kwa maana yeye hujishughulisha sana kwa mambo yenu –1 Petro 5:7. Hatuhitaji kuishi na wasiwasi pamoja na mabadiliko yote mabaya unayoweza kuleta kwenye afya yetu ya kimwili.

Tumia Muda Nje

Watu wanapofikiria kuhusu mwanga wa jua, kwa kiasi kikubwa huonekana kufikiria kuhusu Vitamini D.

Ni kweli kwamba Vitamini D huzalishwa ngozi yetu inapopigwa na mwanga wa jua, lakini mwanga wa jua hufanya mengi zaidi. Kwa mfano, inaonekana kwamba mwanga wa jua huwezesha seli zetu za kinga kufanya kazi kwa ubora wa juu katika kupambana na maambukizi. Kimsingi, seli T husonga kwa kasi zaidi na kwa ufanisi zaidi zinapoangaziwa na mwanga wa jua.5 Pia, kupigwa na mwanga wa jua huongeza viwango vya oksidi ya nitriki katika miili yetu. Hii husaidia kupanua mishipa ya damu, kupunguza shinikizo la damu, na ni kemikali yenye manufaa kwa moyo.

Kama ilivyo kwa mambo yote niliyotaja, jambo la msingi ni kufanya kwa kiasi. Kukaa juani kwenye joto kwa muda mrefu kupita kiasi kunaweza kusababisha kiharusi cha joto, na mwanga mwingi wa urujuanimno hudhuru seli za ngozi yetu, jambo linaloweza kusababisha kuungua na hata saratani za ngozi.

Virutubisho Maalumu

Virutubisho vinaweza kusaidia kujazia mapengo katika mlo wetu au pale ambapo miili yetu haifyonzi kiasi cha kutosha cha kitu fulani.

Vitamini D ni mojawapo ya vinavyonijia akilini, kwa kuwa tunajua kwamba viwango vya chini vya Vitamini D huongeza hatari ya maambukizi makubwa. Miili yetu haijui hasa Vitamini D inatoka wapi. Ingawa huenda njia bora zaidi ni kuipata kupitia mchanganyiko wa chakula na kupigwa na mwanga wa jua, kuongeza virutubisho vya Vitamini D kunaweza kusaidia watu wazee au mtu yeyote ambaye ana shida ya kupata kiasi hicho.6

Zinki imeonyeshwa (kwa muda mfupi) kupunguza muda wa mafua. Ningetoa tahadhari hapa kwamba haikukusudiwa hasa kutumiwa kila siku; badala yake, inapaswa kutumiwa zaidi dalili ya kwanza ya kuanza kwa maambukizi ya njia ya juu ya upumuaji inapoonekana. Hiki si kirutubisho cha kimiujiza, na katika tafiti kilipunguza tu muda wa dalili za mafua kwa takriban siku moja.7

Vitamini C ni kitu kingine ambacho watu wengi hutumia wanapohisi mafua yanakuja. Tafiti zinaonekana kuashiria kwamba huvumilika vizuri na ni chenye ufanisi.8 Pengine ni bora kupata sehemu kubwa ya Vitamini C yako kupitia mlo wako na kuongeza Vitamini C ya ziada tu unapoanza kuhisi dalili za maambukizi.

Kuna virutubisho vingine vingi ambavyo watu hutumia; hivi ni vitatu tu kati ya vile vinavyotumiwa sana.

Mungu aliiumba miili yetu ikiwa na mifumo mingi tofauti. Mifumo hii huponya majeraha, hudumisha miili yetu, na huilinda dhidi ya ulimwengu ulioharibiwa na kuingizwa kwa dhambi wakati wa Anguko la mwanadamu, katika Bustani ya Edeni. Kwa kweli tumeumbwa kwa jinsi ya ajabu na ya kutisha. Mifumo hii hufanya kazi bila sisi hata kufikiria kuihusu.

Ni muhimu tutambue njia tunazoweza kusaidia, na tusizozuia, seli na miundo hii iliyoundwa kwa namna ya ajabu, ambayo huzuia viumbe hatari kuingia katika miili yetu na kusababisha maambukizi. Si kwamba kuishi kwa afya au kuwa mtoto wa Mungu kutatuzuia tusiugue kamwe, bali ni kwamba kufanya uamuzi wa makusudi wa kufuata njia iliyo sahihi kutaboresha utendaji wa mwili wetu. Ninaamini kwamba tukiwa na afya njema, itakuwa rahisi zaidi kwetu kutimiza utume wetu—kuifikia dunia inayotuzunguka kwa ujumbe wa Injili.

Something that I have noticed repeatedly as I read God’s Word is that God’s people are confident. Consider Noah. When God told him to build an ark, there was no wavering. He spent the next 120 years confidently doing just that. Then I think of Abraham confidently doing whatever God asked of him, even when He asked him to sacrifice his only son. We cannot speak of confidence without mentioning Caleb and Joshua, who after hearing all their comrades give their doubting reports, confidently described what they should do with this new land of Canaan: …Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it –Numbers 13:30.

We cannot forget about David who went out and silenced the large naysayer—Goliath. Nor can we forget Daniel, Gideon, Job, Ezekiel, Isaiah, or Jeremiah and all that they did with confidence. As we study each of these men of faith and many others, we clearly see that they had a great amount of confidence in their God!

Some might say that if God worked the same way today as He did back then, we would be more confident. Maybe if God were still an Old Testament God, it would be easier. If He led us into battle, destroyed our enemies, parted seas, and caused bread to fall from heaven, then we would have more confidence in Him.

Now let us consider the New Testament. It is quite different. God’s people are commanded to leave everything for the sake of Christ. They are promised that the world will hate them. They are told that it is difficult for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. They are guaranteed that they will be blessed if they suffer, if they are poor, if they are hungry, and if they mourn.

Can people still have confidence in a God that asks His people to follow Him under these circumstances? Yes! The disciples proved it. They went about preaching and teaching. They were hunted and beaten repeatedly. The deacon, Stephen, showed great confidence when he was brought before his oppressors, even when they began to gnash their teeth at him, and stone him. Stephen showed confidence until he took his last agonizing breath.

Before he became the apostle Paul, Saul was an enemy of the cross, the chiefest of sinners, and a Pharisee of the Pharisees. He was a prominent man, taught by the best. Then he met the living God, and everything changed. After Paul was baptized, …straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God –Acts 9:20. The next verse says the people were amazed, then in verse 23, five verses after he was baptized, it says that the Jews took counsel to kill him.

It takes a lot of confidence in God to change a man like that, to cause him to, overnight, completely change allegiance. According to his own testimony, Paul was faithful until his death: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: –2 Timothy 4:6-7.

God did amazing things in the New Testament. He healed the blind and raised the dead to life again. He released prisoners and struck people dead. Some may say it would be easier to have great confidence in God if we were still living in the New Testament Bible times when Jesus physically walked and talked here on this earth.

What about after the Bible?

In the early church, we again see a group of people that did not waver; they had confidence in their God, a God they could not see. Tens of thousands of God’s people stood boldly before the world and proclaimed its wickedness, and tens of thousands of God’s people were killed. The confidence of these people was never questioned. They were called fools, for believing in a “God they could not see”. They were mocked and scorned for their ‘foolishness’, they were …killed all the day long… –Psalm 44:22. People questioned their practices, they questioned their religious structure, they questioned the message they preached, they questioned many things, but they never questioned their confidence. These Christians believed in their God, of that there was no doubt.

Strangely, they were not interested in the pleasures of this life; they did not care about the things of this world, and even their very lives were a small thing to give up for their God. Families were torn apart, houses and lands were confiscated, churches were burned, but it did not faze stop them. They lived for something greater, something the heathen could not understand.

Through the time of the early church and the time of the Reformation, people were added to the Kingdom in great numbers. Yes, children did grow up and join their parents’ church, but there were also great masses of new converts from the world. How could anyone convince a worldly person to join a group that was hunted and killed—a group that suffered like the church of Jesus Christ suffered? Yes, we know that salvation is of the Lord, but it was the confidence of God’s people that caused others to wonder, that caused them to seriously consider this new religion of heretics. This was a group of people that would gladly accept the spoiling of their goods, be happy to give all they had to help others, and not resist their capture by the authorities. The true church of Jesus Christ was a group of people that always caused others to wonder, “Who are these people?” They clearly put all their faith in their God, and that was not a common occurrence. They stood up for God’s Truth no matter how hot the fire burned, no matter how miserable their lives were made. It all showed a great confidence, not in themselves, but in their God.

As we look at the church today, what do we see? Some of God’s people are taking up their crosses, and denying the world and the lust thereof, other people are not. Is the church of today still known for being confident in their God?

As professing Christians, have we lost some of this biblical confidence? Are we still out there undeniably serving the one true God? Do people look at us, and stand in awe of the confidence we are displaying in our God? Too many people of today are saying they are Christians, but they demonstrate very little confidence in God. They live quite closely to the ways of the world. Instead of enjoying persecution, they enjoy many of the same things that the world does. Each of us needs the fire of God burning deep within our hearts, a fire that cannot be quenched.

Confidence equals obedience. I have met many Christians of our day whose ancestors gave their lives for Christ, and their grandfathers bravely led the church, but there now seems to be something missing. As I interact with many God-fearing Christians, it seems that there is a prevailing struggle with confidence—a confidence in a living God who is all-powerful, all-knowing, and all-present.

In the uncertainty of our world today, we need to once more boldly proclaim the gospel message just like true believers did in times past. We need to clearly draw distinct biblical lines between right and wrong. We need to rid ourselves of all these wretched gray areas and call sin, sin. It seems that we have lost the confidence to speak out against the sin of our day. If we confidently proclaim what God has declared, there are some people who will not like us. We need brethren that are not afraid to be scoffed at and are willing to take the road less traveled.

Right before our Lord ascended on high, He gave His disciples a glorious promise, …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

Ye shall receive power! Not power from men, not power from kingdoms of this world, but real, overcoming power—power that comes only from the Holy Ghost! After we receive this power, we go forward as a new creature, confidently proclaiming the blessed Gospel of our Redeemer.

We need hearts that burn with God’s will and God’s word. We need hearts aflame!

I was eating lunch one day when a couple approached me with a serious question, “Why does the church think it has to control us?” After they explained how they think they should be able to be ‘free in Christ’, I was excited to answer their questions. However, there was another ordained brother sitting beside me. So, I decided to wait, hoping that he would engage the couple, but he said nothing. As another forty-five minutes passed, I tried to explain to the couple how they needed to deny themselves and submit to the church. And that if they laid down their lives fully, if they surrendered all, they would no longer have such a struggle with church structure.

The couple seemed encouraged and ready to give things another try. However, the minister beside me did not seem too pleased, so I asked him what he thought. He said that his father told him years ago that when he was young, he thought he had all the answers. After he got old, he realized he did not know anything, and that church issues are too complicated to solve. We need to just try to get along.

Is this the answer, to just act like we don’t know anything and hope that it all works out in the end? I do understand that we don’t have all the answers. After all, I realize that I have more questions than answers most times. However, I do know what God wants for His church! …Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

A glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish! Will we, as God’s people, once again stand for truth, deny the world, and like sheep allow ourselves to be led to the slaughter? Or have we made our lives too comfortable to deny, have we chosen the easy (broad) way and denied the straight and narrow? Have we signed a peace deal with the servants of sin? If I weep as I write, will you weep as you read?

The definition of the word confidence is a feeling or consciousness of one’s powers. Many people today have confused confidence with pride, and for good reason. Most people that are confident are confident in themselves, instead of being confident in Christ. We see this self-confidence all around us. There are life coaches and counselors all over the globe, telling people to believe in themselves, telling them to be confident in themselves. When one is confident in themselves, they often do become proud. Remember the world does not look down on pride. You can hear the world boast of its pride everywhere you look. People are proud of their children, proud of their country, proud of their favorite sports team, proud of their lawns, proud of basically everything that is good in their lives. We must remember that pride is sin and will not enter heaven. While confidence in one’s self or things is pride, confidence in God is not!

It is not a new concept to confuse confidence in God, with pride. David’s oldest brother Eliab said to him, “I know thy pride”. Was David proud? No, he simply had a great deal of confidence in his God.

Could it be that a false sense of humility has silenced the church? Could it be that this tactic of the enemy is one of Satan’s current weapons against Christians? Could it also be the reason that the Church seems to be struggling in all parts of the world? What if faithful men would once again step out in faith in their God with great confidence and by their words and actions show this sinned-stained world the straight and narrow way—into the Kingdom of God?!

We all must agree, we live in a confused world—one that is confused as to what is right and what is wrong. What if the world could look at the Church and once again find a group of people that know exactly where they are going—a church that has no doubt which way is the right way—a church that can boldly proclaim the answer to the problems of our day—a church that is nothing less than completely confident in their GOD?

Let us come before our God on bended knee, with our hearts bowed low, demonstrating genuine godly sorrow for where we have lost our way. Let us earnestly seek God’s will for ourselves, for our families, for our churches, and for our neighbors. Let us ask God to show us how we can be His examples to the world around us. The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn; To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified –Isaiah 61:1-3.

خدا کے کلام کو پڑھتے ہوئے میں نے بار بار یہ بات دیکھی ہے کہ خدا کے لوگ پُراعتماد ہوتے ہیں۔ نوح پر غور کریں۔ جب خدا نے اسے کشتی بنانے کو کہا، تو وہ ذرا بھی متذبذب نہ ہوا۔ اگلے 120 سال تک اس نے پورے اعتماد کے ساتھ یہی کام کیا۔ پھر ابراہیم کا خیال آتا ہے، جو اعتماد سے وہ سب کچھ کرنے کو تیار تھا جو خدا اس سے چاہتا، یہاں تک کہ جب خدا نے اس سے اپنے اکلوتے بیٹے کو قربان کرنے کو کہا۔ کالب اور یشوع کا ذکر کیے بغیر ہم اعتماد کی بات نہیں کر سکتے۔ اپنے تمام ساتھیوں کی شک بھری رپورٹیں سننے کے بعد، انہوں نے پورے اعتماد سے بتایا کہ کنعان کی اس نئی سرزمین کے ساتھ انہیں کیا کرنا چاہیے: …ہم فوراً جا کر اُس پر قبضہ کر لیتے ہیں، کیونکہ ہم یقینا اُس پر غالب آئیں گے –گنتی 13:30۔

ہم داؤد کو نہیں بھول سکتے، جو باہر گیا اور بڑے مخالف یعنی جالوت کو خاموش کر دیا۔ نہ ہم دانی ایل، جدعون، ایوب، حزقی ایل، یسعیاہ یا یرمیاہ کو اور ان سب کاموں کو بھول سکتے ہیں جو انہوں نے اعتماد سے کیے۔ جب ہم ان ایمان والے مردوں اور بہت سے دوسرے لوگوں کا مطالعہ کرتے ہیں، تو صاف دیکھتے ہیں کہ انہیں اپنے خدا پر بہت زیادہ اعتماد تھا!

بعض لوگ کہہ سکتے ہیں کہ اگر خدا آج بھی اسی طرح کام کرتا جیسے اُس زمانے میں کرتا تھا، تو ہمیں زیادہ اعتماد ہوتا۔ شاید اگر خدا اب بھی عہدِ عتیق کا خدا ہوتا، تو یہ آسان ہوتا۔ اگر وہ ہمیں جنگ میں لے جاتا، ہمارے دشمنوں کو تباہ کرتا، سمندروں کو چیرتا اور آسمان سے روٹی برساتا، تو ہمیں اُس پر زیادہ اعتماد ہوتا۔

اب عہدِ جدید پر غور کریں۔ یہ بالکل مختلف ہے۔ خدا کے لوگوں کو حکم دیا جاتا ہے کہ مسیح کی خاطر سب کچھ چھوڑ دیں۔ ان سے وعدہ کیا جاتا ہے کہ دنیا ان سے نفرت کرے گی۔ انہیں بتایا جاتا ہے کہ دولت مند آدمی کے لیے خدا کی بادشاہی میں داخل ہونا مشکل ہے۔ انہیں یقین دلایا جاتا ہے کہ اگر وہ دکھ اٹھائیں، غریب ہوں، بھوکے ہوں اور ماتم کریں، تو وہ مبارک ہوں گے۔

کیا لوگ اب بھی ایسے خدا پر اعتماد کر سکتے ہیں جو اپنے لوگوں سے ان حالات میں اپنی پیروی کرنے کو کہتا ہے؟ ہاں! شاگردوں نے یہ ثابت کیا۔ وہ منادی اور تعلیم دیتے پھرتے تھے۔ بار بار ان کا پیچھا کیا گیا اور انہیں مارا پیٹا گیا۔ خادم استیفنس نے اپنے ستانے والوں کے سامنے پیش کیے جانے پر بڑا اعتماد دکھایا، یہاں تک کہ جب وہ اس پر دانت پیسنے لگے اور اسے سنگسار کیا۔ استیفنس نے آخری دردناک سانس تک اعتماد دکھایا۔

رسول پولس بننے سے پہلے، ساؤل صلیب کا دشمن، گنہگاروں میں سب سے بڑا اور فریسیوں کا فریسی تھا۔ وہ ایک ممتاز آدمی تھا جس نے بہترین استادوں سے تعلیم پائی تھی۔ پھر اس کی ملاقات زندہ خدا سے ہوئی اور سب کچھ بدل گیا۔ پولس کے بپتسمہ لینے کے بعد، …وہ فوراً عبادت خانوں میں مسیح کی منادی کرنے لگا کہ وہ خدا کا بیٹا ہے –اعمال 9:20۔ اگلی آیت کہتی ہے کہ لوگ حیران ہوئے، پھر آیت 23 میں، اس کے بپتسمہ لینے کے پانچ آیات بعد، لکھا ہے کہ یہودیوں نے اُسے قتل کرنے کا مشورہ کیا۔

ایسے آدمی کو بدلنے، اسے راتوں رات مکمل طور پر وفاداری بدلنے پر آمادہ کرنے کے لیے خدا پر بہت زیادہ اعتماد درکار ہوتا ہے۔ اپنی گواہی کے مطابق، پولس اپنی موت تک وفادار رہا: کیونکہ اب میں نذر ہونے کو ہوں اور میرے کوچ کرنے کا وقت آ پہنچا ہے۔ میں نے اچھی کشتی لڑی، میں نے اپنا دورہ ختم کر لیا، میں نے ایمان کو محفوظ رکھا: –2 تیمتھیس 4:6-7۔

خدا نے عہدِ جدید میں حیرت انگیز کام کیے۔ اس نے اندھوں کو شفا دی اور مردوں کو پھر سے زندہ کیا۔ اس نے قیدیوں کو رہا کیا اور لوگوں کو موت سے مارا۔ بعض لوگ کہہ سکتے ہیں کہ اگر ہم اب بھی بائبل کے عہدِ جدید کے زمانے میں زندہ ہوتے، جب یسوع جسمانی طور پر اس زمین پر چلتے پھرتے اور باتیں کرتے تھے، تو خدا پر بہت زیادہ اعتماد کرنا آسان ہوتا۔

بائبل کے بعد کیا ہوا؟

ابتدائی کلیسیا میں ہم پھر ایسے لوگوں کے ایک گروہ کو دیکھتے ہیں جو متزلزل نہیں ہوئے؛ انہیں اپنے خدا پر اعتماد تھا، ایسے خدا پر جسے وہ دیکھ نہیں سکتے تھے۔ خدا کے دسیوں ہزار لوگوں نے دنیا کے سامنے دلیری سے کھڑے ہو کر اس کی بدکاری کا اعلان کیا، اور خدا کے دسیوں ہزار لوگ مارے گئے۔ ان لوگوں کے اعتماد پر کبھی سوال نہیں اٹھایا گیا۔ انہیں بے وقوف کہا گیا، کیونکہ وہ ایک ایسے «خدا» پر ایمان رکھتے تھے «جسے وہ دیکھ نہیں سکتے تھے»۔ ان کی «بے وقوفی» کا مذاق اڑایا گیا اور انہیں حقیر جانا گیا؛ انہیں …سارا دن قتل کیا جاتا رہا… –زبور 44:22۔ لوگوں نے ان کے طریقوں پر سوال اٹھائے، ان کے مذہبی نظام پر سوال اٹھائے، ان کے پیغام پر سوال اٹھائے اور بہت سی باتوں پر سوال کیے، مگر ان کے اعتماد پر کبھی سوال نہیں اٹھایا۔ ان مسیحیوں کے اپنے خدا پر ایمان کے بارے میں کوئی شک نہ تھا۔

عجیب بات یہ ہے کہ انہیں اس زندگی کی لذتوں میں دلچسپی نہ تھی؛ انہیں دنیا کی چیزوں کی پروا نہ تھی، اور اپنی جانیں بھی وہ اپنے خدا کے لیے قربان کرنے کو معمولی بات سمجھتے تھے۔ خاندان بکھیر دیے گئے، گھر اور زمینیں ضبط کر لی گئیں، کلیسیائیں جلا دی گئیں، مگر اس سے وہ نہ پریشان ہوئے نہ رکے۔ وہ کسی بڑی چیز کے لیے جیتے تھے، ایسی چیز جسے غیر قومیں سمجھ نہیں سکتی تھیں۔

ابتدائی کلیسیا کے دور سے لے کر اصلاحِ کلیسا کے دور تک، بڑی تعداد میں لوگ بادشاہی میں شامل ہوئے۔ ہاں، بچے بڑے ہو کر اپنے والدین کی کلیسیا میں شامل ہوتے تھے، لیکن دنیا سے نئے ایمان لانے والوں کی بھی بڑی تعداد تھی۔ کوئی دنیادار شخص ایسے گروہ میں شامل ہونے پر کیسے آمادہ ہو سکتا تھا جس کا پیچھا کیا جاتا اور جس کے لوگوں کو قتل کیا جاتا تھا—ایسے گروہ میں جو یسوع مسیح کی کلیسیا کی طرح دکھ اٹھاتا تھا؟ ہاں، ہم جانتے ہیں کہ نجات خداوند کی طرف سے ہے، لیکن خدا کے لوگوں کے اعتماد ہی نے دوسروں کو حیران کیا اور انہیں اس نئے «بدعتی» مذہب پر سنجیدگی سے غور کرنے پر آمادہ کیا۔ یہ لوگوں کا ایسا گروہ تھا جو خوشی سے اپنا مال لٹنے دیتا، دوسروں کی مدد کے لیے اپنی ساری چیزیں بخوشی دے دیتا اور حکام کے ہاتھوں گرفتاری کی مزاحمت نہ کرتا۔ یسوع مسیح کی سچی کلیسیا ایسے لوگوں کا گروہ تھی جو دوسروں کو ہمیشہ یہ سوچنے پر مجبور کرتا تھا: «یہ لوگ کون ہیں؟» انہوں نے واضح طور پر اپنا سارا ایمان اپنے خدا پر رکھا تھا، اور یہ کوئی عام بات نہ تھی۔ وہ خدا کی سچائی کے لیے کھڑے ہوئے، چاہے آگ کتنی ہی بھڑکی، چاہے ان کی زندگیاں کتنی ہی تلخ بنا دی گئیں۔ یہ سب خود ان پر نہیں بلکہ ان کے خدا پر ان کے بڑے اعتماد کا اظہار تھا۔

جب ہم آج کی کلیسیا کو دیکھتے ہیں، تو کیا دیکھتے ہیں؟ خدا کے بعض لوگ اپنی صلیبیں اٹھا رہے ہیں اور دنیا اور اس کی خواہشات کا انکار کر رہے ہیں، جبکہ دوسرے ایسا نہیں کر رہے۔ کیا آج کی کلیسیا اب بھی اپنے خدا پر اعتماد کے لیے پہچانی جاتی ہے؟

کیا اقرار کرنے والے مسیحیوں کی حیثیت سے ہم نے بائبل کے اس اعتماد میں سے کچھ کھو دیا ہے؟ کیا ہم اب بھی بلا شبہ اُس واحد سچے خدا کی خدمت کر رہے ہیں؟ کیا لوگ ہمیں دیکھ کر ہمارے خدا پر ظاہر کیے جانے والے اعتماد پر حیرت کرتے ہیں؟ آج بہت سے لوگ مسیحی ہونے کا دعویٰ کرتے ہیں، مگر خدا پر بہت کم اعتماد دکھاتے ہیں۔ ان کی زندگیاں دنیا کے طریقوں سے بہت قریب ہیں۔ ظلم و ستم میں خوش ہونے کے بجائے، وہ دنیا جیسی ہی بہت سی چیزوں سے لطف اندوز ہوتے ہیں۔ ہم میں سے ہر ایک کو اپنے دل کی گہرائیوں میں خدا کی آگ جلانے کی ضرورت ہے، ایسی آگ جسے بجھایا نہ جا سکے۔

اعتماد کا مطلب فرمانبرداری ہے۔ میں نے اپنے زمانے کے بہت سے مسیحیوں سے ملاقات کی ہے جن کے آباؤ اجداد نے مسیح کے لیے اپنی جانیں دیں، اور جن کے دادا دلیری سے کلیسیا کی رہنمائی کرتے تھے، لیکن اب جیسے کوئی چیز غائب ہے۔ خدا ترس بہت سے مسیحیوں سے بات چیت کرتے ہوئے مجھے لگتا ہے کہ اعتماد کے معاملے میں ایک مسلسل کشمکش پائی جاتی ہے—ایک زندہ خدا پر اعتماد جو قادرِ مطلق، علیمِ کل اور ہر جگہ حاضر ہے۔

آج ہماری دنیا کی بے یقینی میں، ہمیں ایک بار پھر ماضی کے سچے ایمانداروں کی طرح دلیری سے انجیل کا پیغام سنانے کی ضرورت ہے۔ ہمیں درست اور غلط کے درمیان بائبل کے واضح امتیازات قائم کرنے کی ضرورت ہے۔ ہمیں ان تمام قابلِ نفرت خاکستری گوشوں سے جان چھڑانے اور گناہ کو گناہ کہنے کی ضرورت ہے۔ ایسا لگتا ہے کہ ہم اپنے زمانے کے گناہ کے خلاف آواز اٹھانے کا اعتماد کھو چکے ہیں۔ اگر ہم اعتماد سے وہ باتیں بیان کریں جن کا خدا نے اعلان کیا ہے، تو کچھ لوگ ہم سے خوش نہیں ہوں گے۔ ہمیں ایسے بھائیوں کی ضرورت ہے جو تمسخر سے نہ ڈریں اور کم اختیار کیے جانے والے راستے پر چلنے کو تیار ہوں۔

ہمارے خداوند کے آسمان پر صعود کرنے سے عین پہلے، اس نے اپنے شاگردوں سے ایک جلالی وعدہ کیا: …جب روح القدس تم پر نازل ہوگا تو تم قوت پاؤ گے اور یروشلیم اور تمام یہودیہ اور سامریہ میں بلکہ زمین کی انتہا تک میرے گواہ ہوگے –اعمال 1:8۔

تم قوت پاؤ گے! آدمیوں سے قوت نہیں، نہ اس دنیا کی بادشاہیوں سے قوت، بلکہ حقیقی، غالب آنے والی قوت—وہ قوت جو صرف روح القدس سے آتی ہے! یہ قوت پانے کے بعد ہم ایک نئی مخلوق بن کر آگے بڑھتے ہیں اور اپنے نجات دہندہ کی مبارک انجیل کا اعتماد سے اعلان کرتے ہیں۔

ہمیں ایسے دلوں کی ضرورت ہے جو خدا کی مرضی اور خدا کے کلام سے جلتے ہوں۔ ہمیں شعلہ فشاں دلوں کی ضرورت ہے!

ایک دن میں دوپہر کا کھانا کھا رہا تھا کہ ایک جوڑا میرے پاس آیا اور ایک سنجیدہ سوال کیا: «کلیسیا کیوں سمجھتی ہے کہ اسے ہم پر قابو رکھنا چاہیے؟» جب انہوں نے وضاحت کی کہ ان کے خیال میں انہیں «مسیح میں آزاد» ہونے کا حق ہونا چاہیے، تو میں ان کے سوالوں کے جواب دینے کے لیے پُرجوش تھا۔ تاہم، میرے پہلو میں ایک اور مقرر کردہ بھائی بیٹھا تھا۔ اس لیے میں نے انتظار کرنے کا فیصلہ کیا، یہ امید کرتے ہوئے کہ وہ اس جوڑے سے بات کرے گا، مگر اس نے کچھ نہ کہا۔ مزید پینتالیس منٹ گزرنے کے بعد، میں نے اس جوڑے کو سمجھانے کی کوشش کی کہ انہیں اپنا انکار کرکے کلیسیا کے تابع ہونا چاہیے۔ اور یہ کہ اگر وہ پوری طرح اپنی زندگیاں سپرد کر دیں، اگر وہ سب کچھ چھوڑ دیں، تو انہیں کلیسیا کے نظام کے ساتھ ایسی کشمکش نہیں رہے گی۔

یہ جوڑا حوصلہ پاتا اور چیزوں کو ایک اور موقع دینے کے لیے تیار دکھائی دیا۔ تاہم، میرے پہلو میں بیٹھا خادم زیادہ خوش نہیں لگ رہا تھا، اس لیے میں نے اس سے پوچھا کہ اس کی کیا رائے ہے۔ اس نے کہا کہ اس کے والد نے اسے برسوں پہلے بتایا تھا کہ جب وہ جوان تھا تو سمجھتا تھا کہ اس کے پاس سب جواب ہیں۔ جب وہ بوڑھا ہوا تو اسے احساس ہوا کہ وہ کچھ نہیں جانتا، اور کلیسیائی مسائل حل کرنے کے لیے بہت پیچیدہ ہیں۔ ہمیں بس مل جل کر رہنے کی کوشش کرنی چاہیے۔

کیا یہی جواب ہے کہ ہم بس ایسا ظاہر کریں جیسے ہمیں کچھ معلوم نہیں اور امید رکھیں کہ آخرکار سب ٹھیک ہو جائے گا؟ میں سمجھتا ہوں کہ ہمارے پاس تمام جواب نہیں ہیں۔ آخرکار، میں جانتا ہوں کہ اکثر میرے پاس جوابوں سے زیادہ سوال ہوتے ہیں۔ تاہم، میں جانتا ہوں کہ خدا اپنی کلیسیا کے لیے کیا چاہتا ہے! …مسیح نے بھی کلیسیا سے محبت کی اور اپنے آپ کو اُس کے لیے دے دیا تاکہ کلام کے ساتھ پانی سے غسل دے کر اُس کو پاک کرے اور اُس کے لیے ایک جلالی کلیسیا بنا کر پیش کرے جس کے بدن میں داغ یا شکن یا کوئی ایسی چیز نہ ہو بلکہ پاک اور بے عیب ہو –افسیوں 5:25-27۔

ایک جلالی کلیسیا جس کے بدن میں داغ یا شکن یا کوئی ایسی چیز نہ ہو بلکہ پاک اور بے عیب ہو! کیا ہم خدا کے لوگوں کی حیثیت سے ایک بار پھر سچائی کے لیے کھڑے ہوں گے، دنیا کا انکار کریں گے اور بھیڑوں کی طرح خود کو ذبح ہونے کے لیے لے جائے جانے دیں گے؟ یا ہم نے اپنی زندگیوں کو انکار کرنے کے لیے بہت آرام دہ بنا لیا ہے، کیا ہم نے آسان (چوڑا) راستہ چن کر سیدھی اور تنگ راہ کو رد کر دیا ہے؟ کیا ہم نے گناہ کے خادموں کے ساتھ امن کا معاہدہ کر لیا ہے؟ اگر لکھتے ہوئے میری آنکھوں سے آنسو بہتے ہیں، تو کیا پڑھتے ہوئے تم بھی روؤ گے؟

Something that I have noticed repeatedly as I read God’s Word is that God’s people are confident. Consider Noah. When God told him to build an ark, there was no wavering. He spent the next 120 years confidently doing just that. Then I think of Abraham confidently doing whatever God asked of him, even when He asked him to sacrifice his only son. We cannot speak of confidence without mentioning Caleb and Joshua, who after hearing all their comrades give their doubting reports, confidently described what they should do with this new land of Canaan: …Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it –Numbers 13:30.

We cannot forget about David who went out and silenced the large naysayer—Goliath. Nor can we forget Daniel, Gideon, Job, Ezekiel, Isaiah, or Jeremiah and all that they did with confidence. As we study each of these men of faith and many others, we clearly see that they had a great amount of confidence in their God!

Some might say that if God worked the same way today as He did back then, we would be more confident. Maybe if God were still an Old Testament God, it would be easier. If He led us into battle, destroyed our enemies, parted seas, and caused bread to fall from heaven, then we would have more confidence in Him.

Now let us consider the New Testament. It is quite different. God’s people are commanded to leave everything for the sake of Christ. They are promised that the world will hate them. They are told that it is difficult for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. They are guaranteed that they will be blessed if they suffer, if they are poor, if they are hungry, and if they mourn.

Can people still have confidence in a God that asks His people to follow Him under these circumstances? Yes! The disciples proved it. They went about preaching and teaching. They were hunted and beaten repeatedly. The deacon, Stephen, showed great confidence when he was brought before his oppressors, even when they began to gnash their teeth at him, and stone him. Stephen showed confidence until he took his last agonizing breath.

Before he became the apostle Paul, Saul was an enemy of the cross, the chiefest of sinners, and a Pharisee of the Pharisees. He was a prominent man, taught by the best. Then he met the living God, and everything changed. After Paul was baptized, …straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God –Acts 9:20. The next verse says the people were amazed, then in verse 23, five verses after he was baptized, it says that the Jews took counsel to kill him.

It takes a lot of confidence in God to change a man like that, to cause him to, overnight, completely change allegiance. According to his own testimony, Paul was faithful until his death: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: –2 Timothy 4:6-7.

God did amazing things in the New Testament. He healed the blind and raised the dead to life again. He released prisoners and struck people dead. Some may say it would be easier to have great confidence in God if we were still living in the New Testament Bible times when Jesus physically walked and talked here on this earth.

What about after the Bible?

In the early church, we again see a group of people that did not waver; they had confidence in their God, a God they could not see. Tens of thousands of God’s people stood boldly before the world and proclaimed its wickedness, and tens of thousands of God’s people were killed. The confidence of these people was never questioned. They were called fools, for believing in a “God they could not see”. They were mocked and scorned for their ‘foolishness’, they were …killed all the day long… –Psalm 44:22. People questioned their practices, they questioned their religious structure, they questioned the message they preached, they questioned many things, but they never questioned their confidence. These Christians believed in their God, of that there was no doubt.

Strangely, they were not interested in the pleasures of this life; they did not care about the things of this world, and even their very lives were a small thing to give up for their God. Families were torn apart, houses and lands were confiscated, churches were burned, but it did not faze stop them. They lived for something greater, something the heathen could not understand.

Through the time of the early church and the time of the Reformation, people were added to the Kingdom in great numbers. Yes, children did grow up and join their parents’ church, but there were also great masses of new converts from the world. How could anyone convince a worldly person to join a group that was hunted and killed—a group that suffered like the church of Jesus Christ suffered? Yes, we know that salvation is of the Lord, but it was the confidence of God’s people that caused others to wonder, that caused them to seriously consider this new religion of heretics. This was a group of people that would gladly accept the spoiling of their goods, be happy to give all they had to help others, and not resist their capture by the authorities. The true church of Jesus Christ was a group of people that always caused others to wonder, “Who are these people?” They clearly put all their faith in their God, and that was not a common occurrence. They stood up for God’s Truth no matter how hot the fire burned, no matter how miserable their lives were made. It all showed a great confidence, not in themselves, but in their God.

As we look at the church today, what do we see? Some of God’s people are taking up their crosses, and denying the world and the lust thereof, other people are not. Is the church of today still known for being confident in their God?

As professing Christians, have we lost some of this biblical confidence? Are we still out there undeniably serving the one true God? Do people look at us, and stand in awe of the confidence we are displaying in our God? Too many people of today are saying they are Christians, but they demonstrate very little confidence in God. They live quite closely to the ways of the world. Instead of enjoying persecution, they enjoy many of the same things that the world does. Each of us needs the fire of God burning deep within our hearts, a fire that cannot be quenched.

Confidence equals obedience. I have met many Christians of our day whose ancestors gave their lives for Christ, and their grandfathers bravely led the church, but there now seems to be something missing. As I interact with many God-fearing Christians, it seems that there is a prevailing struggle with confidence—a confidence in a living God who is all-powerful, all-knowing, and all-present.

In the uncertainty of our world today, we need to once more boldly proclaim the gospel message just like true believers did in times past. We need to clearly draw distinct biblical lines between right and wrong. We need to rid ourselves of all these wretched gray areas and call sin, sin. It seems that we have lost the confidence to speak out against the sin of our day. If we confidently proclaim what God has declared, there are some people who will not like us. We need brethren that are not afraid to be scoffed at and are willing to take the road less traveled.

Right before our Lord ascended on high, He gave His disciples a glorious promise, …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

Ye shall receive power! Not power from men, not power from kingdoms of this world, but real, overcoming power—power that comes only from the Holy Ghost! After we receive this power, we go forward as a new creature, confidently proclaiming the blessed Gospel of our Redeemer.

We need hearts that burn with God’s will and God’s word. We need hearts aflame!

I was eating lunch one day when a couple approached me with a serious question, “Why does the church think it has to control us?” After they explained how they think they should be able to be ‘free in Christ’, I was excited to answer their questions. However, there was another ordained brother sitting beside me. So, I decided to wait, hoping that he would engage the couple, but he said nothing. As another forty-five minutes passed, I tried to explain to the couple how they needed to deny themselves and submit to the church. And that if they laid down their lives fully, if they surrendered all, they would no longer have such a struggle with church structure.

The couple seemed encouraged and ready to give things another try. However, the minister beside me did not seem too pleased, so I asked him what he thought. He said that his father told him years ago that when he was young, he thought he had all the answers. After he got old, he realized he did not know anything, and that church issues are too complicated to solve. We need to just try to get along.

Is this the answer, to just act like we don’t know anything and hope that it all works out in the end? I do understand that we don’t have all the answers. After all, I realize that I have more questions than answers most times. However, I do know what God wants for His church! …Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

A glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish! Will we, as God’s people, once again stand for truth, deny the world, and like sheep allow ourselves to be led to the slaughter? Or have we made our lives too comfortable to deny, have we chosen the easy (broad) way and denied the straight and narrow? Have we signed a peace deal with the servants of sin? If I weep as I write, will you weep as you read?

The definition of the word confidence is a feeling or consciousness of one’s powers. Many people today have confused confidence with pride, and for good reason. Most people that are confident are confident in themselves, instead of being confident in Christ. We see this self-confidence all around us. There are life coaches and counselors all over the globe, telling people to believe in themselves, telling them to be confident in themselves. When one is confident in themselves, they often do become proud. Remember the world does not look down on pride. You can hear the world boast of its pride everywhere you look. People are proud of their children, proud of their country, proud of their favorite sports team, proud of their lawns, proud of basically everything that is good in their lives. We must remember that pride is sin and will not enter heaven. While confidence in one’s self or things is pride, confidence in God is not!

It is not a new concept to confuse confidence in God, with pride. David’s oldest brother Eliab said to him, “I know thy pride”. Was David proud? No, he simply had a great deal of confidence in his God.

Could it be that a false sense of humility has silenced the church? Could it be that this tactic of the enemy is one of Satan’s current weapons against Christians? Could it also be the reason that the Church seems to be struggling in all parts of the world? What if faithful men would once again step out in faith in their God with great confidence and by their words and actions show this sinned-stained world the straight and narrow way—into the Kingdom of God?!

We all must agree, we live in a confused world—one that is confused as to what is right and what is wrong. What if the world could look at the Church and once again find a group of people that know exactly where they are going—a church that has no doubt which way is the right way—a church that can boldly proclaim the answer to the problems of our day—a church that is nothing less than completely confident in their GOD?

Let us come before our God on bended knee, with our hearts bowed low, demonstrating genuine godly sorrow for where we have lost our way. Let us earnestly seek God’s will for ourselves, for our families, for our churches, and for our neighbors. Let us ask God to show us how we can be His examples to the world around us. The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn; To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified –Isaiah 61:1-3.

Etwas, das mir beim Lesen von Gottes Wort immer wieder aufgefallen ist, ist, dass Gottes Volk zuversichtlich ist. Denken wir an Noah. Als Gott ihm sagte, er solle eine Arche bauen, zögerte er nicht. Die nächsten 120 Jahre verbrachte er zuversichtlich damit, genau das zu tun. Dann denke ich an Abraham, der zuversichtlich alles tat, was Gott von ihm verlangte, selbst als er ihn aufforderte, seinen einzigen Sohn zu opfern. Wir können nicht von Zuversicht sprechen, ohne Kaleb und Josua zu erwähnen, die, nachdem sie die zweifelnden Berichte all ihrer Gefährten gehört hatten, zuversichtlich beschrieben, was sie mit diesem neuen Land Kanaan tun sollten: …Lasst uns sofort hinaufziehen und es einnehmen; denn wir sind sehr wohl imstande, es zu überwinden – 4. Mose 13,30.

Wir dürfen David nicht vergessen, der auszog und den großen Widersacher zum Schweigen brachte – Goliat. Auch Daniel, Gideon, Hiob, Hesekiel, Jesaja oder Jeremia und alles, was sie voller Zuversicht taten, dürfen wir nicht vergessen. Wenn wir jeden dieser Glaubensmänner und viele andere betrachten, sehen wir deutlich, dass sie großes Vertrauen zu ihrem Gott hatten!

Manche mögen sagen, wenn Gott heute noch so wirken würde wie damals, wären wir zuversichtlicher. Vielleicht wäre es einfacher, wenn Gott noch ein Gott des Alten Testaments wäre. Wenn er uns in den Kampf führte, unsere Feinde vernichtete, Meere teilte und Brot vom Himmel fallen ließe, dann hätten wir mehr Vertrauen zu ihm.

Betrachten wir nun das Neue Testament. Es ist ganz anders. Gottes Volk wird geboten, um Christi willen alles zu verlassen. Ihm wird verheißen, dass die Welt es hassen wird. Ihm wird gesagt, dass es für einen Reichen schwer ist, in das Reich Gottes einzugehen. Ihm wird zugesichert, dass es gesegnet sein wird, wenn es leidet, arm ist, hungert und trauert.

Können Menschen noch Vertrauen zu einem Gott haben, der von seinem Volk verlangt, ihm unter solchen Umständen zu folgen? Ja! Die Jünger haben es bewiesen. Sie gingen umher und predigten und lehrten. Sie wurden wiederholt gejagt und geschlagen. Der Diakon Stephanus zeigte große Zuversicht, als er vor seine Unterdrücker gebracht wurde, selbst als sie anfingen, mit den Zähnen gegen ihn zu knirschen und ihn zu steinigen. Stephanus blieb zuversichtlich, bis er seinen letzten qualvollen Atemzug tat.

Bevor er zum Apostel Paulus wurde, war Saulus ein Feind des Kreuzes, der größte der Sünder und ein Pharisäer unter Pharisäern. Er war ein angesehener Mann und von den Besten unterrichtet worden. Dann begegnete er dem lebendigen Gott, und alles änderte sich. Nachdem Paulus getauft worden war, …predigte er sogleich in den Synagogen Christus, dass dieser der Sohn Gottes ist – Apostelgeschichte 9,20. Im nächsten Vers heißt es, dass die Menschen erstaunt waren; dann steht in Vers 23, fünf Verse nach seiner Taufe, dass die Juden sich berieten, ihn zu töten.

Es braucht großes Vertrauen zu Gott, um einen solchen Mann zu verändern und ihn über Nacht dazu zu bringen, seine Loyalität völlig zu wechseln. Seinem eigenen Zeugnis zufolge blieb Paulus bis zu seinem Tod treu: Denn ich werde schon als Trankopfer ausgegossen, und die Zeit meines Abscheidens ist nahe. Ich habe den guten Kampf gekämpft, ich habe den Lauf vollendet, ich habe den Glauben bewahrt – 2. Timotheus 4,6–7.

Gott tat erstaunliche Dinge im Neuen Testament. Er heilte Blinde und erweckte Tote wieder zum Leben. Er befreite Gefangene und ließ Menschen tot niederfallen. Manche mögen sagen, es wäre einfacher, großes Vertrauen zu Gott zu haben, wenn wir noch in den biblischen Zeiten des Neuen Testaments lebten, als Jesus hier auf Erden leibhaftig umherging und sprach.

Und was geschah nach der Bibel?

In der frühen Kirche sehen wir erneut eine Gruppe von Menschen, die nicht wankte; sie vertrauten auf ihren Gott, einen Gott, den sie nicht sehen konnten. Zehntausende von Gottes Volk standen mutig vor der Welt und prangerten ihre Bosheit an, und Zehntausende von Gottes Volk wurden getötet. Die Zuversicht dieser Menschen wurde nie infrage gestellt. Man nannte sie Narren, weil sie an einen „Gott, den sie nicht sehen konnten“, glaubten. Wegen ihrer „Torheit“ wurden sie verspottet und verhöhnt; sie wurden …den ganzen Tag getötet… – Psalm 44,22. Die Menschen stellten ihre Bräuche infrage, sie stellten ihre religiöse Ordnung infrage, sie stellten die Botschaft infrage, die sie verkündeten, sie stellten vieles infrage, aber niemals ihr Vertrauen. Diese Christen glaubten an ihren Gott; daran gab es keinen Zweifel.

Merkwürdigerweise waren sie nicht an den Vergnügungen dieses Lebens interessiert; die Dinge dieser Welt waren ihnen gleichgültig, und sogar ihr eigenes Leben aufzugeben, war eine Kleinigkeit, wenn es um ihren Gott ging. Familien wurden auseinandergerissen, Häuser und Ländereien beschlagnahmt, Kirchen niedergebrannt, doch das brachte sie nicht davon ab. Sie lebten für etwas Größeres, etwas, das die Heiden nicht verstehen konnten.

In der Zeit der frühen Kirche und während der Reformation wurden dem Reich in großer Zahl Menschen hinzugefügt. Ja, Kinder wuchsen auf und schlossen sich der Kirche ihrer Eltern an, aber auch große Scharen von Neubekehrten kamen aus der Welt. Wie konnte man einen weltlich gesinnten Menschen dazu bewegen, sich einer Gruppe anzuschließen, die gejagt und getötet wurde – einer Gruppe, die so litt wie die Kirche Jesu Christi? Ja, wir wissen, dass das Heil vom Herrn kommt, aber das Vertrauen von Gottes Volk brachte andere zum Staunen und dazu, diese neue Religion der Ketzer ernsthaft in Betracht zu ziehen. Das war eine Gruppe von Menschen, die gern hinnahm, dass man ihnen ihren Besitz raubte, froh war, alles zu geben, was sie hatten, um anderen zu helfen, und sich ihrer Gefangennahme durch die Obrigkeit nicht widersetzte. Die wahre Kirche Jesu Christi war eine Gruppe von Menschen, die andere stets staunen ließ: „Wer sind diese Menschen?“ Sie setzten ihr ganzes Vertrauen eindeutig auf ihren Gott, und das kam nicht oft vor. Sie traten für Gottes Wahrheit ein, ganz gleich, wie heiß das Feuer brannte und wie elend ihr Leben gemacht wurde. All das zeigte großes Vertrauen – nicht in sich selbst, sondern in ihren Gott.

Wenn wir die Kirche heute betrachten, was sehen wir? Einige von Gottes Volk nehmen ihr Kreuz auf sich und verleugnen die Welt und ihre Begierde, andere tun es nicht. Ist die Kirche von heute noch dafür bekannt, auf ihren Gott zu vertrauen?

Haben wir als bekennende Christen etwas von dieser biblischen Zuversicht verloren? Dienen wir immer noch unmissverständlich dem einen wahren Gott? Sehen die Menschen uns an und staunen über das Vertrauen, das wir unserem Gott entgegenbringen? Zu viele Menschen von heute sagen, sie seien Christen, zeigen aber nur sehr wenig Vertrauen zu Gott. Sie leben den Wegen der Welt ziemlich nahe. Statt sich über Verfolgung zu freuen, genießen sie vieles von dem, was auch die Welt genießt. Jeder von uns braucht das Feuer Gottes, das tief in unseren Herzen brennt, ein Feuer, das nicht gelöscht werden kann.

Zuversicht bedeutet Gehorsam. Ich habe viele Christen unserer Zeit kennengelernt, deren Vorfahren ihr Leben für Christus gaben und deren Großväter die Kirche mutig führten, doch nun scheint etwas zu fehlen. Wenn ich mit vielen gottesfürchtigen Christen spreche, scheint ein anhaltender Kampf mit der Zuversicht zu bestehen – dem Vertrauen auf einen lebendigen Gott, der allmächtig, allwissend und allgegenwärtig ist.

In der Unsicherheit unserer heutigen Welt müssen wir die Botschaft des Evangeliums wieder mutig verkünden, so wie es wahre Gläubige in vergangenen Zeiten taten. Wir müssen klare, eindeutige biblische Grenzen zwischen Recht und Unrecht ziehen. Wir müssen all diese elenden Grauzonen beseitigen und Sünde Sünde nennen. Es scheint, dass wir den Mut verloren haben, uns gegen die Sünde unserer Zeit auszusprechen. Wenn wir zuversichtlich verkünden, was Gott erklärt hat, wird es Menschen geben, die uns nicht mögen. Wir brauchen Brüder, die keine Angst davor haben, verspottet zu werden, und bereit sind, den weniger begangenen Weg zu gehen.

Kurz bevor unser Herr in die Höhe auffuhr, gab er seinen Jüngern eine herrliche Verheißung: …ihr werdet Kraft empfangen, wenn der Heilige Geist auf euch gekommen ist; und ihr werdet meine Zeugen sein in Jerusalem und in ganz Judäa und Samaria und bis an das Ende der Erde – Apostelgeschichte 1,8.

Ihr werdet Kraft empfangen! Nicht Kraft von Menschen, nicht Kraft von den Königreichen dieser Welt, sondern echte, überwindende Kraft – Kraft, die allein vom Heiligen Geist kommt! Nachdem wir diese Kraft empfangen haben, gehen wir als neue Kreatur voran und verkünden voller Zuversicht das gesegnete Evangelium unseres Erlösers.

Wir brauchen Herzen, die für Gottes Willen und Gottes Wort brennen. Wir brauchen Herzen in Flammen!

Eines Tages aß ich zu Mittag, als ein Paar mit einer ernsten Frage auf mich zukam: „Warum meint die Kirche, sie müsse uns kontrollieren?“ Nachdem sie erklärt hatten, warum sie glaubten, sie sollten „frei in Christus“ sein können, freute ich mich darauf, ihre Fragen zu beantworten. Doch neben mir saß ein anderer ordinierter Bruder. Deshalb beschloss ich zu warten, in der Hoffnung, dass er mit dem Paar ins Gespräch kommen würde, aber er sagte nichts. Als weitere fünfundvierzig Minuten verstrichen waren, versuchte ich dem Paar zu erklären, dass es sich selbst verleugnen und sich der Kirche unterordnen müsse. Und dass es, wenn es sein Leben ganz hingäbe, wenn es alles aufgäbe, nicht länger so mit der Kirchenordnung zu kämpfen hätte.

Das Paar schien ermutigt und bereit, es noch einmal zu versuchen. Der Geistliche neben mir schien jedoch nicht sehr erfreut zu sein, also fragte ich ihn, was er davon hielt. Er sagte, sein Vater habe ihm vor Jahren erzählt, dass er als junger Mann geglaubt habe, alle Antworten zu haben. Als er älter geworden sei, habe er erkannt, dass er nichts wisse und dass Fragen der Kirche zu kompliziert seien, um sie zu lösen. Wir müssten einfach versuchen, miteinander auszukommen.

Ist das die Antwort: einfach so zu tun, als wüssten wir nichts, und zu hoffen, dass sich am Ende alles ergibt? Ich verstehe, dass wir nicht alle Antworten haben. Schließlich weiß ich, dass ich meistens mehr Fragen als Antworten habe. Aber ich weiß, was Gott für seine Kirche will! …Christus hat auch die Kirche geliebt und sich selbst für sie hingegeben, damit er sie heilige, nachdem er sie gereinigt hat durch das Wasserbad im Wort, damit er sie sich selbst herrlich darstelle, ohne Flecken oder Runzeln oder etwas dergleichen, sondern heilig und untadelig – Epheser 5,25–27.

Eine herrliche Kirche, ohne Flecken oder Runzeln oder etwas dergleichen, sondern heilig und untadelig! Werden wir als Gottes Volk wieder für die Wahrheit eintreten, die Welt verleugnen und uns wie Schafe zur Schlachtbank führen lassen? Oder haben wir es uns zu bequem gemacht, um zu verleugnen; haben wir den leichten (breiten) Weg gewählt und den schmalen und geraden Weg abgelehnt? Haben wir einen Friedensvertrag mit den Dienern der Sünde geschlossen? Wenn ich beim Schreiben weine, werdet ihr beim Lesen weinen?

Die Definition des Wortes Zuversicht lautet: ein Gefühl oder Bewusstsein der eigenen Fähigkeiten. Viele Menschen verwechseln heute Zuversicht mit Stolz, und das aus gutem Grund. Die meisten zuversichtlichen Menschen vertrauen auf sich selbst, statt auf Christus. Diese Selbstsicherheit sehen wir überall um uns herum. Überall auf der Welt gibt es Lebensberater und Therapeuten, die den Menschen sagen, sie sollten an sich selbst glauben und auf sich selbst vertrauen. Wer auf sich selbst vertraut, wird oft stolz. Denkt daran: Die Welt verurteilt Stolz nicht. Überall, wohin man blickt, hört man, wie die Welt ihren Stolz zur Schau stellt. Menschen sind stolz auf ihre Kinder, ihr Land, ihre Lieblingssportmannschaft, ihren Rasen, ja auf so ziemlich alles Gute in ihrem Leben. Wir müssen daran denken, dass Stolz Sünde ist und nicht in den Himmel eingehen wird. Während das Vertrauen auf sich selbst oder auf Dinge Stolz ist, ist Vertrauen auf Gott kein Stolz!

Es ist keine neue Vorstellung, Vertrauen auf Gott mit Stolz zu verwechseln. Davids ältester Bruder Eliab sagte zu ihm: „Ich kenne deinen Stolz.“ War David stolz? Nein, er hatte einfach großes Vertrauen zu seinem Gott.

Könnte es sein, dass eine falsche Demut die Kirche zum Schweigen gebracht hat? Könnte diese Taktik des Feindes eine der gegenwärtigen Waffen Satans gegen Christen sein? Könnte es auch der Grund dafür sein, dass die Kirche in allen Teilen der Welt zu kämpfen scheint? Was wäre, wenn treue Männer wieder im Glauben mit großem Vertrauen auf ihren Gott vorangingen und dieser von Sünde befleckten Welt durch ihre Worte und Taten den schmalen und geraden Weg ins Reich Gottes zeigten?!

Wir müssen alle zugeben: Wir leben in einer verwirrten Welt – einer Welt, die nicht weiß, was richtig und was falsch ist. Was wäre, wenn die Welt auf die Kirche blicken und wieder eine Gruppe von Menschen finden könnte, die genau weiß, wohin sie geht – eine Kirche, die keinen Zweifel daran hat, welcher Weg der richtige ist – eine Kirche, die mutig die Antwort auf die Probleme unserer Zeit verkünden kann – eine Kirche, die uneingeschränkt ihrem GOTT vertraut?

Lasst uns mit gebeugten Knien und tief gesenktem Herzen vor unseren Gott treten und echte, gottgemäße Trauer darüber zeigen, dass wir uns verirrt haben. Lasst uns ernsthaft Gottes Willen für uns selbst, für unsere Familien, für unsere Kirchen und für unsere Nachbarn suchen. Lasst uns Gott bitten, uns zu zeigen, wie wir für die Welt um uns herum seine Vorbilder sein können. Der Geist des Herrn, des HERRN, ist auf mir, weil der HERR mich gesalbt hat, den Elenden gute Botschaft zu bringen; er hat mich gesandt, die zu verbinden, die gebrochenen Herzens sind, den Gefangenen Freiheit zu verkünden und den Gebundenen die Öffnung des Gefängnisses; auszurufen das angenehme Jahr des HERRN und den Tag der Rache unseres Gottes; alle Trauernden zu trösten; den Trauernden in Zion Kopfschmuck statt Asche zu geben, Freudenöl statt Trauer und ein Ruhmesgewand statt eines verzagten Geistes, damit sie Bäume der Gerechtigkeit genannt werden, eine Pflanzung des HERRN, zu seiner Verherrlichung – Jesaja 61,1–3.

Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalm 37:4.

Down deep within every person is a desire to be, or to do, something of value. If we, as humans, had no desire to do anything, life would be boring, and we would be nothing more than a robot. We all know that God wants more from us than to be a robot; He wants us to serve Him with our whole heart.

The meaning for the word desire is: to wish or long for; to crave; to want. Wish, want, crave, and covet all mean to have a longing for. Desire stresses the strength of feeling and often implies strong intention or aim.

Isn’t that what God wants from us—a desire with craving and intentional aim? Yes, it is, but this doesn’t happen on its own, nor does it happen automatically. Our desires are so strong that of ourselves we are no match for them; we need something outside of ourselves to be in control. According to the Bible, we must become born again. When we get born again, we become a new creature in Christ with new desires that God puts inside us. The way He does this, is by giving us a new heart.

God allows each of us to choose if we will serve Him or if we will not. He will not force us to yield ourselves to His will, nor will He force us to serve Him. But, if we are truly born again and serve the Lord joyfully and willingly, then He will give us godly desires which we will want to fulfill.

Does the Christian life become like clockwork just because we get a new heart and our desires have been turned towards serving God? I believe the answer is both yes and no. After we are walking with Christ for some time, we discover that Satan wants to change our desires in such a way that we would rather please him (Satan) instead of the Lord. Because of this, we need to be on guard. Satan wants to set spiritual snares for us. One of the ways he does this is by enticing our flesh.

There are good desires and bad desires. Some desires will bring us closer to Christ and some will draw us away. As Jesus walked on this earth, we know that His desire was to do the will of His Father. Out of His desire, He stayed focused on what He needed to do, even when His flesh was weak. There are two examples of this: one was when Jesus was tempted in the desert to make stones into bread, and the other was when He was in the garden praying right before He was crucified.

When we look at the account in the garden, we see that He did not want to take the cup that was before Him. In other words, Jesus desired to not go through the suffering, but praise God, He chose to please His Father. He laid down His flesh, obeyed the will of God, and allowed Himself to be crucified for our sins. Jesus looked at the long-term effect, and poured Himself into what He knew was right, rather than going by His own feelings. However, He did acknowledge His feelings by expressing them to God when He was praying in the garden. It is the same way with us—there are times that we need to be honest about our feelings and express them to God or to someone else. Yet we cannot walk by our feelings because we must act and do what we know is right according to the word of God.

Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23. If Solomon, the wisest man who ever lived says this, then we should take heed to it. The desires of the heart will make a difference on where we will end up in life. As we are fulfilling one of our desires by acting on it…with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength… –Mark 12:30, we actually feed that desire, causing it to develop into an even deeper longing and passion. As we then act on this stronger, passionate desire, we end up feeding that desire even more. Thus, the vicious cycle continues, repeating itself again and again.

Instead of feeding your desire, you can choose to hinder it—by acting against it. If you have a desire that is not good, and you need to change it to a godly desire, you can act against your original desire and do what is right. In so doing it will start to change your bad desire into one that is right. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also –Matthew 6:21; Luke 12:34.

And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth –Luke 12:15. Covetousness is an ungodly desire. Without bringing it into check, it will become a snare. Money is something that we all need, yet it is something that almost everyone at some point in life covets. Every day we spend much of our time working in some way to earn money.

In so doing, our heart’s desires tend to become focused on our work. Instead, we should see our job as a way of doing God’s work by being a light and encouragement to the ones around us. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him –Colossians 3:17.

Here and there we hear a lot about coveting money; however, we don’t hear much about coveting positions that are not lawful for us. It is not wrong to desire leadership in business or whatever it may be. In fact, it is a blessing for others if someone will stand up and provide leadership as a way to bless others. However, it is a wrong desire to want leadership for our own reputation, which is pride. We are all human and we are not perfect, yet we need to rise above our weaknesses and be a blessing. We all know that God gave each of us different gifts. Let’s use those gifts for the kingdom of God.

Sometimes we are trying so hard to fulfill our fleshly comforts that we lose sight of the real purpose that God has put us here. Our flesh stands in the way. It was this way with Achan. Instead of Achan putting his whole focus on the fight against the enemy, he said that, When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them… –Joshua 7:21.

I don’t know what it was like, but I picture there being loud noises and a bloody mess. If that’s the case, what was Achan thinking in the midst of a bloody battle that made him covet? The only thing I can think of, is that Achan’s number one desire was not on God’s will but was on fulfilling his own desires. It’s very sad that there were so many of God’s people killed because of Achan’s sin. If we see that we have a desire that is not godly, then let’s flee from that desire and work towards gaining a desire that is godly.

We see it is important to develop a godly desire that will encourage or lead us closer to God. The most important desire is to truly know God. That would be very close to the greatest commandment—to love the Lord thy God with all thy heart. To love the Lord thy God with all thy heart you obviously also need to have a desire to love Him. However, there are times in our life that we will need to take a specific action or purpose to love God with all our heart. There are many things that God may want us to surrender.

We all know that peer pressure influences our desires. We need brothers and sisters to walk beside us and encourage us in our relationship with Christ. Friends can draw our attention to something other than Christ. That is why we need to be careful who our close friends are. We need to seek out friends who will be upbuilding. A friend that can walk beside us and encourage us in our walk with God, is worth everything. As humans, we can’t always see everything correctly by ourselves. We need others to help us see our blind spots. A close friend who genuinely wants to help us follow God, will help us look at what is right in God’s eyes. Maybe we need to surrender our flesh and get right with God so we can develop desires that are pure and godly.

As we look at the heart’s desires, we see they have a major impact on who we are and who we will become. When our heart desires something, we pursue it with a deep longing. In fact, there are examples in the Bible where God gave people desires to serve Him. And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon –Nehemiah 2:12. Reading further… And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it –Exodus 36:2.

Remember, the word desire is a deep longing, craving, or wish. If we are wanting a walk with God that is flourishing, then we must have the desires that God has, since His desires will change our life. So they did eat, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire; They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths, The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel –Psalm 78:29-31. Even though God led the Israelites into the wilderness, gave them water and manna, and even a place to worship Him, they were still not satisfied and desired other things. The children of Israel were granted their desires, but they ended up needing to pay with their own lives.

Another good example of God giving people their own desires is found in 1 Samuel 8 when the children of Israel wanted a king over them just like all the other nations. And [they] said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the LORD. And the LORD said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them –1 Samuel 8:5-7. Oh Israel, …for he (God) gave them their own desire –Psalm 78:29.

It sounds like the Lord is saying, “Let’s let them have their own way and give them a king.” However, later in the chapter He lists all the bad things that will come with having a king. The Lord also tells Samuel who will rule over the children of Israel. After their king was anointed, they needed to serve him and could no longer serve God only. Consider why God brought them out of Egypt in the first place. Wasn’t it so they could serve the only true God?

Just like the children of Israel, we have seen God’s wonderous works. If we have been born of God’s Spirit, He led us out of our “Egypt”; He showed us the path of life; He brought us out of the miry clay; He set our feet on a solid rock. Still, we as humans tend to covet and long for something that we think is better. We ask God to give us wisdom and that He would provide for our needs, yet down deep inside we beg for God to give us our selfish desires.

We need to surrender every area of our life to God’s control. God knows what is best for us, however, if we insist, He will give us according to our selfish desires.

Remember, this earth is not our home. The end is coming, which is what God has in mind. We don’t know what is best for us, but God does. Let’s have faith and change our desires for that which God wants us to fulfill in this life. Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalms 37:4. And, Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it–Isaiah 58:14
