하나님의 말씀을 읽으면서 반복해서 깨닫게 된 한 가지는 하나님의 백성이 확신에 차 있다는 것입니다. 노아를 생각해 보십시오. 하나님께서 방주를 지으라고 말씀하셨을 때 그는 흔들리지 않았습니다. 그는 그 후 120년 동안 확신을 가지고 그 일을 했습니다. 아브라함도 하나님께서 무엇을 요구하시든 확신을 가지고 행했으며, 하나님께서 외아들을 제물로 바치라고 하셨을 때도 그러했습니다. 동료들이 모두 의심에 찬 보고를 한 뒤, 새 땅 가나안에서 무엇을 해야 하는지 확신에 차서 말한 갈렙과 여호수아를 언급하지 않고는 확신을 이야기할 수 없습니다. …우리가 곧 올라가서 그 땅을 차지하자. 우리는 능히 이길 수 있다 –민수기 13:30.

나가서 큰 반대자 골리앗을 잠잠하게 한 다윗도 잊을 수 없습니다. 다니엘, 기드온, 욥, 에스겔, 이사야, 예레미야와 그들이 확신을 가지고 행한 모든 일도 잊을 수 없습니다. 이 믿음의 사람들과 그 밖의 많은 이들을 하나하나 살펴보면, 그들이 하나님을 크게 신뢰했다는 것을 분명히 알 수 있습니다!

어떤 사람들은 하나님께서 과거와 똑같이 오늘날에도 일하신다면 우리가 더 큰 확신을 가질 것이라고 말할지 모릅니다. 하나님께서 여전히 구약의 하나님이시라면 더 쉬울지도 모릅니다. 하나님께서 우리를 전쟁터로 이끄시고, 적을 멸하시고, 바다를 가르시고, 하늘에서 빵이 떨어지게 하신다면 우리는 하나님을 더 확신할 것입니다.

이제 신약성경을 생각해 봅시다. 상황은 사뭇 다릅니다. 하나님의 백성은 그리스도를 위해 모든 것을 버리라는 명령을 받습니다. 세상이 그들을 미워할 것이라는 약속을 받습니다. 부자가 하나님의 나라에 들어가는 것이 어렵다는 말을 듣습니다. 고난을 받고, 가난하고, 굶주리고, 애통하면 복을 받을 것이라는 보장을 받습니다.

이런 상황에서도 사람들은 자기 백성에게 자신을 따르라고 요구하시는 하나님을 여전히 확신할 수 있을까요? 그렇습니다! 제자들이 그것을 증명했습니다. 그들은 두루 다니며 전파하고 가르쳤습니다. 그들은 거듭 쫓기고 매를 맞았습니다. 집사 스데반은 박해자들 앞에 끌려갔을 때 큰 확신을 보여 주었습니다. 그들이 그를 향해 이를 갈기 시작하고 돌을 던질 때에도 그랬습니다. 스데반은 마지막 고통스러운 숨을 거둘 때까지 확신을 보였습니다.

사도 바울이 되기 전 사울은 십자가의 원수였고, 죄인 중의 괴수였으며, 바리새인 중의 바리새인이었습니다. 그는 뛰어난 사람이었고 최고의 스승에게 배웠습니다. 그러다가 살아 계신 하나님을 만났고, 모든 것이 바뀌었습니다. 바울은 세례를 받은 뒤 …곧 회당에서 예수님을 전파하여 그분이 하나님의 아들이심을 증언하였다 –사도행전 9:20. 다음 절은 사람들이 놀랐다고 말합니다. 그리고 23절에는 세례를 받은 지 다섯 절 뒤에 유대인들이 그를 죽이려고 모의했다고 기록되어 있습니다.

그런 사람을 변화시키고, 하루아침에 완전히 충성을 바꾸게 하려면 하나님을 크게 신뢰해야 합니다. 바울 자신의 증언에 따르면, 그는 죽을 때까지 충성했습니다. 나는 이제 부어 드려질 준비가 되었고, 떠날 때가 이르렀다. 나는 선한 싸움을 싸우고, 나의 달려갈 길을 마치고, 믿음을 지켰다 –디모데후서 4:6-7.

하나님께서는 신약성경 시대에 놀라운 일을 행하셨습니다. 눈먼 이들을 고치시고 죽은 자들을 다시 살리셨습니다. 죄수들을 풀어 주시고 사람들을 쳐서 죽게 하셨습니다. 어떤 사람들은 예수님께서 이 땅에 육신으로 걸어 다니시고 말씀하시던 신약성경 시대에 우리가 여전히 살고 있다면 하나님을 크게 신뢰하기가 더 쉬울 것이라고 말할지도 모릅니다.

성경 이후에는 어떠했을까요?

초대 교회에서도 우리는 흔들리지 않고 보이지 않는 하나님을 신뢰한 사람들의 무리를 다시 봅니다. 수만 명의 하나님의 백성이 세상 앞에 담대히 서서 세상의 사악함을 선포했고, 수만 명의 하나님의 백성이 죽임을 당했습니다. 이들의 확신은 한 번도 의심받지 않았습니다. 그들은 “볼 수 없는 하나님”을 믿는 어리석은 자들이라고 불렸습니다. 그들의 ‘어리석음’ 때문에 조롱과 멸시를 받았고, …온종일 죽임을 당하며… –시편 44:22. 사람들은 그들의 관행을 문제 삼았고, 종교 체계를 문제 삼았으며, 그들이 전한 메시지를 문제 삼았고, 많은 것을 문제 삼았습니다. 그러나 그들의 확신만은 의심하지 않았습니다. 이 그리스도인들이 하나님을 믿었다는 사실에는 의심의 여지가 없었습니다.

이상하게도 그들은 이생의 쾌락에 관심이 없었습니다. 세상의 것들을 개의치 않았고, 하나님을 위해 자기 목숨을 내놓는 일조차 작은 일로 여겼습니다. 가족은 뿔뿔이 흩어지고, 집과 땅은 몰수되고, 교회는 불탔지만, 그들은 동요하지 않았습니다. 그들은 이교도들이 이해할 수 없는, 더 위대한 것을 위해 살았습니다.

초대 교회 시대부터 종교개혁 시대에 이르기까지, 수많은 사람이 하나님 나라에 더해졌습니다. 그렇습니다. 아이들이 자라 부모의 교회에 들어오기도 했지만, 세상에서 새로 회심한 사람들도 큰 무리를 이루었습니다. 세상에 속한 사람을 어떻게 쫓기고 죽임당하는 무리, 예수 그리스도의 교회가 겪은 것처럼 고난받는 무리에 합류하도록 설득할 수 있었을까요? 그렇습니다. 우리는 구원이 주님께 속한 것임을 압니다. 그러나 하나님의 백성이 지닌 확신은 다른 이들이 궁금해하고, 이 ‘이단자들’의 새로운 종교를 진지하게 생각해 보게 만들었습니다. 이들은 기꺼이 재산을 빼앗기고, 가진 모든 것을 기쁘게 내어 다른 사람을 돕고, 당국에 붙잡혀도 저항하지 않는 사람들이었습니다. 예수 그리스도의 참된 교회는 언제나 다른 사람들로 하여금 “이 사람들은 누구인가?” 하고 궁금해하게 하는 무리였습니다. 그들은 분명 하나님께 모든 믿음을 두었으며, 그것은 흔한 일이 아니었습니다. 불길이 아무리 뜨겁게 타오르든, 삶이 아무리 비참해지든 그들은 하나님의 진리를 위해 일어섰습니다. 이 모든 모습은 자신이 아니라 하나님을 크게 신뢰하고 있음을 보여 주었습니다.

오늘날 교회를 바라보면 무엇이 보입니까? 하나님의 백성 중에는 자기 십자가를 지고 세상과 세상의 정욕을 부인하는 이들이 있지만, 그렇지 않은 이들도 있습니다. 오늘날의 교회는 여전히 하나님을 신뢰하는 것으로 알려져 있습니까?

그리스도인이라고 고백하는 우리에게 성경적인 확신이 일부 사라진 것은 아닙니까? 우리는 여전히 참 하나님 한 분을 단호하게 섬기고 있습니까? 사람들이 우리를 보고 우리가 하나님을 얼마나 신뢰하는지 경외하며 바라봅니까? 오늘날 너무 많은 사람이 자신을 그리스도인이라고 말하지만 하나님을 거의 신뢰하지 않는 모습을 보입니다. 그들은 세상의 방식에 상당히 가까이 살아갑니다. 박해를 기뻐하기는커녕 세상 사람들이 즐기는 것과 같은 많은 것을 즐깁니다. 우리 각자의 마음 깊은 곳에서 꺼지지 않는 하나님의 불이 타올라야 합니다.

확신은 순종과 같습니다. 오늘날 그리스도를 위해 목숨을 바친 조상들과 교회를 용감하게 이끌었던 할아버지를 둔 그리스도인을 많이 만났지만, 지금은 무언가 빠져 있는 듯합니다. 하나님을 경외하는 많은 그리스도인과 교류하다 보면, 살아 계시며 전능하고 전지하시고 어디에나 계시는 하나님을 신뢰하는 확신과 관련해 널리 퍼진 갈등이 있는 듯합니다.

오늘날 세상이 불확실한 가운데, 우리는 과거의 참된 신자들처럼 복음의 메시지를 다시 담대히 선포해야 합니다. 옳고 그름 사이에 분명한 성경적 경계를 그어야 합니다. 이 비참한 회색 지대를 모두 없애고 죄를 죄라고 불러야 합니다. 오늘날의 죄에 맞서 목소리를 낼 확신을 잃은 듯합니다. 하나님께서 선언하신 것을 확신을 가지고 선포하면 우리를 좋아하지 않을 사람들도 있습니다. 조롱을 두려워하지 않고 사람들이 덜 가는 길을 기꺼이 택하는 형제들이 필요합니다.

우리 주님께서는 높은 곳으로 올라가시기 바로 전에 제자들에게 영광스러운 약속을 주셨습니다. …성령이 너희에게 임하시면 너희가 권능을 받고, 예루살렘과 온 유대와 사마리아와 땅끝까지 이르러 내 증인이 되리라 –사도행전 1:8.

너희가 권능을 받으리라! 사람에게서 오는 권능도 아니고 이 세상 왕국에서 오는 권능도 아니라, 참으로 모든 것을 이기는 권능, 오직 성령께서 주시는 권능입니다! 이 권능을 받은 뒤 우리는 새 피조물로서 나아가, 우리의 구속자께서 주신 복된 복음을 확신을 가지고 선포합니다.

하나님의 뜻과 말씀으로 불타는 마음이 필요합니다. 우리 마음이 불길처럼 타올라야 합니다!

어느 날 점심을 먹고 있는데 한 부부가 다가와 심각한 질문을 했습니다. “교회는 왜 우리를 통제해야 한다고 생각하나요?” 그들은 자신들이 ‘그리스도 안에서 자유로울’ 수 있어야 한다고 생각하는 이유를 설명했고, 저는 기쁘게 그 질문에 답하려 했습니다. 그런데 제 옆에 안수를 받은 형제가 한 명 앉아 있었습니다. 그래서 그 형제가 그 부부와 대화하기를 바라며 기다렸지만, 그는 아무 말도 하지 않았습니다. 다시 45분이 흐른 뒤, 저는 그 부부에게 자신을 부인하고 교회에 복종해야 한다고 설명하려 했습니다. 그리고 그들이 온전히 자기 삶을 내려놓고 모든 것을 내어 드린다면 교회의 질서와 관련한 갈등을 더는 겪지 않을 것이라고 말했습니다.

그 부부는 격려를 받은 듯했고 다시 한번 해 볼 마음이 있어 보였습니다. 그러나 제 옆의 목회자는 그다지 흡족해 보이지 않았습니다. 그래서 저는 그가 어떻게 생각하는지 물었습니다. 그는 오래전에 아버지가 해 준 말을 들려주었습니다. 젊었을 때는 자신이 모든 답을 안다고 생각했지만, 나이가 든 뒤에는 아무것도 모른다는 것과 교회의 문제는 해결하기에 너무 복잡하다는 사실을 깨달았다고 했습니다. 그저 서로 잘 지내려고 노력하면 된다고 했습니다.

아무것도 모르는 척하고 모든 일이 결국 잘되기를 바라는 것이 답일까요? 우리에게 모든 답이 있는 것은 아니라는 점은 저도 압니다. 사실 저는 대개 답보다 질문이 더 많다는 것을 알고 있습니다. 하지만 하나님께서 교회에 원하시는 것은 압니다! …그리스도께서도 교회를 사랑하시고 교회를 위해 자신을 내주셨으니, 이는 물로 씻고 말씀으로 깨끗하게 하여 거룩하게 하시고, 티나 주름이나 그와 같은 흠이 없는 영광스러운 교회로 자신 앞에 세우시며, 거룩하고 흠이 없게 하시려는 것입니다 –에베소서 5:25-27.

티나 주름이나 그와 같은 흠이 없는 영광스러운 교회, 곧 거룩하고 흠이 없는 교회! 하나님의 백성인 우리는 다시 진리를 위해 서고 세상을 부인하며, 양처럼 도살장으로 끌려가도록 내맡기겠습니까? 아니면 부인하기에는 삶을 너무 안락하게 만들어 버렸습니까? 쉽고 넓은 길을 택하고 좁고 협착한 길을 거부했습니까? 죄의 종들과 평화 협정을 맺었습니까? 제가 이 글을 쓰며 운다면, 여러분도 읽으며 울겠습니까?

확신이라는 말의 정의는 자신의 능력에 대한 느낌이나 자각입니다. 오늘날 많은 사람은 확신과 교만을 혼동하는데, 그럴 만한 이유가 있습니다. 확신을 가진 사람 대부분은 그리스도가 아니라 자신을 신뢰합니다. 우리는 이런 자기 확신을 사방에서 봅니다. 전 세계 곳곳에 인생 코치와 상담가들이 있고, 사람들에게 자신을 믿으라고, 자신에게 확신을 가지라고 말합니다. 자신을 신뢰하면 흔히 교만해집니다. 세상이 교만을 나쁘게 보지 않는다는 사실을 기억하십시오. 어디를 보아도 세상이 교만을 자랑하는 소리를 들을 수 있습니다. 사람들은 자녀를 자랑하고, 나라를 자랑하고, 좋아하는 스포츠 팀을 자랑하고, 잔디밭을 자랑하고, 삶에서 좋은 것은 거의 무엇이든 자랑합니다. 교만은 죄이며 천국에 들어가지 못한다는 사실을 기억해야 합니다. 자신이나 사물을 신뢰하는 것은 교만이지만, 하나님을 신뢰하는 것은 그렇지 않습니다!

하나님을 신뢰하는 것과 교만을 혼동하는 일은 새로운 일이 아닙니다. 다윗의 맏형 엘리압은 다윗에게 “네 교만을 내가 안다”고 말했습니다. 다윗은 교만했습니까? 아닙니다. 그는 그저 하나님을 크게 신뢰했을 뿐입니다.

거짓된 겸손이 교회의 입을 막았을 수 있을까요? 원수의 이런 계략이 사탄이 오늘날 그리스도인들을 대적하는 무기 가운데 하나일 수 있을까요? 교회가 세계 곳곳에서 어려움을 겪는 듯한 이유도 이것일 수 있을까요? 신실한 사람들이 다시 믿음으로 나서서 하나님을 크게 신뢰하고, 말과 행동으로 죄에 물든 세상에 하나님 나라로 들어가는 좁고 협착한 길을 보여 준다면 어떨까요?!

우리 모두 동의해야 합니다. 우리는 무엇이 옳고 무엇이 그른지 혼란스러워하는 세상에 살고 있습니다. 세상이 교회를 바라보고, 정확히 어디로 가는지 아는 사람들의 무리를 다시 발견한다면 어떨까요? 어느 길이 옳은 길인지 조금도 의심하지 않는 교회, 오늘날의 문제에 대한 답을 담대하게 선포할 수 있는 교회, 자기들의 하나님을 완전히 신뢰하는 교회라면 어떨까요?

무릎을 꿇고 마음을 낮추어 하나님 앞에 나아가, 우리가 길을 잃은 데 대해 참으로 경건한 슬픔을 드러냅시다. 우리 자신과 가족과 교회와 이웃을 향한 하나님의 뜻을 간절히 구합시다. 우리 주변 세상에 하나님의 본보기가 되려면 어떻게 해야 하는지 하나님께 보여 달라고 간구합시다. 주 여호와의 영이 내게 임하셨으니, 이는 여호와께서 내게 기름을 부으사 온유한 자에게 기쁜 소식을 전하게 하셨기 때문이다. 나를 보내사 마음이 상한 자를 싸매고 포로 된 자에게 자유를, 갇힌 자에게 놓임을 선포하게 하셨다. 여호와의 은혜의 해와 우리 하나님의 보복의 날을 선포하고, 모든 슬퍼하는 자를 위로하게 하셨다. 시온에서 슬퍼하는 자들에게 재 대신 아름다움을, 슬픔 대신 기쁨의 기름을, 무거운 마음 대신 찬양의 옷을 주어 그들이 의의 나무, 여호와께서 심으신 나무라 불리게 하시고, 여호와께서 영광을 받으시게 하려 하셨다 –이사야 61:1-3.

Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalm 37:4.

Down deep within every person is a desire to be, or to do, something of value. If we, as humans, had no desire to do anything, life would be boring, and we would be nothing more than a robot. We all know that God wants more from us than to be a robot; He wants us to serve Him with our whole heart.

The meaning for the word desire is: to wish or long for; to crave; to want. Wish, want, crave, and covet all mean to have a longing for. Desire stresses the strength of feeling and often implies strong intention or aim.

Isn’t that what God wants from us—a desire with craving and intentional aim? Yes, it is, but this doesn’t happen on its own, nor does it happen automatically. Our desires are so strong that of ourselves we are no match for them; we need something outside of ourselves to be in control. According to the Bible, we must become born again. When we get born again, we become a new creature in Christ with new desires that God puts inside us. The way He does this, is by giving us a new heart.

God allows each of us to choose if we will serve Him or if we will not. He will not force us to yield ourselves to His will, nor will He force us to serve Him. But, if we are truly born again and serve the Lord joyfully and willingly, then He will give us godly desires which we will want to fulfill.

Does the Christian life become like clockwork just because we get a new heart and our desires have been turned towards serving God? I believe the answer is both yes and no. After we are walking with Christ for some time, we discover that Satan wants to change our desires in such a way that we would rather please him (Satan) instead of the Lord. Because of this, we need to be on guard. Satan wants to set spiritual snares for us. One of the ways he does this is by enticing our flesh.

There are good desires and bad desires. Some desires will bring us closer to Christ and some will draw us away. As Jesus walked on this earth, we know that His desire was to do the will of His Father. Out of His desire, He stayed focused on what He needed to do, even when His flesh was weak. There are two examples of this: one was when Jesus was tempted in the desert to make stones into bread, and the other was when He was in the garden praying right before He was crucified.

When we look at the account in the garden, we see that He did not want to take the cup that was before Him. In other words, Jesus desired to not go through the suffering, but praise God, He chose to please His Father. He laid down His flesh, obeyed the will of God, and allowed Himself to be crucified for our sins. Jesus looked at the long-term effect, and poured Himself into what He knew was right, rather than going by His own feelings. However, He did acknowledge His feelings by expressing them to God when He was praying in the garden. It is the same way with us—there are times that we need to be honest about our feelings and express them to God or to someone else. Yet we cannot walk by our feelings because we must act and do what we know is right according to the word of God.

Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23. If Solomon, the wisest man who ever lived says this, then we should take heed to it. The desires of the heart will make a difference on where we will end up in life. As we are fulfilling one of our desires by acting on it…with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength… –Mark 12:30, we actually feed that desire, causing it to develop into an even deeper longing and passion. As we then act on this stronger, passionate desire, we end up feeding that desire even more. Thus, the vicious cycle continues, repeating itself again and again.

Instead of feeding your desire, you can choose to hinder it—by acting against it. If you have a desire that is not good, and you need to change it to a godly desire, you can act against your original desire and do what is right. In so doing it will start to change your bad desire into one that is right. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also –Matthew 6:21; Luke 12:34.

And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth –Luke 12:15. Covetousness is an ungodly desire. Without bringing it into check, it will become a snare. Money is something that we all need, yet it is something that almost everyone at some point in life covets. Every day we spend much of our time working in some way to earn money.

In so doing, our heart’s desires tend to become focused on our work. Instead, we should see our job as a way of doing God’s work by being a light and encouragement to the ones around us. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him –Colossians 3:17.

Here and there we hear a lot about coveting money; however, we don’t hear much about coveting positions that are not lawful for us. It is not wrong to desire leadership in business or whatever it may be. In fact, it is a blessing for others if someone will stand up and provide leadership as a way to bless others. However, it is a wrong desire to want leadership for our own reputation, which is pride. We are all human and we are not perfect, yet we need to rise above our weaknesses and be a blessing. We all know that God gave each of us different gifts. Let’s use those gifts for the kingdom of God.

Sometimes we are trying so hard to fulfill our fleshly comforts that we lose sight of the real purpose that God has put us here. Our flesh stands in the way. It was this way with Achan. Instead of Achan putting his whole focus on the fight against the enemy, he said that, When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them… –Joshua 7:21.

I don’t know what it was like, but I picture there being loud noises and a bloody mess. If that’s the case, what was Achan thinking in the midst of a bloody battle that made him covet? The only thing I can think of, is that Achan’s number one desire was not on God’s will but was on fulfilling his own desires. It’s very sad that there were so many of God’s people killed because of Achan’s sin. If we see that we have a desire that is not godly, then let’s flee from that desire and work towards gaining a desire that is godly.

We see it is important to develop a godly desire that will encourage or lead us closer to God. The most important desire is to truly know God. That would be very close to the greatest commandment—to love the Lord thy God with all thy heart. To love the Lord thy God with all thy heart you obviously also need to have a desire to love Him. However, there are times in our life that we will need to take a specific action or purpose to love God with all our heart. There are many things that God may want us to surrender.

We all know that peer pressure influences our desires. We need brothers and sisters to walk beside us and encourage us in our relationship with Christ. Friends can draw our attention to something other than Christ. That is why we need to be careful who our close friends are. We need to seek out friends who will be upbuilding. A friend that can walk beside us and encourage us in our walk with God, is worth everything. As humans, we can’t always see everything correctly by ourselves. We need others to help us see our blind spots. A close friend who genuinely wants to help us follow God, will help us look at what is right in God’s eyes. Maybe we need to surrender our flesh and get right with God so we can develop desires that are pure and godly.

As we look at the heart’s desires, we see they have a major impact on who we are and who we will become. When our heart desires something, we pursue it with a deep longing. In fact, there are examples in the Bible where God gave people desires to serve Him. And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon –Nehemiah 2:12. Reading further… And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it –Exodus 36:2.

Remember, the word desire is a deep longing, craving, or wish. If we are wanting a walk with God that is flourishing, then we must have the desires that God has, since His desires will change our life. So they did eat, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire; They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths, The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel –Psalm 78:29-31. Even though God led the Israelites into the wilderness, gave them water and manna, and even a place to worship Him, they were still not satisfied and desired other things. The children of Israel were granted their desires, but they ended up needing to pay with their own lives.

Another good example of God giving people their own desires is found in 1 Samuel 8 when the children of Israel wanted a king over them just like all the other nations. And [they] said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the LORD. And the LORD said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them –1 Samuel 8:5-7. Oh Israel, …for he (God) gave them their own desire –Psalm 78:29.

It sounds like the Lord is saying, “Let’s let them have their own way and give them a king.” However, later in the chapter He lists all the bad things that will come with having a king. The Lord also tells Samuel who will rule over the children of Israel. After their king was anointed, they needed to serve him and could no longer serve God only. Consider why God brought them out of Egypt in the first place. Wasn’t it so they could serve the only true God?

Just like the children of Israel, we have seen God’s wonderous works. If we have been born of God’s Spirit, He led us out of our “Egypt”; He showed us the path of life; He brought us out of the miry clay; He set our feet on a solid rock. Still, we as humans tend to covet and long for something that we think is better. We ask God to give us wisdom and that He would provide for our needs, yet down deep inside we beg for God to give us our selfish desires.

We need to surrender every area of our life to God’s control. God knows what is best for us, however, if we insist, He will give us according to our selfish desires.

Remember, this earth is not our home. The end is coming, which is what God has in mind. We don’t know what is best for us, but God does. Let’s have faith and change our desires for that which God wants us to fulfill in this life. Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalms 37:4. And, Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it–Isaiah 58:14

Fais aussi de l’Éternel tes délices, et il te donnera ce que ton cœur désire –Psaume 37:4.

Au plus profond de chaque personne se trouve le désir d’être ou de faire quelque chose qui ait de la valeur. Si, en tant qu’êtres humains, nous n’avions aucun désir de faire quoi que ce soit, la vie serait ennuyeuse et nous ne serions rien de plus que des robots. Nous savons tous que Dieu attend de nous davantage que d’être des robots ; il veut que nous le servions de tout notre cœur.

Le mot « désir » signifie : souhaiter ou aspirer à ; convoiter ; vouloir. Souhaiter, vouloir, convoiter et désirer signifient tous éprouver une aspiration. Le mot « désir » souligne l’intensité du sentiment et implique souvent une intention ou un objectif ferme.

N’est-ce pas ce que Dieu veut de nous : un désir ardent, assorti d’une intention déterminée ? Oui, mais cela ne se produit pas de soi-même, ni automatiquement. Nos désirs sont si puissants que nous ne pouvons pas leur résister par nous-mêmes ; nous avons besoin de quelque chose d’extérieur à nous pour les maîtriser. Selon la Bible, nous devons naître de nouveau. Lorsque nous naissons de nouveau, nous devenons une nouvelle créature en Christ, avec de nouveaux désirs que Dieu met en nous. Il fait cela en nous donnant un cœur nouveau.

Dieu permet à chacun de choisir de le servir ou non. Il ne nous forcera pas à nous soumettre à sa volonté, pas plus qu’il ne nous forcera à le servir. Mais si nous sommes véritablement nés de nouveau et servons le Seigneur avec joie et de bon gré, alors il nous donnera des désirs conformes à sa volonté, que nous voudrons réaliser.

La vie chrétienne devient-elle réglée comme une horloge simplement parce que nous recevons un cœur nouveau et que nos désirs se tournent vers le service de Dieu ? Je crois que la réponse est à la fois oui et non. Après avoir marché quelque temps avec Christ, nous découvrons que Satan veut changer nos désirs de telle sorte que nous préférerions lui plaire, à lui, plutôt qu’au Seigneur. C’est pourquoi nous devons rester sur nos gardes. Satan veut nous tendre des pièges spirituels. L’un des moyens qu’il emploie consiste à séduire notre chair.

Il y a de bons désirs et de mauvais désirs. Certains désirs nous rapprochent du Christ et d’autres nous en éloignent. Lorsque Jésus a marché sur cette terre, nous savons qu’il désirait faire la volonté de son Père. Ce désir l’a aidé à rester concentré sur ce qu’il devait faire, même lorsque sa chair était faible. Nous en avons deux exemples : d’abord, lorsque Jésus fut tenté dans le désert de changer des pierres en pain ; puis, lorsqu’il priait dans le jardin, juste avant sa crucifixion.

En examinant le récit dans le jardin, nous voyons qu’il ne voulait pas prendre la coupe qui se présentait à lui. Autrement dit, Jésus désirait ne pas subir la souffrance, mais, loué soit Dieu, il a choisi de plaire à son Père. Il a renoncé aux désirs de sa chair, obéi à la volonté de Dieu et s’est laissé crucifier pour nos péchés. Jésus a considéré les conséquences à long terme et s’est consacré à ce qu’il savait être juste, plutôt que de se laisser guider par ses propres sentiments. Cependant, il a reconnu ses sentiments en les exprimant à Dieu lorsqu’il priait dans le jardin. Il en va de même pour nous : il nous faut parfois être honnêtes au sujet de nos sentiments et les exprimer à Dieu ou à quelqu’un d’autre. Pourtant, nous ne pouvons pas nous laisser guider par nos sentiments, car nous devons agir et faire ce que nous savons être juste selon la parole de Dieu.

Garde ton cœur plus que toute autre chose, car de lui viennent les sources de la vie –Proverbes 4:23. Si Salomon, l’homme le plus sage qui ait jamais vécu, dit cela, nous devons en tenir compte. Les désirs de notre cœur déterminent où nous finirons dans la vie. Lorsque nous réalisons l’un de nos désirs en agissant pour le satisfaire…de toute ton âme, de toute ta pensée et de toute ta force… –Marc 12:30, nous nourrissons en fait ce désir, et le faisons grandir jusqu’à devenir une aspiration et une passion encore plus profondes. Puis, lorsque nous agissons selon ce désir plus fort et passionné, nous le nourrissons davantage. Ainsi, le cercle vicieux continue de se répéter encore et encore.

Au lieu de nourrir votre désir, vous pouvez choisir de le freiner en agissant à son encontre. Si vous avez un désir qui n’est pas bon et que vous devez le changer pour qu’il devienne un désir conforme à la volonté de Dieu, vous pouvez agir contre votre désir initial et faire ce qui est juste. Ce faisant, vous commencerez à transformer ce mauvais désir en un désir juste. Car là où est ton trésor, là aussi sera ton cœur –Matthieu 6:21 ; Luc 12:34.

Il leur dit encore : Gardez-vous avec soin de toute avarice ; car la vie d’un homme ne dépend pas de ses biens, même s’il est dans l’abondance –Luc 12:15. L’avarice est un désir impie. Si on ne la maîtrise pas, elle devient un piège. Nous avons tous besoin d’argent, et pourtant presque tout le monde en convoite à un moment ou à un autre de sa vie. Chaque jour, nous consacrons beaucoup de temps à travailler d’une manière ou d’une autre pour gagner de l’argent.

Ce faisant, les désirs de notre cœur ont tendance à se concentrer sur notre travail. Nous devrions plutôt considérer notre emploi comme un moyen d’accomplir l’œuvre de Dieu, en étant une lumière et un encouragement pour ceux qui nous entourent. Et quoi que vous fassiez, en parole ou en œuvre, faites tout au nom du Seigneur Jésus, en rendant par lui des actions de grâces à Dieu le Père –Colossiens 3:17.

De temps à autre, nous entendons beaucoup parler de la convoitise de l’argent ; cependant, nous entendons peu parler de la convoitise de positions qui ne nous sont pas légitimement accessibles. Désirer exercer un rôle de direction dans les affaires ou dans tout autre domaine n’est pas mauvais. En fait, c’est une bénédiction pour les autres lorsqu’une personne se lève et assume un rôle de direction afin de les bénir. En revanche, désirer diriger pour notre propre réputation est un mauvais désir, car c’est de l’orgueil. Nous sommes tous humains et imparfaits, mais nous devons dépasser nos faiblesses et être une bénédiction. Nous savons tous que Dieu a donné à chacun de nous des dons différents. Utilisons ces dons pour le royaume de Dieu.

Parfois, nous nous efforçons tant de satisfaire les désirs de confort de notre chair que nous perdons de vue le véritable but pour lequel Dieu nous a placés ici. Notre chair fait obstacle. Il en fut ainsi pour Acan. Au lieu de concentrer toute son attention sur le combat contre l’ennemi, Acan a dit : Quand je vis parmi les dépouilles un beau manteau de Schinear, deux cents sicles d’argent et un lingot d’or du poids de cinquante sicles, je les convoitai et je les pris… –Josué 7:21.

Je ne sais pas à quoi cela ressemblait, mais j’imagine des bruits assourdissants et un carnage sanglant. Si c’était le cas, à quoi pensait Acan, au milieu d’une bataille sanglante, qui l’a poussé à convoiter ? La seule explication que je trouve, c’est que le désir premier d’Acan n’était pas d’accomplir la volonté de Dieu, mais de satisfaire ses propres désirs. Il est très triste que tant de membres du peuple de Dieu aient été tués à cause du péché d’Acan. Si nous constatons que nous avons un désir qui n’est pas conforme à la volonté de Dieu, fuyons ce désir et efforçons-nous d’acquérir un désir qui le soit.

Nous voyons qu’il est important de développer un désir conforme à la volonté de Dieu, qui nous encourage ou nous rapproche de lui. Le désir le plus important est de connaître véritablement Dieu. Cela se rapproche beaucoup du plus grand commandement : aimer le Seigneur, ton Dieu, de tout ton cœur. Pour aimer le Seigneur, ton Dieu, de tout ton cœur, tu dois évidemment aussi avoir le désir de l’aimer. Cependant, il arrive dans notre vie que nous devions poser un acte précis ou nous fixer un objectif afin d’aimer Dieu de tout notre cœur. Il y a bien des choses auxquelles Dieu peut vouloir que nous renoncions.

Nous savons tous que la pression des pairs influence nos désirs. Nous avons besoin de frères et de sœurs qui marchent à nos côtés et nous encouragent dans notre relation avec Christ. Nos amis peuvent attirer notre attention vers autre chose que Christ. C’est pourquoi nous devons choisir avec soin nos amis proches. Cherchons des amis qui nous édifient. Un ami qui peut marcher à nos côtés et nous encourager dans notre marche avec Dieu vaut tout l’or du monde. En tant qu’êtres humains, nous ne pouvons pas toujours voir toutes choses correctement par nous-mêmes. Nous avons besoin des autres pour nous aider à repérer nos angles morts. Un ami proche qui veut sincèrement nous aider à suivre Dieu nous aidera à examiner ce qui est juste aux yeux de Dieu. Peut-être devons-nous renoncer aux désirs de notre chair et nous remettre en règle avec Dieu afin de développer des désirs purs et conformes à sa volonté.

Lorsque nous examinons les désirs du cœur, nous voyons qu’ils ont une grande influence sur qui nous sommes et sur ce que nous deviendrons. Quand notre cœur désire quelque chose, nous la poursuivons avec une profonde aspiration. En fait, la Bible donne des exemples de personnes auxquelles Dieu a donné le désir de le servir. Je me levai de nuit, moi et quelques hommes avec moi, sans avoir dit à personne ce que mon Dieu m’avait mis au cœur de faire à Jérusalem ; je n’avais avec moi aucune autre bête que celle que je montais –Néhémie 2:12. Plus loin, nous lisons : Moïse appela Betsaleel et Oholiab, et tous les hommes habiles dans l’art, dans le cœur desquels l’Éternel avait mis de la sagesse, tous ceux dont le cœur était disposé à entreprendre cette œuvre et à l’exécuter –Exode 36:2.

Souvenez-vous que le mot désir désigne une aspiration profonde, une envie ardente ou un souhait. Si nous voulons que notre marche avec Dieu s’épanouisse, nous devons avoir les désirs que Dieu veut pour nous, car ses désirs transformeront notre vie. Ils mangèrent et furent rassasiés ; Dieu leur donna ce qu’ils désiraient. Ils ne furent pas privés de ce qu’ils convoitaient. Mais tandis que la viande était encore dans leur bouche, la colère de Dieu s’éleva contre eux ; il frappa les plus vigoureux et abattit les jeunes hommes d’Israël –Psaume 78:29-31. Bien que Dieu ait conduit les Israélites dans le désert, leur ait donné de l’eau et de la manne, et même un lieu où l’adorer, ils n’étaient toujours pas satisfaits et désiraient d’autres choses. Les enfants d’Israël ont obtenu ce qu’ils désiraient, mais ils ont fini par le payer de leur vie.

On trouve un autre bon exemple de Dieu accordant aux gens ce qu’ils désirent dans 1 Samuel 8, lorsque les enfants d’Israël ont voulu avoir un roi, comme toutes les autres nations. Ils lui dirent : Voici, tu es vieux, et tes fils ne marchent pas sur tes traces ; établis maintenant sur nous un roi pour nous juger, comme il y en a chez toutes les nations. Samuel vit avec déplaisir qu’ils disaient : Donne-nous un roi pour nous juger. Et Samuel pria l’Éternel. L’Éternel dit à Samuel : Écoute la voix du peuple dans tout ce qu’il te dira ; car ce n’est pas toi qu’ils rejettent, c’est moi, afin que je ne règne plus sur eux –1 Samuel 8:5-7. Ô Israël, …il leur donna ce qu’ils désiraient –Psaume 78:29.

On dirait que le Seigneur dit : « Laissons-les agir à leur guise et donnons-leur un roi. » Pourtant, plus loin dans le chapitre, il énumère toutes les mauvaises conséquences qu’entraînera la présence d’un roi. Le Seigneur dit aussi à Samuel qui régnera sur les enfants d’Israël. Après que leur roi eut été oint, ils durent le servir et ne purent plus servir Dieu seul. Rappelons-nous pourquoi Dieu les avait fait sortir d’Égypte au départ. N’était-ce pas pour qu’ils puissent servir le seul vrai Dieu ?

Comme les enfants d’Israël, nous avons vu les œuvres merveilleuses de Dieu. Si nous sommes nés de l’Esprit de Dieu, il nous a fait sortir de notre « Égypte » ; il nous a montré le chemin de la vie ; il nous a tirés du bourbier ; il a affermi nos pieds sur le roc. Pourtant, nous, les êtres humains, avons tendance à convoiter et à désirer ardemment quelque chose que nous croyons meilleur. Nous demandons à Dieu de nous accorder la sagesse et de pourvoir à nos besoins, mais, au plus profond de nous, nous le supplions de nous accorder les désirs égoïstes de notre cœur.

Nous devons soumettre chaque aspect de notre vie à Dieu. Dieu sait ce qui est le mieux pour nous ; cependant, si nous insistons, il nous accordera ce que nous désirons égoïstement.

Souvenez-vous que cette terre n’est pas notre demeure. La fin approche, et c’est ce que Dieu a à l’esprit. Nous ne savons pas ce qui est le mieux pour nous, mais Dieu le sait. Ayons la foi et réorientons nos désirs vers ce que Dieu veut que nous accomplissions dans cette vie. Fais aussi de l’Éternel tes délices, et il te donnera ce que ton cœur désire –Psaumes 37:4. Et, Alors tu feras de l’Éternel tes délices, et je te ferai passer sur les hauteurs du pays, je te nourrirai de l’héritage de Jacob, ton père ; car la bouche de l’Éternel a parlé–Ésaïe 58:14

Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalm 37:4.

Down deep within every person is a desire to be, or to do, something of value. If we, as humans, had no desire to do anything, life would be boring, and we would be nothing more than a robot. We all know that God wants more from us than to be a robot; He wants us to serve Him with our whole heart.

The meaning for the word desire is: to wish or long for; to crave; to want. Wish, want, crave, and covet all mean to have a longing for. Desire stresses the strength of feeling and often implies strong intention or aim.

Isn’t that what God wants from us—a desire with craving and intentional aim? Yes, it is, but this doesn’t happen on its own, nor does it happen automatically. Our desires are so strong that of ourselves we are no match for them; we need something outside of ourselves to be in control. According to the Bible, we must become born again. When we get born again, we become a new creature in Christ with new desires that God puts inside us. The way He does this, is by giving us a new heart.

God allows each of us to choose if we will serve Him or if we will not. He will not force us to yield ourselves to His will, nor will He force us to serve Him. But, if we are truly born again and serve the Lord joyfully and willingly, then He will give us godly desires which we will want to fulfill.

Does the Christian life become like clockwork just because we get a new heart and our desires have been turned towards serving God? I believe the answer is both yes and no. After we are walking with Christ for some time, we discover that Satan wants to change our desires in such a way that we would rather please him (Satan) instead of the Lord. Because of this, we need to be on guard. Satan wants to set spiritual snares for us. One of the ways he does this is by enticing our flesh.

There are good desires and bad desires. Some desires will bring us closer to Christ and some will draw us away. As Jesus walked on this earth, we know that His desire was to do the will of His Father. Out of His desire, He stayed focused on what He needed to do, even when His flesh was weak. There are two examples of this: one was when Jesus was tempted in the desert to make stones into bread, and the other was when He was in the garden praying right before He was crucified.

When we look at the account in the garden, we see that He did not want to take the cup that was before Him. In other words, Jesus desired to not go through the suffering, but praise God, He chose to please His Father. He laid down His flesh, obeyed the will of God, and allowed Himself to be crucified for our sins. Jesus looked at the long-term effect, and poured Himself into what He knew was right, rather than going by His own feelings. However, He did acknowledge His feelings by expressing them to God when He was praying in the garden. It is the same way with us—there are times that we need to be honest about our feelings and express them to God or to someone else. Yet we cannot walk by our feelings because we must act and do what we know is right according to the word of God.

Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23. If Solomon, the wisest man who ever lived says this, then we should take heed to it. The desires of the heart will make a difference on where we will end up in life. As we are fulfilling one of our desires by acting on it…with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength… –Mark 12:30, we actually feed that desire, causing it to develop into an even deeper longing and passion. As we then act on this stronger, passionate desire, we end up feeding that desire even more. Thus, the vicious cycle continues, repeating itself again and again.

Instead of feeding your desire, you can choose to hinder it—by acting against it. If you have a desire that is not good, and you need to change it to a godly desire, you can act against your original desire and do what is right. In so doing it will start to change your bad desire into one that is right. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also –Matthew 6:21; Luke 12:34.

And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth –Luke 12:15. Covetousness is an ungodly desire. Without bringing it into check, it will become a snare. Money is something that we all need, yet it is something that almost everyone at some point in life covets. Every day we spend much of our time working in some way to earn money.

In so doing, our heart’s desires tend to become focused on our work. Instead, we should see our job as a way of doing God’s work by being a light and encouragement to the ones around us. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him –Colossians 3:17.

Here and there we hear a lot about coveting money; however, we don’t hear much about coveting positions that are not lawful for us. It is not wrong to desire leadership in business or whatever it may be. In fact, it is a blessing for others if someone will stand up and provide leadership as a way to bless others. However, it is a wrong desire to want leadership for our own reputation, which is pride. We are all human and we are not perfect, yet we need to rise above our weaknesses and be a blessing. We all know that God gave each of us different gifts. Let’s use those gifts for the kingdom of God.

Sometimes we are trying so hard to fulfill our fleshly comforts that we lose sight of the real purpose that God has put us here. Our flesh stands in the way. It was this way with Achan. Instead of Achan putting his whole focus on the fight against the enemy, he said that, When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them… –Joshua 7:21.

I don’t know what it was like, but I picture there being loud noises and a bloody mess. If that’s the case, what was Achan thinking in the midst of a bloody battle that made him covet? The only thing I can think of, is that Achan’s number one desire was not on God’s will but was on fulfilling his own desires. It’s very sad that there were so many of God’s people killed because of Achan’s sin. If we see that we have a desire that is not godly, then let’s flee from that desire and work towards gaining a desire that is godly.

We see it is important to develop a godly desire that will encourage or lead us closer to God. The most important desire is to truly know God. That would be very close to the greatest commandment—to love the Lord thy God with all thy heart. To love the Lord thy God with all thy heart you obviously also need to have a desire to love Him. However, there are times in our life that we will need to take a specific action or purpose to love God with all our heart. There are many things that God may want us to surrender.

We all know that peer pressure influences our desires. We need brothers and sisters to walk beside us and encourage us in our relationship with Christ. Friends can draw our attention to something other than Christ. That is why we need to be careful who our close friends are. We need to seek out friends who will be upbuilding. A friend that can walk beside us and encourage us in our walk with God, is worth everything. As humans, we can’t always see everything correctly by ourselves. We need others to help us see our blind spots. A close friend who genuinely wants to help us follow God, will help us look at what is right in God’s eyes. Maybe we need to surrender our flesh and get right with God so we can develop desires that are pure and godly.

As we look at the heart’s desires, we see they have a major impact on who we are and who we will become. When our heart desires something, we pursue it with a deep longing. In fact, there are examples in the Bible where God gave people desires to serve Him. And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon –Nehemiah 2:12. Reading further… And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it –Exodus 36:2.

Remember, the word desire is a deep longing, craving, or wish. If we are wanting a walk with God that is flourishing, then we must have the desires that God has, since His desires will change our life. So they did eat, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire; They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths, The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel –Psalm 78:29-31. Even though God led the Israelites into the wilderness, gave them water and manna, and even a place to worship Him, they were still not satisfied and desired other things. The children of Israel were granted their desires, but they ended up needing to pay with their own lives.

Another good example of God giving people their own desires is found in 1 Samuel 8 when the children of Israel wanted a king over them just like all the other nations. And [they] said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the LORD. And the LORD said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them –1 Samuel 8:5-7. Oh Israel, …for he (God) gave them their own desire –Psalm 78:29.

It sounds like the Lord is saying, “Let’s let them have their own way and give them a king.” However, later in the chapter He lists all the bad things that will come with having a king. The Lord also tells Samuel who will rule over the children of Israel. After their king was anointed, they needed to serve him and could no longer serve God only. Consider why God brought them out of Egypt in the first place. Wasn’t it so they could serve the only true God?

Just like the children of Israel, we have seen God’s wonderous works. If we have been born of God’s Spirit, He led us out of our “Egypt”; He showed us the path of life; He brought us out of the miry clay; He set our feet on a solid rock. Still, we as humans tend to covet and long for something that we think is better. We ask God to give us wisdom and that He would provide for our needs, yet down deep inside we beg for God to give us our selfish desires.

We need to surrender every area of our life to God’s control. God knows what is best for us, however, if we insist, He will give us according to our selfish desires.

Remember, this earth is not our home. The end is coming, which is what God has in mind. We don’t know what is best for us, but God does. Let’s have faith and change our desires for that which God wants us to fulfill in this life. Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalms 37:4. And, Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it–Isaiah 58:14

«تلذّذ بالرب أيضًا، فيعطيك سؤل قلبك» –مزمور 37:4.

في أعماق كل إنسان رغبة في أن يكون أو يفعل شيئًا ذا قيمة. ولو لم تكن لدينا نحن البشر رغبة في فعل أي شيء، لكانت الحياة مملّة، ولما كنا أكثر من روبوت. ونحن جميعًا نعلم أن الله يريد منا أكثر من أن نكون روبوتًا؛ فهو يريدنا أن نخدمه بكل قلوبنا.

معنى كلمة «رغبة» هو: أن تتمنى أو تتوق إلى شيء؛ أن تشتهيه؛ أن تريده. فالتمني والإرادة والاشتهاء والطمع كلها تعني التوق إلى شيء. وتؤكد الرغبة قوة الشعور، وغالبًا ما تنطوي على نية أو هدف قوي.

أليس هذا ما يريده الله منا—رغبة تنطوي على الشوق والهدف المقصود؟ بلى، لكنه لا يحدث من تلقاء نفسه ولا يحدث تلقائيًا. رغباتنا قوية جدًا، حتى إننا لا نستطيع بمفردنا مجابهتها؛ فنحن بحاجة إلى شيء خارج ذواتنا يسيطر عليها. ووفقًا للكتاب المقدس، يجب أن نولد من جديد. وعندما نولد من جديد، نصير خليقة جديدة في المسيح، لنا رغبات جديدة يضعها الله في داخلنا. وهو يفعل ذلك بأن يمنحنا قلبًا جديدًا.

يتيح الله لكل واحد منا أن يختار ما إذا كان سيخدمه أم لا. فهو لن يجبرنا على إخضاع أنفسنا لمشيئته، ولن يجبرنا على خدمته. لكن إن كنا مولودين حقًا من جديد ونخدم الرب بفرح وطواعية، فإنه يمنحنا رغبات صالحة ترضي الله، نرغب في تحقيقها.

هل تصبح الحياة المسيحية تسير بانتظام آلي لمجرد أننا نلنا قلبًا جديدًا وتحوّلت رغباتنا نحو خدمة الله؟ أعتقد أن الجواب نعم ولا في آن واحد. فبعد أن نسير مع المسيح بعض الوقت، نكتشف أن الشيطان يريد تغيير رغباتنا بحيث نفضّل إرضاءه (الشيطان) على إرضاء الرب. لذلك علينا أن نكون يقظين. فالشيطان يريد أن ينصب لنا فخاخًا روحية، وإحدى الطرق التي يفعل بها ذلك هي إغواء جسدنا.

هناك رغبات صالحة وأخرى شريرة. بعض الرغبات تقرّبنا من المسيح، وبعضها يبعدنا عنه. ونحن نعلم أن رغبة يسوع، حين سار على الأرض، كانت أن يفعل مشيئة أبيه. وبفضل هذه الرغبة، ظل مركزًا على ما ينبغي له فعله، حتى عندما كان جسده ضعيفًا. وهناك مثالان على ذلك: الأول حين جُرّب يسوع في البرية ليحوّل الحجارة إلى خبز، والثاني حين كان يصلي في البستان قبيل صلبه.

عندما نتأمل ما جرى في البستان، نرى أنه لم يكن يريد أن يأخذ الكأس التي أمامه. بعبارة أخرى، رغب يسوع في ألا يمرّ بالعذاب، لكن الحمد لله، اختار أن يرضي أباه. أخضع جسده، وأطاع مشيئة الله، وسمح بأن يُصلب من أجل خطايانا. نظر يسوع إلى العاقبة البعيدة، وبذل نفسه فيما عرف أنه صواب، بدلًا من أن يتبع مشاعره الخاصة. ومع ذلك، أقرّ بمشاعره إذ عبّر عنها لله وهو يصلي في البستان. وينطبق الأمر نفسه علينا—فثمة أوقات ينبغي لنا فيها أن نكون صريحين بشأن مشاعرنا وأن نعبّر عنها لله أو لشخص آخر. لكن لا يمكننا أن نسلك بحسب مشاعرنا، إذ علينا أن نعمل ونفعل ما نعرف أنه صواب وفقًا لكلمة الله.

«فوق كل تحفظ احفظ قلبك، لأن منه مخارج الحياة» –أمثال 4:23. إذا كان سليمان، أحكم من عاش قط، يقول هذا، فعلينا أن نأخذه على محمل الجد. فرغبات القلب تؤثر في المكان الذي سننتهي إليه في الحياة. وعندما نحقق إحدى رغباتنا بالعمل بمقتضاها «…بكل نفسك، وبكل فكرك، وبكل قوتك…» –مرقس 12:30، فإننا نغذّي تلك الرغبة بالفعل، ونجعلها تتحول إلى توق وشغف أعمق. ثم، عندما نعمل بمقتضى هذه الرغبة الأقوى والأشد شغفًا، نواصل تغذيتها أكثر. وهكذا تستمر الحلقة المفرغة، وتتكرر مرة بعد مرة.

بدلًا من تغذية رغبتك، يمكنك أن تختار كبحها بالعمل ضدها. فإذا كانت لديك رغبة غير صالحة، وكان عليك تغييرها إلى رغبة صالحة ترضي الله، يمكنك أن تعمل ضد رغبتك الأصلية وتفعل ما هو صواب. وبذلك تبدأ في تغيير رغبتك السيئة إلى رغبة صالحة. «لأنه حيث يكون كنزك هناك يكون قلبك أيضًا» –متى 6:21؛ لوقا 12:34.

«وقال لهم: انظروا وتحفّظوا من الطمع، فإنه متى كان لأحد كثير فليست حياته من أمواله» –لوقا 12:15. الطمع رغبة لا ترضي الله. وإن لم نكبحه، فسيصبح فخًا. المال شيء نحتاج إليه جميعًا، ومع ذلك فهو شيء يطمع فيه الجميع تقريبًا في مرحلة ما من حياتهم. ونحن نقضي كل يوم جانبًا كبيرًا من وقتنا في العمل بطريقة ما لكسب المال.

وبذلك تميل رغبات قلوبنا إلى التمركز حول عملنا. لكن ينبغي لنا بدلًا من ذلك أن ننظر إلى عملنا على أنه وسيلة للقيام بعمل الله، بأن نكون نورًا ومصدر تشجيع لمن حولنا. «وكل ما فعلتم بقول أو فعل، فاعملوا الكل باسم الرب يسوع، شاكرين الله والآب به» –كولوسي 3:17.

نسمع هنا وهناك كثيرًا عن الطمع في المال؛ لكننا لا نسمع كثيرًا عن الطمع في مناصب لا يحق لنا السعي إليها. ليس من الخطأ أن نرغب في القيادة في مجال الأعمال أو غيره. بل إن تولي شخص زمام القيادة ليكون وسيلة لبركة الآخرين هو بركة لهم. غير أن الرغبة في القيادة من أجل سمعتنا الشخصية رغبة خاطئة، وهي كبرياء. فنحن جميعًا بشر ولسنا كاملين، ومع ذلك ينبغي أن نتجاوز نقائصنا ونكون بركة. ونعلم جميعًا أن الله أعطى كل واحد منا مواهب مختلفة. فلنستخدم تلك المواهب من أجل ملكوت الله.

أحيانًا نبذل جهدًا كبيرًا لإشباع رغبات جسدنا في الراحة، فنغفل عن الغرض الحقيقي الذي وضعنا الله هنا من أجله. ويقف جسدنا في طريقنا. وهذا ما حدث مع عخان. فبدلًا من أن يكرّس عخان اهتمامه كله للقتال ضد العدو، قال: «إني رأيت في الغنيمة رداءً شنعاريًا نفيسًا ومئتي شاقل فضة ولسان ذهب وزنه خمسون شاقلًا، فاشتهيتها وأخذتها…» –يشوع 7:21.

لا أعرف كيف كان الأمر، لكنني أتصور أن المكان كان يعج بالضوضاء والفوضى الدامية. إن كان الأمر كذلك، فبماذا كان عخان يفكر وسط معركة دامية حتى يطمع؟ لا أستطيع أن أفكر إلا في أن الرغبة الأولى لدى عخان لم تكن مشيئة الله، بل إشباع رغباته الخاصة. ومن المحزن جدًا أن كثيرين من شعب الله قُتلوا بسبب خطية عخان. فإذا رأينا أن لدينا رغبة لا ترضي الله، فلنهرب منها ونسعَ إلى اكتساب رغبة ترضي الله.

نرى أن تنمية رغبة صالحة ترضي الله وتشجعنا أو تقودنا إلى الاقتراب منه أمر مهم. وأهم رغبة هي أن نعرف الله حقًا. وهذا قريب جدًا من الوصية العظمى—أن نحب الرب إلهنا بكل قلبنا. ومن الواضح أننا نحتاج أيضًا إلى الرغبة في محبة الرب إلهنا بكل قلبنا. غير أنه تمر في حياتنا أوقات نحتاج فيها إلى اتخاذ خطوة محددة أو اتخاذ قرار بأن نحب الله بكل قلبنا. وقد تكون هناك أمور كثيرة يريد الله منا أن نتخلى عنها.

نعلم جميعًا أن ضغط الأقران يؤثر في رغباتنا. ونحتاج إلى إخوة وأخوات يسيرون إلى جانبنا ويشجعوننا في علاقتنا بالمسيح. وقد يصرف الأصدقاء انتباهنا إلى شيء غير المسيح. لذلك علينا أن ننتبه إلى أصدقائنا المقربين. وينبغي أن نبحث عن أصدقاء يبنوننا. فالصديق الذي يستطيع أن يسير إلى جانبنا ويشجعنا في مسيرتنا مع الله يساوي كل شيء. وبصفتنا بشرًا، لا نستطيع دائمًا أن نرى الأمور كلها على نحو صحيح بمفردنا. ونحتاج إلى آخرين يساعدوننا على رؤية مواطن عَمَانا. والصديق المقرّب الذي يريد بصدق أن يساعدنا على اتباع الله، يعيننا على النظر إلى ما هو صواب في عيني الله. وربما نحتاج إلى إخضاع جسدنا والرجوع إلى الله، لكي ننمّي رغبات طاهرة وصالحة.

عندما نتأمل رغبات القلب، نرى أن لها تأثيرًا كبيرًا فيمن نكون ومن سنصير. فعندما يرغب قلبنا في شيء، نسعى إليه بتوق عميق. وفي الواقع، ترد في الكتاب المقدس أمثلة أعطى فيها الله أناسًا رغبات تخدمه. «فقمت ليلًا أنا ورجال قليلون معي، ولم أخبر أحدًا بما جعله إلهي في قلبي لأعمله في أورشليم. ولم يكن معي دابة إلا الدابة التي كنت راكبًا عليها» –نحميا 2:12. ونقرأ أيضًا… «ودعا موسى بصلئيل وأهوليآب وكل رجل حكيم القلب، الذي جعل الرب في قلبه حكمة، كل من أنهضه قلبه أن يتقدم إلى العمل ليعمله» –الخروج 36:2.

تذكّروا أن كلمة رغبة تعني توقًا عميقًا أو اشتهاءً أو أمنية. فإذا أردنا أن تكون مسيرتنا مع الله مثمرة، فعلينا أن تكون لدينا الرغبات التي لدى الله، لأن رغباته ستغيّر حياتنا. «فأكلوا وشبعوا جدًا، وأتاهم بما اشتهوا. لم يبرحوا عن شهوتهم. والطعام بعد في أفواههم، غضب الله صعد عليهم وقتل من أسمنهم، وأسقط مختاري إسرائيل» –مزمور 78:29-31. مع أن الله قاد بني إسرائيل إلى البرية، وأعطاهم ماءً ومنًا، بل ومكانًا يعبدونه فيه، فإنهم لم يكتفوا وظلوا يشتهون أمورًا أخرى. وقد نال بنو إسرائيل ما اشتهوه، لكن انتهى بهم الأمر إلى دفع الثمن بأرواحهم.

ومن الأمثلة الجيدة الأخرى على أن الله يعطي الناس ما يشتهونه ما نجده في 1 صموئيل 8، حين أراد بنو إسرائيل ملكًا عليهم مثل سائر الأمم. «وقالوا له: هوذا أنت قد شخت، وابناك لم يسيرا في طرقك. فالآن اجعل لنا ملكًا يقضي لنا كسائر الشعوب. فساء الأمر في عيني صموئيل إذ قالوا: أعطنا ملكًا يقضي لنا. وصلى صموئيل إلى الرب. فقال الرب لصموئيل: اسمع لصوت الشعب في كل ما يقولون لك، لأنهم لم يرفضوك أنت، بل إياي رفضوا لكي لا أملك عليهم» –1 صموئيل 8:5-7. يا إسرائيل، «…فأتاهم بما اشتهوا» –مزمور 78:29.

يبدو كأن الرب يقول: «لنتركهم يفعلون ما يريدون ونعطهم ملكًا». لكن الرب يعدد لاحقًا في الإصحاح كل الأمور السيئة التي ستأتي مع وجود ملك. كما يخبر الرب صموئيل بمن سيحكم بني إسرائيل. وبعد أن مُسح ملكهم، كان عليهم أن يخدموه، ولم يعودوا قادرين على خدمة الله وحده. تأملوا سبب إخراج الله لهم من مصر في المقام الأول. ألم يكن ذلك لكي يخدموا الله الحقيقي وحده؟

مثل بني إسرائيل، شهدنا أعمال الله العجيبة. إن كنا قد وُلدنا من روح الله، فهو الذي أخرجنا من «مصرنا»؛ وأرانا طريق الحياة؛ وأخرجنا من الوحل؛ وأثبت أقدامنا على صخرة صلبة. ومع ذلك، نميل نحن البشر إلى الطمع والتوق إلى شيء نظن أنه أفضل. نطلب من الله أن يمنحنا الحكمة وأن يسدّ احتياجاتنا، لكننا في أعماقنا نتوسل إلى الله أن يحقق رغباتنا الأنانية.

علينا أن نسلّم كل جانب من جوانب حياتنا لسيطرة الله. فالله يعرف ما هو الأفضل لنا، لكن إن أصررنا، فإنه سيعطينا بحسب رغباتنا الأنانية.

تذكّروا أن هذه الأرض ليست موطننا. والنهاية آتية، وهذا ما يضعه الله في حسبانه. نحن لا نعرف ما هو الأفضل لنا، لكن الله يعرف. فلنؤمن ونغيّر رغباتنا، طالبين ما يريد الله منا أن نحققه في هذه الحياة. «تلذّذ بالرب أيضًا، فيعطيك سؤل قلبك» –مزامير 37:4. و«حينئذ تتلذّذ بالرب، وأركبك على مرتفعات الأرض، وأطعمك ميراث يعقوب أبيك، لأن فم الرب تكلم» –إشعياء 58:14

Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalm 37:4.

Down deep within every person is a desire to be, or to do, something of value. If we, as humans, had no desire to do anything, life would be boring, and we would be nothing more than a robot. We all know that God wants more from us than to be a robot; He wants us to serve Him with our whole heart.

The meaning for the word desire is: to wish or long for; to crave; to want. Wish, want, crave, and covet all mean to have a longing for. Desire stresses the strength of feeling and often implies strong intention or aim.

Isn’t that what God wants from us—a desire with craving and intentional aim? Yes, it is, but this doesn’t happen on its own, nor does it happen automatically. Our desires are so strong that of ourselves we are no match for them; we need something outside of ourselves to be in control. According to the Bible, we must become born again. When we get born again, we become a new creature in Christ with new desires that God puts inside us. The way He does this, is by giving us a new heart.

God allows each of us to choose if we will serve Him or if we will not. He will not force us to yield ourselves to His will, nor will He force us to serve Him. But, if we are truly born again and serve the Lord joyfully and willingly, then He will give us godly desires which we will want to fulfill.

Does the Christian life become like clockwork just because we get a new heart and our desires have been turned towards serving God? I believe the answer is both yes and no. After we are walking with Christ for some time, we discover that Satan wants to change our desires in such a way that we would rather please him (Satan) instead of the Lord. Because of this, we need to be on guard. Satan wants to set spiritual snares for us. One of the ways he does this is by enticing our flesh.

There are good desires and bad desires. Some desires will bring us closer to Christ and some will draw us away. As Jesus walked on this earth, we know that His desire was to do the will of His Father. Out of His desire, He stayed focused on what He needed to do, even when His flesh was weak. There are two examples of this: one was when Jesus was tempted in the desert to make stones into bread, and the other was when He was in the garden praying right before He was crucified.

When we look at the account in the garden, we see that He did not want to take the cup that was before Him. In other words, Jesus desired to not go through the suffering, but praise God, He chose to please His Father. He laid down His flesh, obeyed the will of God, and allowed Himself to be crucified for our sins. Jesus looked at the long-term effect, and poured Himself into what He knew was right, rather than going by His own feelings. However, He did acknowledge His feelings by expressing them to God when He was praying in the garden. It is the same way with us—there are times that we need to be honest about our feelings and express them to God or to someone else. Yet we cannot walk by our feelings because we must act and do what we know is right according to the word of God.

Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23. If Solomon, the wisest man who ever lived says this, then we should take heed to it. The desires of the heart will make a difference on where we will end up in life. As we are fulfilling one of our desires by acting on it…with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength… –Mark 12:30, we actually feed that desire, causing it to develop into an even deeper longing and passion. As we then act on this stronger, passionate desire, we end up feeding that desire even more. Thus, the vicious cycle continues, repeating itself again and again.

Instead of feeding your desire, you can choose to hinder it—by acting against it. If you have a desire that is not good, and you need to change it to a godly desire, you can act against your original desire and do what is right. In so doing it will start to change your bad desire into one that is right. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also –Matthew 6:21; Luke 12:34.

And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth –Luke 12:15. Covetousness is an ungodly desire. Without bringing it into check, it will become a snare. Money is something that we all need, yet it is something that almost everyone at some point in life covets. Every day we spend much of our time working in some way to earn money.

In so doing, our heart’s desires tend to become focused on our work. Instead, we should see our job as a way of doing God’s work by being a light and encouragement to the ones around us. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him –Colossians 3:17.

Here and there we hear a lot about coveting money; however, we don’t hear much about coveting positions that are not lawful for us. It is not wrong to desire leadership in business or whatever it may be. In fact, it is a blessing for others if someone will stand up and provide leadership as a way to bless others. However, it is a wrong desire to want leadership for our own reputation, which is pride. We are all human and we are not perfect, yet we need to rise above our weaknesses and be a blessing. We all know that God gave each of us different gifts. Let’s use those gifts for the kingdom of God.

Sometimes we are trying so hard to fulfill our fleshly comforts that we lose sight of the real purpose that God has put us here. Our flesh stands in the way. It was this way with Achan. Instead of Achan putting his whole focus on the fight against the enemy, he said that, When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them… –Joshua 7:21.

I don’t know what it was like, but I picture there being loud noises and a bloody mess. If that’s the case, what was Achan thinking in the midst of a bloody battle that made him covet? The only thing I can think of, is that Achan’s number one desire was not on God’s will but was on fulfilling his own desires. It’s very sad that there were so many of God’s people killed because of Achan’s sin. If we see that we have a desire that is not godly, then let’s flee from that desire and work towards gaining a desire that is godly.

We see it is important to develop a godly desire that will encourage or lead us closer to God. The most important desire is to truly know God. That would be very close to the greatest commandment—to love the Lord thy God with all thy heart. To love the Lord thy God with all thy heart you obviously also need to have a desire to love Him. However, there are times in our life that we will need to take a specific action or purpose to love God with all our heart. There are many things that God may want us to surrender.

We all know that peer pressure influences our desires. We need brothers and sisters to walk beside us and encourage us in our relationship with Christ. Friends can draw our attention to something other than Christ. That is why we need to be careful who our close friends are. We need to seek out friends who will be upbuilding. A friend that can walk beside us and encourage us in our walk with God, is worth everything. As humans, we can’t always see everything correctly by ourselves. We need others to help us see our blind spots. A close friend who genuinely wants to help us follow God, will help us look at what is right in God’s eyes. Maybe we need to surrender our flesh and get right with God so we can develop desires that are pure and godly.

As we look at the heart’s desires, we see they have a major impact on who we are and who we will become. When our heart desires something, we pursue it with a deep longing. In fact, there are examples in the Bible where God gave people desires to serve Him. And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon –Nehemiah 2:12. Reading further… And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it –Exodus 36:2.

Remember, the word desire is a deep longing, craving, or wish. If we are wanting a walk with God that is flourishing, then we must have the desires that God has, since His desires will change our life. So they did eat, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire; They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths, The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel –Psalm 78:29-31. Even though God led the Israelites into the wilderness, gave them water and manna, and even a place to worship Him, they were still not satisfied and desired other things. The children of Israel were granted their desires, but they ended up needing to pay with their own lives.

Another good example of God giving people their own desires is found in 1 Samuel 8 when the children of Israel wanted a king over them just like all the other nations. And [they] said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the LORD. And the LORD said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them –1 Samuel 8:5-7. Oh Israel, …for he (God) gave them their own desire –Psalm 78:29.

It sounds like the Lord is saying, “Let’s let them have their own way and give them a king.” However, later in the chapter He lists all the bad things that will come with having a king. The Lord also tells Samuel who will rule over the children of Israel. After their king was anointed, they needed to serve him and could no longer serve God only. Consider why God brought them out of Egypt in the first place. Wasn’t it so they could serve the only true God?

Just like the children of Israel, we have seen God’s wonderous works. If we have been born of God’s Spirit, He led us out of our “Egypt”; He showed us the path of life; He brought us out of the miry clay; He set our feet on a solid rock. Still, we as humans tend to covet and long for something that we think is better. We ask God to give us wisdom and that He would provide for our needs, yet down deep inside we beg for God to give us our selfish desires.

We need to surrender every area of our life to God’s control. God knows what is best for us, however, if we insist, He will give us according to our selfish desires.

Remember, this earth is not our home. The end is coming, which is what God has in mind. We don’t know what is best for us, but God does. Let’s have faith and change our desires for that which God wants us to fulfill in this life. Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalms 37:4. And, Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it–Isaiah 58:14

Verlustig u ook in de HEERE; dan zal Hij u geven de begeerten van uw hart –Psalm 37:4.

Diep vanbinnen heeft ieder mens de wens om iets waardevols te zijn of te doen. Als wij mensen geen verlangen hadden om iets te doen, zou het leven saai zijn en zouden we niet meer zijn dan een robot. We weten allemaal dat God meer van ons wil dan dat we een robot zijn; Hij wil dat we Hem met heel ons hart dienen.

De betekenis van het woord verlangen is: wensen of ergens naar verlangen; begeren; willen. Wensen, willen, begeren en begeren hebben allemaal de betekenis van ergens naar verlangen. Verlangen benadrukt de kracht van het gevoel en impliceert vaak een sterke bedoeling of een duidelijk doel.

Is dat niet wat God van ons wil: een verlangen met begeerte en een doelgerichte bedoeling? Jazeker, maar dat gebeurt niet vanzelf en ook niet automatisch. Onze verlangens zijn zo sterk dat we er op eigen kracht niet tegenop kunnen; we hebben iets buiten onszelf nodig om de controle te hebben. Volgens de Bijbel moeten we wedergeboren worden. Wanneer we wedergeboren worden, worden we een nieuw schepsel in Christus, met nieuwe verlangens die God in ons legt. Dat doet Hij door ons een nieuw hart te geven.

God laat ieder van ons kiezen of we Hem wel of niet zullen dienen. Hij zal ons niet dwingen ons aan Zijn wil over te geven en Hij zal ons evenmin dwingen Hem te dienen. Maar als we werkelijk wedergeboren zijn en de Heer met vreugde en bereidwillig dienen, zal Hij ons godvruchtige verlangens geven die we willen vervullen.

Wordt het christelijke leven vanzelf als een uurwerk, alleen omdat we een nieuw hart krijgen en onze verlangens op het dienen van God gericht zijn? Ik geloof dat het antwoord zowel ja als nee is. Nadat we enige tijd met Christus hebben gewandeld, ontdekken we dat Satan onze verlangens wil veranderen, zodat we liever hem (Satan) behagen dan de Heer. Daarom moeten we op onze hoede zijn. Satan wil geestelijke strikken voor ons spannen. Een van de manieren waarop hij dat doet, is door ons vlees te verleiden.

Er zijn goede en slechte verlangens. Sommige verlangens brengen ons dichter bij Christus en andere voeren ons van Hem weg. Toen Jezus op aarde wandelde, weten we dat het Zijn verlangen was de wil van Zijn Vader te doen. Vanuit dat verlangen bleef Hij gericht op wat Hij moest doen, zelfs wanneer Zijn vlees zwak was. Daar zijn twee voorbeelden van: het eerste was toen Jezus in de woestijn werd verzocht om stenen in brood te veranderen, en het andere toen Hij in de tuin bad, vlak voordat Hij werd gekruisigd.

Wanneer we het verslag over de tuin bekijken, zien we dat Hij de beker die Hem wachtte niet wilde drinken. Met andere woorden, Jezus verlangde ernaar het lijden niet te hoeven ondergaan, maar God zij geprezen: Hij koos ervoor Zijn Vader te behagen. Hij legde Zijn vlees af, gehoorzaamde Gods wil en liet Zich voor onze zonden kruisigen. Jezus keek naar de gevolgen op lange termijn en zette Zich volledig in voor wat Hij wist dat juist was, in plaats van af te gaan op Zijn eigen gevoelens. Toch erkende Hij Zijn gevoelens door ze tegenover God uit te spreken toen Hij in de tuin bad. Zo is het ook met ons: soms moeten we eerlijk zijn over onze gevoelens en ze aan God of aan iemand anders uiten. Toch kunnen we niet op onze gevoelens afgaan, want we moeten handelen en doen wat we weten dat juist is volgens het woord van God.

Behoed uw hart boven al wat te bewaren is, want daaruit zijn de uitgangen des levens –Spreuken 4:23. Als Salomo, de wijste man die ooit heeft geleefd, dit zegt, moeten we er acht op slaan. De verlangens van ons hart maken verschil voor waar we in het leven terechtkomen. Wanneer we een van onze verlangens vervullen door ernaar te handelen…met geheel uw ziel, en met geheel uw verstand, en met geheel uw kracht… –Markus 12:30, voeden we dat verlangen in feite, waardoor het uitgroeit tot een nog dieper verlangen en een grotere hartstocht. Wanneer we vervolgens naar dat sterkere, hartstochtelijke verlangen handelen, voeden we het nog meer. Zo gaat de vicieuze cirkel door en herhaalt die zich steeds opnieuw.

In plaats van je verlangen te voeden, kun je ervoor kiezen het te beteugelen door ertegenin te handelen. Als je een verlangen hebt dat niet goed is en je het in een godvruchtig verlangen wilt veranderen, kun je tegen je oorspronkelijke verlangen ingaan en doen wat juist is. Zo zal je slechte verlangen beginnen te veranderen in een juist verlangen. Want waar uw schat is, daar zal ook uw hart zijn –Mattheüs 6:21; Lukas 12:34.

En Hij zeide tot hen: Ziet toe, en wacht u van de gierigheid; want iemands leven bestaat niet in den overvloed zijner goederen –Lukas 12:15. Gierigheid is een goddeloos verlangen. Als we die niet beteugelen, wordt ze een strik. Geld is iets wat we allemaal nodig hebben, en toch is het iets waar bijna iedereen op een bepaald moment in het leven naar begeert. Elke dag besteden we veel van onze tijd aan werk om op de een of andere manier geld te verdienen.

Daardoor raken de verlangens van ons hart vaak op ons werk gericht. In plaats daarvan zouden we ons werk moeten zien als een manier om Gods werk te doen, door een licht en een bemoediging te zijn voor de mensen om ons heen. En al wat gij doet met woorden of met werken, doet alles in den Naam van den Heere Jezus, dankende God en den Vader door Hem –Kolossenzen 3:17.

Hier en daar horen we veel over het begeren van geld, maar we horen niet veel over het begeren van posities waarop we geen recht hebben. Het is niet verkeerd om leiderschap in het bedrijfsleven of op welk ander gebied ook te verlangen. Het is zelfs een zegen voor anderen als iemand opstaat en leiding geeft om anderen tot zegen te zijn. Het is echter verkeerd om leiderschap te willen voor onze eigen reputatie; dat is trots. We zijn allemaal mensen en niet volmaakt, maar toch moeten we boven onze zwakheden uitstijgen en tot zegen zijn. We weten allemaal dat God ieder van ons verschillende gaven heeft gegeven. Laten we die gaven gebruiken voor het koninkrijk van God.

Soms proberen we zo hard om het onze vleselijke gemakken naar de zin te maken, dat we het werkelijke doel uit het oog verliezen waarvoor God ons hier heeft geplaatst. Ons vlees staat ons in de weg. Zo was het ook met Achan. In plaats van al zijn aandacht op de strijd tegen de vijand te richten, zei hij: Toen ik onder den roof zag een schoon Babylonisch overkleed, en tweehonderd sikkelen zilver, en een gouden tong, van vijftig sikkelen zijn gewicht, zo begeerde ik ze en nam ze… –Jozua 7:21.

Ik weet niet hoe het eraan toeging, maar ik stel me voor dat er harde geluiden waren en dat het een bloederige puinhoop was. Als dat zo was, wat dacht Achan dan midden in een bloedige strijd, dat hij iets begeerde? Ik kan alleen maar denken dat Achans grootste verlangen niet op Gods wil gericht was, maar op het vervullen van zijn eigen verlangens. Het is heel verdrietig dat er zoveel van Gods volk zijn gedood vanwege Achans zonde. Als we zien dat we een verlangen hebben dat niet godvruchtig is, laten we dat verlangen dan ontvluchten en ernaar streven een godvruchtig verlangen te krijgen.

We zien dat het belangrijk is een godvruchtig verlangen te ontwikkelen dat ons aanmoedigt of dichter bij God brengt. Het belangrijkste verlangen is God werkelijk te kennen. Dat komt heel dicht bij het grootste gebod: de Heere, uw God, lief te hebben met heel uw hart. Om de Heere, uw God, met heel uw hart lief te hebben, moet u uiteraard ook een verlangen hebben om Hem lief te hebben. Toch zijn er momenten in ons leven waarop we doelbewust iets moeten doen om God met heel ons hart lief te hebben. Er zijn veel dingen die God van ons kan vragen op te geven.

We weten allemaal dat groepsdruk onze verlangens beïnvloedt. We hebben broeders en zusters nodig die met ons meelopen en ons aanmoedigen in onze relatie met Christus. Vrienden kunnen onze aandacht op iets anders dan Christus richten. Daarom moeten we zorgvuldig kiezen wie onze goede vrienden zijn. We moeten vrienden zoeken die ons opbouwen. Een vriend die met ons meeloopt en ons aanmoedigt in onze wandel met God, is alles waard. Als mensen kunnen we niet altijd alles zelf goed zien. We hebben anderen nodig om ons op onze blinde vlekken te wijzen. Een goede vriend die ons oprecht wil helpen God te volgen, zal ons helpen te zien wat goed is in Gods ogen. Misschien moeten we ons vlees overgeven en ons met God verzoenen, zodat we verlangens kunnen ontwikkelen die zuiver en godvruchtig zijn.

Wanneer we de verlangens van het hart bekijken, zien we dat die grote invloed hebben op wie we zijn en wie we zullen worden. Wanneer ons hart iets verlangt, streven we ernaar met een diep verlangen. In de Bijbel staan zelfs voorbeelden van mensen aan wie God het verlangen gaf Hem te dienen. En ik stond des nachts op, ik en enige weinige mannen met mij; en ik vertelde niemand, wat mijn God in mijn hart gegeven had te doen te Jeruzalem: en er was geen beest met mij, dan het beest waarop ik reed –Nehemia 2:12. Lees verder… En Mozes riep Bezaleël en Aholiab, en allen die wijs van hart waren, in wier hart de HEERE wijsheid had gegeven, ja, een ieder wiens hart hem aandreef, om tot het werk te komen, om dat te doen –Exodus 36:2.

Denk eraan: het woord verlangen betekent een diep verlangen, een sterke begeerte of een wens. Als we een bloeiende wandel met God willen hebben, moeten we de verlangens hebben die God heeft, want Zijn verlangens zullen ons leven veranderen. En zij aten en werden zeer verzadigd; Hij gaf hun hun begeerte; zij werden niet vervreemd van hun lust. Terwijl hun spijze nog in hun mond was, zo kwam de toorn Gods over hen, en doodde de vetsten onder hen, en sloeg de jongelingen van Israël neder –Psalm 78:29-31. Hoewel God de Israëlieten naar de woestijn leidde, hun water en manna gaf en hun zelfs een plaats gaf om Hem te aanbidden, waren ze nog steeds niet tevreden en verlangden ze naar andere dingen. De kinderen Israëls kregen wat ze verlangden, maar uiteindelijk moesten ze dat met hun eigen leven bekopen.

Een ander goed voorbeeld van God die mensen hun eigen verlangens geeft, vinden we in 1 Samuël 8, toen de kinderen Israëls een koning over zich wilden, net als alle andere volken. En [zij] zeiden tot hem: Zie, gij zijt oud, en uw zonen wandelen niet in uw wegen; zo stel nu een koning over ons, om ons te richten, gelijk al de volken. Maar dit woord was kwaad in de ogen van Samuël, als zij zeiden: Geef ons een koning, om ons te richten. En Samuël bad tot den HEERE. Doch de HEERE zeide tot Samuël: Hoor naar de stem des volks, in alles wat zij tot u zullen zeggen; want zij hebben u niet verworpen, maar Mij hebben zij verworpen, dat Ik over hen geen Koning zou zijn –1 Samuël 8:5-7. O Israël, …want Hij gaf hun hun begeerte –Psalm 78:29.

Het klinkt alsof de Heer zegt: ‘Laten we hun hun zin geven en hun een koning geven.’ Later in het hoofdstuk noemt Hij echter alle slechte dingen die gepaard zullen gaan met het hebben van een koning. De Heer vertelt Samuël ook wie er over de kinderen Israëls zal heersen. Nadat hun koning gezalfd was, moesten ze hem dienen en konden ze niet langer alleen God dienen. Bedenk waarom God hen in de eerste plaats uit Egypte leidde. Was dat niet zodat ze de enige ware God konden dienen?

Net als de kinderen Israëls hebben wij Gods wonderbare werken gezien. Als we uit Gods Geest geboren zijn, heeft Hij ons uit ons ‘Egypte’ geleid; Hij heeft ons de weg ten leven gewezen; Hij heeft ons uit het modderige slijk gehaald; Hij heeft onze voeten op een vaste rots gezet. Toch hebben wij als mensen de neiging iets te begeren en ernaar te verlangen waarvan we denken dat het beter is. We vragen God ons wijsheid te geven en in onze behoeften te voorzien, maar diep vanbinnen smeken we God onze zelfzuchtige verlangens te vervullen.

We moeten elk gebied van ons leven aan Gods heerschappij overgeven. God weet wat het beste voor ons is, maar als we erop staan, zal Hij ons geven wat overeenkomt met onze zelfzuchtige verlangens.

Denk eraan: deze aarde is niet ons thuis. Het einde komt eraan; daar houdt God rekening mee. Wij weten niet wat het beste voor ons is, maar God wel. Laten we geloof hebben en onze verlangens veranderen, zodat we verlangen te vervullen wat God in dit leven van ons wil. Verlustig u ook in de HEERE; dan zal Hij u geven de begeerten van uw hart –Psalmen 37:4. En: Dan zult gij u verlustigen in den HEERE, en Ik zal u doen rijden op de hoogten der aarde, en Ik zal u spijzigen met de erve van Jakob, uw vader; want de mond des HEEREN heeft het gesproken –Jesaja 58:14
