Something that I have noticed repeatedly as I read God’s Word is that God’s people are confident. Consider Noah. When God told him to build an ark, there was no wavering. He spent the next 120 years confidently doing just that. Then I think of Abraham confidently doing whatever God asked of him, even when He asked him to sacrifice his only son. We cannot speak of confidence without mentioning Caleb and Joshua, who after hearing all their comrades give their doubting reports, confidently described what they should do with this new land of Canaan: …Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it –Numbers 13:30.

We cannot forget about David who went out and silenced the large naysayer—Goliath. Nor can we forget Daniel, Gideon, Job, Ezekiel, Isaiah, or Jeremiah and all that they did with confidence. As we study each of these men of faith and many others, we clearly see that they had a great amount of confidence in their God!

Some might say that if God worked the same way today as He did back then, we would be more confident. Maybe if God were still an Old Testament God, it would be easier. If He led us into battle, destroyed our enemies, parted seas, and caused bread to fall from heaven, then we would have more confidence in Him.

Now let us consider the New Testament. It is quite different. God’s people are commanded to leave everything for the sake of Christ. They are promised that the world will hate them. They are told that it is difficult for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. They are guaranteed that they will be blessed if they suffer, if they are poor, if they are hungry, and if they mourn.

Can people still have confidence in a God that asks His people to follow Him under these circumstances? Yes! The disciples proved it. They went about preaching and teaching. They were hunted and beaten repeatedly. The deacon, Stephen, showed great confidence when he was brought before his oppressors, even when they began to gnash their teeth at him, and stone him. Stephen showed confidence until he took his last agonizing breath.

Before he became the apostle Paul, Saul was an enemy of the cross, the chiefest of sinners, and a Pharisee of the Pharisees. He was a prominent man, taught by the best. Then he met the living God, and everything changed. After Paul was baptized, …straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God –Acts 9:20. The next verse says the people were amazed, then in verse 23, five verses after he was baptized, it says that the Jews took counsel to kill him.

It takes a lot of confidence in God to change a man like that, to cause him to, overnight, completely change allegiance. According to his own testimony, Paul was faithful until his death: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: –2 Timothy 4:6-7.

God did amazing things in the New Testament. He healed the blind and raised the dead to life again. He released prisoners and struck people dead. Some may say it would be easier to have great confidence in God if we were still living in the New Testament Bible times when Jesus physically walked and talked here on this earth.

What about after the Bible?

In the early church, we again see a group of people that did not waver; they had confidence in their God, a God they could not see. Tens of thousands of God’s people stood boldly before the world and proclaimed its wickedness, and tens of thousands of God’s people were killed. The confidence of these people was never questioned. They were called fools, for believing in a “God they could not see”. They were mocked and scorned for their ‘foolishness’, they were …killed all the day long… –Psalm 44:22. People questioned their practices, they questioned their religious structure, they questioned the message they preached, they questioned many things, but they never questioned their confidence. These Christians believed in their God, of that there was no doubt.

Strangely, they were not interested in the pleasures of this life; they did not care about the things of this world, and even their very lives were a small thing to give up for their God. Families were torn apart, houses and lands were confiscated, churches were burned, but it did not faze stop them. They lived for something greater, something the heathen could not understand.

Through the time of the early church and the time of the Reformation, people were added to the Kingdom in great numbers. Yes, children did grow up and join their parents’ church, but there were also great masses of new converts from the world. How could anyone convince a worldly person to join a group that was hunted and killed—a group that suffered like the church of Jesus Christ suffered? Yes, we know that salvation is of the Lord, but it was the confidence of God’s people that caused others to wonder, that caused them to seriously consider this new religion of heretics. This was a group of people that would gladly accept the spoiling of their goods, be happy to give all they had to help others, and not resist their capture by the authorities. The true church of Jesus Christ was a group of people that always caused others to wonder, “Who are these people?” They clearly put all their faith in their God, and that was not a common occurrence. They stood up for God’s Truth no matter how hot the fire burned, no matter how miserable their lives were made. It all showed a great confidence, not in themselves, but in their God.

As we look at the church today, what do we see? Some of God’s people are taking up their crosses, and denying the world and the lust thereof, other people are not. Is the church of today still known for being confident in their God?

As professing Christians, have we lost some of this biblical confidence? Are we still out there undeniably serving the one true God? Do people look at us, and stand in awe of the confidence we are displaying in our God? Too many people of today are saying they are Christians, but they demonstrate very little confidence in God. They live quite closely to the ways of the world. Instead of enjoying persecution, they enjoy many of the same things that the world does. Each of us needs the fire of God burning deep within our hearts, a fire that cannot be quenched.

Confidence equals obedience. I have met many Christians of our day whose ancestors gave their lives for Christ, and their grandfathers bravely led the church, but there now seems to be something missing. As I interact with many God-fearing Christians, it seems that there is a prevailing struggle with confidence—a confidence in a living God who is all-powerful, all-knowing, and all-present.

In the uncertainty of our world today, we need to once more boldly proclaim the gospel message just like true believers did in times past. We need to clearly draw distinct biblical lines between right and wrong. We need to rid ourselves of all these wretched gray areas and call sin, sin. It seems that we have lost the confidence to speak out against the sin of our day. If we confidently proclaim what God has declared, there are some people who will not like us. We need brethren that are not afraid to be scoffed at and are willing to take the road less traveled.

Right before our Lord ascended on high, He gave His disciples a glorious promise, …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

Ye shall receive power! Not power from men, not power from kingdoms of this world, but real, overcoming power—power that comes only from the Holy Ghost! After we receive this power, we go forward as a new creature, confidently proclaiming the blessed Gospel of our Redeemer.

We need hearts that burn with God’s will and God’s word. We need hearts aflame!

I was eating lunch one day when a couple approached me with a serious question, “Why does the church think it has to control us?” After they explained how they think they should be able to be ‘free in Christ’, I was excited to answer their questions. However, there was another ordained brother sitting beside me. So, I decided to wait, hoping that he would engage the couple, but he said nothing. As another forty-five minutes passed, I tried to explain to the couple how they needed to deny themselves and submit to the church. And that if they laid down their lives fully, if they surrendered all, they would no longer have such a struggle with church structure.

The couple seemed encouraged and ready to give things another try. However, the minister beside me did not seem too pleased, so I asked him what he thought. He said that his father told him years ago that when he was young, he thought he had all the answers. After he got old, he realized he did not know anything, and that church issues are too complicated to solve. We need to just try to get along.

Is this the answer, to just act like we don’t know anything and hope that it all works out in the end? I do understand that we don’t have all the answers. After all, I realize that I have more questions than answers most times. However, I do know what God wants for His church! …Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

A glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish! Will we, as God’s people, once again stand for truth, deny the world, and like sheep allow ourselves to be led to the slaughter? Or have we made our lives too comfortable to deny, have we chosen the easy (broad) way and denied the straight and narrow? Have we signed a peace deal with the servants of sin? If I weep as I write, will you weep as you read?

The definition of the word confidence is a feeling or consciousness of one’s powers. Many people today have confused confidence with pride, and for good reason. Most people that are confident are confident in themselves, instead of being confident in Christ. We see this self-confidence all around us. There are life coaches and counselors all over the globe, telling people to believe in themselves, telling them to be confident in themselves. When one is confident in themselves, they often do become proud. Remember the world does not look down on pride. You can hear the world boast of its pride everywhere you look. People are proud of their children, proud of their country, proud of their favorite sports team, proud of their lawns, proud of basically everything that is good in their lives. We must remember that pride is sin and will not enter heaven. While confidence in one’s self or things is pride, confidence in God is not!

It is not a new concept to confuse confidence in God, with pride. David’s oldest brother Eliab said to him, “I know thy pride”. Was David proud? No, he simply had a great deal of confidence in his God.

Could it be that a false sense of humility has silenced the church? Could it be that this tactic of the enemy is one of Satan’s current weapons against Christians? Could it also be the reason that the Church seems to be struggling in all parts of the world? What if faithful men would once again step out in faith in their God with great confidence and by their words and actions show this sinned-stained world the straight and narrow way—into the Kingdom of God?!

We all must agree, we live in a confused world—one that is confused as to what is right and what is wrong. What if the world could look at the Church and once again find a group of people that know exactly where they are going—a church that has no doubt which way is the right way—a church that can boldly proclaim the answer to the problems of our day—a church that is nothing less than completely confident in their GOD?

Let us come before our God on bended knee, with our hearts bowed low, demonstrating genuine godly sorrow for where we have lost our way. Let us earnestly seek God’s will for ourselves, for our families, for our churches, and for our neighbors. Let us ask God to show us how we can be His examples to the world around us. The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn; To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified –Isaiah 61:1-3.

Noe jeg gjentatte ganger har lagt merke til når jeg leser Guds ord, er at Guds folk er frimodige. Tenk på Noah. Da Gud ba ham bygge en ark, nølte han ikke. De neste 120 årene brukte han frimodig på nettopp dette. Så tenker jeg på Abraham, som frimodig gjorde alt Gud ba ham om, også da Han ba ham ofre sin eneste sønn. Vi kan ikke snakke om frimodighet uten å nevne Kaleb og Josva. Etter å ha hørt alle kameratene sine komme med tvilende rapporter, beskrev de frimodig hva de burde gjøre med dette nye landet Kanaan: …La oss straks dra opp og ta det i eie! Vi er sterke nok til å innta det – 4. Mosebok 13:30.

Vi må heller ikke glemme David, som gikk ut og brakte den store motstanderen – Goliat – til taushet. Vi må heller ikke glemme Daniel, Gideon, Job, Esekiel, Jesaja eller Jeremia, og alt de gjorde med frimodighet. Når vi studerer hver av disse troens menn og mange andre, ser vi tydelig at de hadde stor frimodighet i sin Gud!

Noen vil kanskje si at dersom Gud handlet på samme måte i dag som den gang, ville vi vært mer frimodige. Kanskje det ville vært lettere dersom Gud fortsatt var en Gud fra Det gamle testamentet. Hvis Han førte oss ut i kamp, tilintetgjorde fiendene våre, delte havene og lot brød falle fra himmelen, ville vi da hatt større frimodighet i Ham?

La oss nå se på Det nye testamentet. Det er ganske annerledes. Guds folk blir befalt å forlate alt for Kristi skyld. De blir lovet at verden skal hate dem. De får høre at det er vanskelig for en rik å komme inn i Guds rike. De blir forsikret om at de skal bli velsignet hvis de lider, hvis de er fattige, hvis de sulter, og hvis de sørger.

Kan folk fortsatt ha frimodighet i en Gud som ber sitt folk følge Ham under slike omstendigheter? Ja! Disiplene beviste det. De gikk omkring og forkynte og underviste. De ble gjentatte ganger forfulgt og slått. Diakonen Stefan viste stor frimodighet da han ble ført fram for undertrykkerne sine, selv da de begynte å skjære tenner mot ham og steine ham. Stefan viste frimodighet helt til han drog sitt siste smertefulle åndedrag.

Før han ble apostelen Paulus, var Saulus en fiende av korset, den største av syndere og en fariseer blant fariseere. Han var en fremstående mann, opplært av de beste. Så møtte han den levende Gud, og alt forandret seg. Etter at Paulus var blitt døpt, …begynte han straks å forkynne i synagogene at Jesus er Guds Sønn – Apostlenes gjerninger 9:20. Det neste verset sier at folk ble forundret, og i vers 23, fem vers etter at han ble døpt, står det at jødene la planer om å drepe ham.

Det krever stor frimodighet i Gud å forandre en mann slik, å få ham til over natten å skifte lojalitet fullstendig. Ifølge hans eget vitnesbyrd var Paulus trofast helt til sin død: For jeg blir alt ofret, og tiden for min bortgang er nær. Jeg har stridd den gode strid, fullendt løpet og bevart troen – 2. Timoteus 4:6–7.

Gud gjorde fantastiske ting i Det nye testamentet. Han helbredet blinde og vekket døde til liv igjen. Han satte fanger fri og slo folk i hjel. Noen vil kanskje si at det ville vært lettere å ha stor frimodighet i Gud dersom vi fortsatt levde på bibelsk tid i Det nye testamentet, da Jesus fysisk vandret og talte her på jorden.

Hva med tiden etter Bibelen?

I den tidlige kirken ser vi igjen en gruppe mennesker som ikke vaklet; de hadde frimodighet i sin Gud, en Gud de ikke kunne se. Titusener av Guds folk sto modig fram for verden og forkynte dens ondskap, og titusener av Guds folk ble drept. Disse menneskenes frimodighet ble aldri trukket i tvil. De ble kalt dårer fordi de trodde på en «Gud de ikke kunne se». De ble hånet og spottet for sin «dårskap», de ble …drept dagen lang … – Salme 44:22. Folk satte spørsmålstegn ved skikkene deres, ved den religiøse strukturen deres, ved budskapet de forkynte og ved mange andre ting, men aldri ved frimodigheten deres. Det var ingen tvil om at disse kristne trodde på sin Gud.

Merkelig nok var de ikke interessert i dette livets gleder; de brydde seg ikke om tingene i denne verden, og selv livet deres var en liten ting å gi avkall på for Gud. Familier ble revet fra hverandre, hus og jord ble beslaglagt, kirker ble brent, men det stanset dem ikke. De levde for noe større, noe hedningene ikke kunne forstå.

Gjennom den tidlige kirkens tid og reformasjonstiden ble mange føyd til riket. Ja, barn vokste opp og sluttet seg til foreldrenes kirke, men det kom også store mengder nye omvendte fra verden. Hvordan kunne noen overtale et menneske som levde etter verdens skikker, til å slutte seg til en gruppe som ble forfulgt og drept – en gruppe som led slik Jesu Kristi kirke led? Ja, vi vet at frelsen er fra Herren, men det var Guds folks frimodighet som fikk andre til å undre seg, som fikk dem til å overveie denne nye religionen til «kjetterne» alvorlig. Dette var en gruppe mennesker som med glede ville godta at eiendelene deres ble plyndret, gladelig gi alt de hadde for å hjelpe andre, og ikke gjøre motstand når myndighetene pågrep dem. Jesu Kristi sanne kirke var en gruppe mennesker som alltid fikk andre til å undre seg: «Hvem er disse menneskene?» De satte tydelig all sin tro til sin Gud, og det var ikke vanlig. De sto opp for Guds sannhet uansett hvor heftig ilden brant, uansett hvor elendig livet deres ble gjort. Alt dette viste stor frimodighet, ikke i dem selv, men i deres Gud.

Når vi ser på kirken i dag, hva ser vi? Noen av Guds folk tar opp korsene sine og fornekter verden og dens begjær, andre gjør det ikke. Er kirken i dag fortsatt kjent for å være frimodig i sin Gud?

Har vi som bekjenner oss til kristendommen, mistet noe av denne bibelske frimodigheten? Tjener vi fortsatt den ene sanne Gud på en måte som ingen kan være i tvil om? Ser folk på oss og står målløse over frimodigheten vi viser i vår Gud? Altfor mange i dag sier at de er kristne, men viser svært liten frimodighet i Gud. De lever ganske nært verdens veier. I stedet for å glede seg over forfølgelse gleder de seg over mange av de samme tingene som verden gjør. Hver og en av oss trenger Guds ild som brenner dypt i hjertet, en ild som ikke kan slukkes.

Frimodighet betyr lydighet. Jeg har møtt mange kristne i vår tid som har forfedre som ga livet for Kristus, og bestefedre som modig ledet kirken, men nå ser det ut til at noe mangler. Når jeg møter mange gudfryktige kristne, virker det som om frimodighet er en gjennomgående utfordring – frimodighet i en levende Gud som er allmektig, allvitende og allestedsnærværende.

I vår tids usikre verden må vi igjen frimodig forkynne evangeliet, slik sanne troende gjorde før i tiden. Vi må trekke tydelige bibelske grenser mellom rett og galt. Vi må kvitte oss med alle disse elendige gråsonene og kalle synd for synd. Det virker som om vi har mistet frimodigheten til å tale imot vår tids synd. Hvis vi frimodig forkynner det Gud har erklært, vil noen ikke like oss. Vi trenger brødre som ikke er redde for å bli hånet, og som er villige til å gå den mindre beferdede veien.

Like før vår Herre fór opp til himmelen, ga Han disiplene sine et herlig løfte: …dere skal få kraft når Den hellige ånd kommer over dere, og dere skal være mine vitner i Jerusalem og hele Judea, i Samaria og helt til jordens ender – Apostlenes gjerninger 1:8.

Dere skal få kraft! Ikke kraft fra mennesker, ikke kraft fra denne verdens riker, men virkelig, overvinnende kraft – kraft som bare kommer fra Den hellige ånd! Når vi har fått denne kraften, går vi videre som en ny skapning og forkynner frimodig vår Forløsers velsignede evangelium.

Vi trenger hjerter som brenner for Guds vilje og Guds ord. Vi trenger hjerter i brann!

En dag satt jeg og spiste lunsj da et par kom bort til meg med et alvorlig spørsmål: «Hvorfor tror kirken at den må kontrollere oss?» Etter at de hadde forklart hvordan de mente at de burde kunne være «fri i Kristus», gledet jeg meg til å svare på spørsmålene deres. Men en annen ordinert bror satt ved siden av meg. Derfor bestemte jeg meg for å vente, i håp om at han ville snakke med paret, men han sa ingenting. Etter at ytterligere førtifem minutter hadde gått, forsøkte jeg å forklare paret at de måtte fornekte seg selv og underordne seg kirken. Og at hvis de la livet sitt helt ned, hvis de overga alt, ville de ikke lenger streve så mye med kirkens struktur.

Paret virket oppmuntret og klare til å prøve igjen. Men predikanten ved siden av meg virket ikke særlig fornøyd, så jeg spurte ham hva han mente. Han sa at faren hans for mange år siden hadde fortalt ham at da han var ung, trodde han at han hadde alle svarene. Da han ble eldre, innså han at han ikke visste noe, og at spørsmålene i kirken var for kompliserte til å løse. Vi burde bare prøve å komme overens.

Er dette svaret – å bare oppføre oss som om vi ikke vet noe og håpe at alt ordner seg til slutt? Jeg forstår at vi ikke har alle svarene. Jeg innser jo at jeg som oftest har flere spørsmål enn svar. Men jeg vet hva Gud ønsker for sin kirke! …Kristus elsket også kirken og ga seg selv for den, for å hellige den og rense den med vannbadet i Ordet, og slik stille kirken fram for seg i herlighet, uten flekk eller rynke eller noe slikt, men hellig og uten feil – Efeserne 5:25–27.

En herlig kirke, uten flekk eller rynke eller noe slikt, men hellig og uten feil! Skal vi, som Guds folk, igjen stå opp for sannheten, fornekte verden og la oss føre til slakting som sauer? Eller har vi gjort livet vårt for behagelig til å fornekte oss selv? Har vi valgt den lette, brede veien og vendt oss bort fra den smale og trange? Har vi inngått en fredsavtale med syndens tjenere? Hvis jeg gråter mens jeg skriver, vil du gråte mens du leser?

Ordet frimodighet betyr en følelse av eller bevissthet om egne evner. Mange i dag har forvekslet frimodighet med stolthet, og med god grunn. De fleste som er frimodige, er frimodige i seg selv i stedet for i Kristus. Vi ser denne selvtilliten overalt omkring oss. Livsveiledere og rådgivere finnes over hele kloden og forteller folk at de skal tro på seg selv, at de skal ha tillit til seg selv. Når man har tillit til seg selv, blir man ofte stolt. Husk at verden ikke ser ned på stolthet. Overalt hvor du ser, hører du verden skryte av sin stolthet. Folk er stolte av barna sine, landet sitt, favorittidrettslaget sitt, plenene sine, ja, så å si alt som er godt i livet deres. Vi må huske at stolthet er synd og ikke kommer inn i himmelen. Selv om tillit til seg selv eller ting er stolthet, er tillit til Gud det ikke!

Det er ikke noe nytt å forveksle frimodighet i Gud med stolthet. Davids eldste bror Eliab sa til ham: «Jeg kjenner din stolthet.» Var David stolt? Nei, han hadde ganske enkelt stor frimodighet i sin Gud.

Kan det være at en falsk form for ydmykhet har gjort kirken taus? Kan denne fiendens taktikk være et av Satans nåværende våpen mot kristne? Kan det også være grunnen til at kirken ser ut til å streve i alle deler av verden? Hva om trofaste menn igjen trådte fram i tro på sin Gud og med stor frimodighet, og med ord og handlinger viste denne syndbesmittede verden den smale og trange veien inn i Guds rike?!

Vi må alle være enige om at vi lever i en forvirret verden – en verden som er forvirret når det gjelder hva som er rett og galt. Hva om verden kunne se på kirken og igjen finne en gruppe mennesker som vet nøyaktig hvor de er på vei – en kirke som ikke er i tvil om hvilken vei som er den rette – en kirke som frimodig kan forkynne svaret på vår tids problemer – en kirke som ikke er noe mindre enn fullstendig frimodig i sin GUD?

La oss komme fram for vår Gud på kne, med ydmyke hjerter, og vise ekte, gudfryktig sorg over at vi har kommet på avveier. La oss oppriktig søke Guds vilje for oss selv, for familiene våre, for kirkene våre og for naboene våre. La oss be Gud vise oss hvordan vi kan være eksempler for verden omkring oss. Herren Guds Ånd er over meg, for Herren har salvet meg til å forkynne et godt budskap for de ydmyke. Han har sendt meg for å forbinde dem som har et knust hjerte, for å rope ut frihet for fangene og løslatelse for dem som er bundet, for å rope ut et nådens år fra Herren og en hevnens dag fra vår Gud, for å trøste alle som sørger, for å gi dem som sørger i Sion, hodepryd i stedet for aske, gledens olje i stedet for sorg, lovsangsdrakt i stedet for motløs ånd. De skal kalles rettferdighetens terebinter, Herrens planting, så Han kan bli herliggjort – Jesaja 61:1–3.

Something that I have noticed repeatedly as I read God’s Word is that God’s people are confident. Consider Noah. When God told him to build an ark, there was no wavering. He spent the next 120 years confidently doing just that. Then I think of Abraham confidently doing whatever God asked of him, even when He asked him to sacrifice his only son. We cannot speak of confidence without mentioning Caleb and Joshua, who after hearing all their comrades give their doubting reports, confidently described what they should do with this new land of Canaan: …Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it –Numbers 13:30.

We cannot forget about David who went out and silenced the large naysayer—Goliath. Nor can we forget Daniel, Gideon, Job, Ezekiel, Isaiah, or Jeremiah and all that they did with confidence. As we study each of these men of faith and many others, we clearly see that they had a great amount of confidence in their God!

Some might say that if God worked the same way today as He did back then, we would be more confident. Maybe if God were still an Old Testament God, it would be easier. If He led us into battle, destroyed our enemies, parted seas, and caused bread to fall from heaven, then we would have more confidence in Him.

Now let us consider the New Testament. It is quite different. God’s people are commanded to leave everything for the sake of Christ. They are promised that the world will hate them. They are told that it is difficult for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. They are guaranteed that they will be blessed if they suffer, if they are poor, if they are hungry, and if they mourn.

Can people still have confidence in a God that asks His people to follow Him under these circumstances? Yes! The disciples proved it. They went about preaching and teaching. They were hunted and beaten repeatedly. The deacon, Stephen, showed great confidence when he was brought before his oppressors, even when they began to gnash their teeth at him, and stone him. Stephen showed confidence until he took his last agonizing breath.

Before he became the apostle Paul, Saul was an enemy of the cross, the chiefest of sinners, and a Pharisee of the Pharisees. He was a prominent man, taught by the best. Then he met the living God, and everything changed. After Paul was baptized, …straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God –Acts 9:20. The next verse says the people were amazed, then in verse 23, five verses after he was baptized, it says that the Jews took counsel to kill him.

It takes a lot of confidence in God to change a man like that, to cause him to, overnight, completely change allegiance. According to his own testimony, Paul was faithful until his death: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: –2 Timothy 4:6-7.

God did amazing things in the New Testament. He healed the blind and raised the dead to life again. He released prisoners and struck people dead. Some may say it would be easier to have great confidence in God if we were still living in the New Testament Bible times when Jesus physically walked and talked here on this earth.

What about after the Bible?

In the early church, we again see a group of people that did not waver; they had confidence in their God, a God they could not see. Tens of thousands of God’s people stood boldly before the world and proclaimed its wickedness, and tens of thousands of God’s people were killed. The confidence of these people was never questioned. They were called fools, for believing in a “God they could not see”. They were mocked and scorned for their ‘foolishness’, they were …killed all the day long… –Psalm 44:22. People questioned their practices, they questioned their religious structure, they questioned the message they preached, they questioned many things, but they never questioned their confidence. These Christians believed in their God, of that there was no doubt.

Strangely, they were not interested in the pleasures of this life; they did not care about the things of this world, and even their very lives were a small thing to give up for their God. Families were torn apart, houses and lands were confiscated, churches were burned, but it did not faze stop them. They lived for something greater, something the heathen could not understand.

Through the time of the early church and the time of the Reformation, people were added to the Kingdom in great numbers. Yes, children did grow up and join their parents’ church, but there were also great masses of new converts from the world. How could anyone convince a worldly person to join a group that was hunted and killed—a group that suffered like the church of Jesus Christ suffered? Yes, we know that salvation is of the Lord, but it was the confidence of God’s people that caused others to wonder, that caused them to seriously consider this new religion of heretics. This was a group of people that would gladly accept the spoiling of their goods, be happy to give all they had to help others, and not resist their capture by the authorities. The true church of Jesus Christ was a group of people that always caused others to wonder, “Who are these people?” They clearly put all their faith in their God, and that was not a common occurrence. They stood up for God’s Truth no matter how hot the fire burned, no matter how miserable their lives were made. It all showed a great confidence, not in themselves, but in their God.

As we look at the church today, what do we see? Some of God’s people are taking up their crosses, and denying the world and the lust thereof, other people are not. Is the church of today still known for being confident in their God?

As professing Christians, have we lost some of this biblical confidence? Are we still out there undeniably serving the one true God? Do people look at us, and stand in awe of the confidence we are displaying in our God? Too many people of today are saying they are Christians, but they demonstrate very little confidence in God. They live quite closely to the ways of the world. Instead of enjoying persecution, they enjoy many of the same things that the world does. Each of us needs the fire of God burning deep within our hearts, a fire that cannot be quenched.

Confidence equals obedience. I have met many Christians of our day whose ancestors gave their lives for Christ, and their grandfathers bravely led the church, but there now seems to be something missing. As I interact with many God-fearing Christians, it seems that there is a prevailing struggle with confidence—a confidence in a living God who is all-powerful, all-knowing, and all-present.

In the uncertainty of our world today, we need to once more boldly proclaim the gospel message just like true believers did in times past. We need to clearly draw distinct biblical lines between right and wrong. We need to rid ourselves of all these wretched gray areas and call sin, sin. It seems that we have lost the confidence to speak out against the sin of our day. If we confidently proclaim what God has declared, there are some people who will not like us. We need brethren that are not afraid to be scoffed at and are willing to take the road less traveled.

Right before our Lord ascended on high, He gave His disciples a glorious promise, …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

Ye shall receive power! Not power from men, not power from kingdoms of this world, but real, overcoming power—power that comes only from the Holy Ghost! After we receive this power, we go forward as a new creature, confidently proclaiming the blessed Gospel of our Redeemer.

We need hearts that burn with God’s will and God’s word. We need hearts aflame!

I was eating lunch one day when a couple approached me with a serious question, “Why does the church think it has to control us?” After they explained how they think they should be able to be ‘free in Christ’, I was excited to answer their questions. However, there was another ordained brother sitting beside me. So, I decided to wait, hoping that he would engage the couple, but he said nothing. As another forty-five minutes passed, I tried to explain to the couple how they needed to deny themselves and submit to the church. And that if they laid down their lives fully, if they surrendered all, they would no longer have such a struggle with church structure.

The couple seemed encouraged and ready to give things another try. However, the minister beside me did not seem too pleased, so I asked him what he thought. He said that his father told him years ago that when he was young, he thought he had all the answers. After he got old, he realized he did not know anything, and that church issues are too complicated to solve. We need to just try to get along.

Is this the answer, to just act like we don’t know anything and hope that it all works out in the end? I do understand that we don’t have all the answers. After all, I realize that I have more questions than answers most times. However, I do know what God wants for His church! …Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

A glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish! Will we, as God’s people, once again stand for truth, deny the world, and like sheep allow ourselves to be led to the slaughter? Or have we made our lives too comfortable to deny, have we chosen the easy (broad) way and denied the straight and narrow? Have we signed a peace deal with the servants of sin? If I weep as I write, will you weep as you read?

The definition of the word confidence is a feeling or consciousness of one’s powers. Many people today have confused confidence with pride, and for good reason. Most people that are confident are confident in themselves, instead of being confident in Christ. We see this self-confidence all around us. There are life coaches and counselors all over the globe, telling people to believe in themselves, telling them to be confident in themselves. When one is confident in themselves, they often do become proud. Remember the world does not look down on pride. You can hear the world boast of its pride everywhere you look. People are proud of their children, proud of their country, proud of their favorite sports team, proud of their lawns, proud of basically everything that is good in their lives. We must remember that pride is sin and will not enter heaven. While confidence in one’s self or things is pride, confidence in God is not!

It is not a new concept to confuse confidence in God, with pride. David’s oldest brother Eliab said to him, “I know thy pride”. Was David proud? No, he simply had a great deal of confidence in his God.

Could it be that a false sense of humility has silenced the church? Could it be that this tactic of the enemy is one of Satan’s current weapons against Christians? Could it also be the reason that the Church seems to be struggling in all parts of the world? What if faithful men would once again step out in faith in their God with great confidence and by their words and actions show this sinned-stained world the straight and narrow way—into the Kingdom of God?!

We all must agree, we live in a confused world—one that is confused as to what is right and what is wrong. What if the world could look at the Church and once again find a group of people that know exactly where they are going—a church that has no doubt which way is the right way—a church that can boldly proclaim the answer to the problems of our day—a church that is nothing less than completely confident in their GOD?

Let us come before our God on bended knee, with our hearts bowed low, demonstrating genuine godly sorrow for where we have lost our way. Let us earnestly seek God’s will for ourselves, for our families, for our churches, and for our neighbors. Let us ask God to show us how we can be His examples to the world around us. The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn; To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified –Isaiah 61:1-3.

ঈশ্বরের বাক্য পড়তে পড়তে আমি বারবার একটি বিষয় লক্ষ করেছি—ঈশ্বরের লোকেরা আত্মবিশ্বাসী। নোহের কথা ভাবুন। ঈশ্বর যখন তাঁকে একটি জাহাজ বানাতে বললেন, তখন তিনি একটুও দ্বিধা করেননি। পরবর্তী ১২০ বছর তিনি আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে ঠিক সেই কাজটিই করে গেছেন। তারপর মনে পড়ে অব্রাহামের কথা—ঈশ্বর তাঁর কাছে যা-ই চেয়েছেন, তিনি আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে তা-ই করেছেন, এমনকি যখন ঈশ্বর তাঁকে তাঁর একমাত্র পুত্রকে উৎসর্গ করতে বলেছিলেন। কালেব ও যিহোশূয়ের কথা উল্লেখ না করে আত্মবিশ্বাসের কথা বলা যায় না। তাঁদের সঙ্গীরা যখন সংশয়ে ভরা প্রতিবেদন দিল, তখন তাঁরা আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে বললেন, এই নতুন কনান দেশে তাঁদের কী করা উচিত: …এখনই চল, আমরা উঠে গিয়ে দেশ অধিকার করি; কেননা আমরা তা জয় করতে অবশ্যই সক্ষম—গণনাপুস্তক ১৩:৩০।

দায়ূদের কথাও আমরা ভুলতে পারি না, যিনি এগিয়ে গিয়ে সেই বড় বিরোধী—গলিয়াতকে—চুপ করিয়েছিলেন। দানিয়েল, গিদিয়োন, ইয়োব, যিহিষ্কেল, যিশাইয় কিংবা যিরমিয়ের কথাও আমরা ভুলতে পারি না, আর আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে তাঁরা যা কিছু করেছিলেন, তাও নয়। বিশ্বাসী এই প্রত্যেক পুরুষ এবং আরও অনেকের জীবন অধ্যয়ন করলে আমরা স্পষ্ট দেখতে পাই, তাঁদের ঈশ্বরের প্রতি তাঁদের গভীর আত্মবিশ্বাস ছিল!

কেউ কেউ হয়তো বলবেন, ঈশ্বর যদি আজও সেই আগেকার মতো কাজ করতেন, তাহলে আমরা আরও আত্মবিশ্বাসী হতাম। ঈশ্বর যদি এখনও পুরাতন নিয়মের ঈশ্বর হতেন, তাহলে হয়তো সহজ হতো। তিনি যদি আমাদের যুদ্ধে পরিচালনা করতেন, শত্রুদের ধ্বংস করতেন, সমুদ্র ভাগ করতেন এবং আকাশ থেকে রুটি বর্ষণ করতেন, তাহলে আমরা তাঁর প্রতি আরও আত্মবিশ্বাসী হতাম।

এবার নতুন নিয়মের কথা ভাবা যাক। এটি বেশ আলাদা। ঈশ্বরের লোকদের খ্রিষ্টের জন্য সবকিছু ত্যাগ করতে আদেশ করা হয়েছে। তাদের প্রতিশ্রুতি দেওয়া হয়েছে যে জগৎ তাদের ঘৃণা করবে। তাদের বলা হয়েছে, একজন ধনীর পক্ষে ঈশ্বরের রাজ্যে প্রবেশ করা কঠিন। তাদের নিশ্চয়তা দেওয়া হয়েছে যে তারা ধন্য হবে—যদি তারা দুঃখভোগ করে, দরিদ্র হয়, ক্ষুধার্ত হয় এবং শোক করে।

এই পরিস্থিতিতে তাঁর লোকদের অনুসরণ করতে বলেন—এমন একজন ঈশ্বরের ওপর কি মানুষ এখনও আস্থা রাখতে পারে? পারে! শিষ্যরা তা প্রমাণ করেছিলেন। তাঁরা প্রচার ও শিক্ষা দিয়ে বেড়াতেন। তাঁদের বারবার খুঁজে বের করে ধরে নিয়ে যাওয়া হতো এবং প্রহার করা হতো। তারা যখন তাঁর ওপর দাঁত কিড়মিড় করতে এবং তাঁকে পাথর ছুড়ে মারতে শুরু করল, তখন নিপীড়কদের সামনে উপস্থিত হয়েও পরিচারক স্তিফান দারুণ আত্মবিশ্বাস দেখিয়েছিলেন। শেষ যন্ত্রণাভরা নিঃশ্বাস ত্যাগ করা পর্যন্ত স্তিফান আত্মবিশ্বাস ধরে রেখেছিলেন।

প্রেরিত পৌল হওয়ার আগে শৌল ছিলেন ক্রুশের শত্রু, পাপীদের মধ্যে প্রধান এবং ফরীশীদের মধ্যে ফরীশী। তিনি ছিলেন একজন প্রভাবশালী ব্যক্তি, শ্রেষ্ঠ শিক্ষকদের কাছে শিক্ষাপ্রাপ্ত। তারপর তিনি জীবন্ত ঈশ্বরের সাক্ষাৎ পেলেন, আর সবকিছু বদলে গেল। পৌল বাপ্তিস্ম নেওয়ার পর …অবিলম্বে সমাজগৃহে খ্রিষ্টের বিষয়ে প্রচার করতে লাগলেন যে, তিনিই ঈশ্বরের পুত্র—প্রেরিত ৯:২০। পরের পদে বলা হয়েছে, লোকেরা বিস্মিত হয়েছিল; তারপর ২৩ পদে, তাঁর বাপ্তিস্মের মাত্র পাঁচ পদ পরে, বলা হয়েছে যে যিহুদিরা তাঁকে হত্যা করার পরামর্শ করল।

এমন একজন মানুষকে বদলে দিতে, রাতারাতি তাঁর আনুগত্য সম্পূর্ণ পাল্টে দিতে, ঈশ্বরের প্রতি গভীর আত্মবিশ্বাস প্রয়োজন। পৌলের নিজের সাক্ষ্য অনুযায়ী, তিনি মৃত্যু পর্যন্ত বিশ্বস্ত ছিলেন: কেননা এখন আমি উৎসর্গিত হইবার উপক্রম হইয়াছি, এবং আমার প্রস্থানের সময় উপস্থিত। আমি উত্তম যুদ্ধে প্রাণপণ করিয়াছি, নিরূপিত পথের শেষ পর্যন্ত দৌড়িয়াছি, বিশ্বাস রক্ষা করিয়াছি—২ তীমথিয় ৪:৬-৭।

নতুন নিয়মে ঈশ্বর আশ্চর্য কাজ করেছিলেন। তিনি অন্ধদের সুস্থ করেছিলেন এবং মৃতদের আবার জীবিত করেছিলেন। তিনি বন্দিদের মুক্ত করেছিলেন এবং মানুষকে আঘাত করে হত্যা করেছিলেন। কেউ কেউ হয়তো বলবেন, যিশু যখন শারীরিকভাবে এই পৃথিবীতে হেঁটে বেড়াতেন ও কথা বলতেন, সেই বাইবেলের নতুন নিয়মের যুগে আমরা যদি এখনও বাস করতাম, তাহলে ঈশ্বরের ওপর গভীর আত্মবিশ্বাস রাখা সহজ হতো।

বাইবেলের পরের সময়ের কথা?

প্রাথমিক মণ্ডলীতে আমরা আবার এমন একদল মানুষকে দেখি, যারা টলেনি; তারা তাদের ঈশ্বরের ওপর আস্থা রেখেছিল—এমন এক ঈশ্বরের ওপর, যাঁকে তারা দেখতে পেত না। ঈশ্বরের অগণিত লোক সাহসের সঙ্গে জগতের সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে তার দুষ্টতার কথা ঘোষণা করেছিল, আর ঈশ্বরের অগণিত লোককে হত্যা করা হয়েছিল। এই লোকদের আত্মবিশ্বাস নিয়ে কখনও প্রশ্ন তোলা হয়নি। “যে ঈশ্বরকে তারা দেখতে পায় না”, তাঁকে বিশ্বাস করার জন্য তাদের মূর্খ বলা হতো। তাদের ‘মূর্খতার’ জন্য উপহাস ও তাচ্ছিল্য করা হতো; তাদের …সারা দিনই বধ করা হইত…—গীতসংহিতা ৪৪:২২। লোকেরা তাদের আচার-আচরণ নিয়ে প্রশ্ন তুলত, তাদের ধর্মীয় কাঠামো নিয়ে প্রশ্ন তুলত, তাদের প্রচারিত বার্তা নিয়ে প্রশ্ন তুলত, অনেক বিষয় নিয়েই প্রশ্ন তুলত—কিন্তু তাদের আত্মবিশ্বাস নিয়ে কখনও প্রশ্ন তুলত না। এই খ্রিষ্টানরা তাদের ঈশ্বরে বিশ্বাস করত—এ বিষয়ে কোনো সন্দেহ ছিল না।

আশ্চর্যের বিষয়, এই জীবনের সুখভোগে তাদের আগ্রহ ছিল না; জগতের বিষয়গুলো নিয়ে তারা চিন্তা করত না, এমনকি তাদের নিজেদের জীবনও তাদের ঈশ্বরের জন্য ত্যাগ করার মতো সামান্য বিষয় ছিল। পরিবারগুলো বিচ্ছিন্ন হয়েছিল, ঘরবাড়ি ও জমিজমা বাজেয়াপ্ত হয়েছিল, গির্জাগুলো পুড়িয়ে দেওয়া হয়েছিল—কিন্তু এসব তাদের থামাতে পারেনি। তারা আরও মহৎ কিছুর জন্য বেঁচেছিল, এমন কিছুর জন্য যা অইহুদিরা বুঝতে পারত না।

প্রাথমিক মণ্ডলীর সময় থেকে সংস্কার আন্দোলনের সময় পর্যন্ত বহু মানুষ দলে দলে রাজ্যে যুক্ত হয়েছিল। হ্যাঁ, শিশুরা বড় হয়ে তাদের বাবা-মায়ের মণ্ডলীতে যোগ দিয়েছিল, কিন্তু জগৎ থেকেও দলে দলে নতুন বিশ্বাসী এসেছিল। জগতের একজন মানুষকে কীভাবে এমন একটি দলে যোগ দিতে রাজি করানো সম্ভব—যে দলকে তাড়া করে হত্যা করা হতো, যে দল যিশু খ্রিষ্টের মণ্ডলীর মতোই দুঃখভোগ করত? হ্যাঁ, আমরা জানি পরিত্রাণ প্রভুর কাছ থেকেই আসে, কিন্তু ঈশ্বরের লোকদের আত্মবিশ্বাসই অন্যদের বিস্মিত করত, তাদের এই ‘ধর্মদ্রোহীদের’ নতুন ধর্মটি গুরুত্ব দিয়ে বিবেচনা করতে বাধ্য করত। এ ছিল এমন একদল মানুষ, যারা আনন্দের সঙ্গে নিজেদের সম্পদ লুট হতে দিত, অন্যদের সাহায্য করার জন্য তাদের যা ছিল সব দিতে খুশি হতো, এবং কর্তৃপক্ষের হাতে ধরা পড়লেও বাধা দিত না। যিশু খ্রিষ্টের প্রকৃত মণ্ডলী ছিল এমন একদল মানুষ, যাদের দেখে অন্যরা সবসময় অবাক হয়ে জিজ্ঞাসা করত, “এরা কারা?” তারা স্পষ্টতই তাদের সমস্ত বিশ্বাস ঈশ্বরের ওপর রেখেছিল, আর তা ছিল বিরল ঘটনা। আগুন যতই প্রচণ্ড জ্বলুক, তাদের জীবন যতই দুর্বিষহ করে তোলা হোক, তারা ঈশ্বরের সত্যের পক্ষে দাঁড়িয়েছিল। এসবই দেখিয়েছিল যে তাদের গভীর আত্মবিশ্বাস নিজেদের ওপর নয়, বরং ঈশ্বরের ওপর।

আজকের মণ্ডলীর দিকে তাকালে আমরা কী দেখি? ঈশ্বরের কিছু লোক নিজেদের ক্রুশ তুলে নিচ্ছে, জগৎ ও তার কামনা-বাসনা অস্বীকার করছে; অন্যেরা তা করছে না। আজকের মণ্ডলী কি এখনও ঈশ্বরের ওপর আস্থার জন্য পরিচিত?

খ্রিষ্টান বলে দাবি করি আমরা—আমরা কি এই বাইবেলসম্মত আত্মবিশ্বাসের কিছুটা হারিয়েছি? আমরা কি এখনও দৃঢ়ভাবে একমাত্র সত্য ঈশ্বরের সেবা করছি? ঈশ্বরের প্রতি আমাদের প্রদর্শিত আত্মবিশ্বাস দেখে লোকেরা কি আমাদের দিকে তাকিয়ে বিস্মিত হয়? আজ অনেক বেশি মানুষ নিজেদের খ্রিষ্টান বলে, অথচ ঈশ্বরের ওপর তাদের আত্মবিশ্বাস খুব সামান্যই। তারা জগতের রীতির খুব কাছাকাছি জীবনযাপন করে। নির্যাতন উপভোগ করার বদলে, তারা জগতের মতোই অনেক বিষয় উপভোগ করে। আমাদের প্রত্যেকের হৃদয়ের গভীরে ঈশ্বরের আগুন জ্বলতে থাকা দরকার—এমন আগুন, যা নেভানো যায় না।

আত্মবিশ্বাস মানেই আনুগত্য। আমাদের সময়ের এমন অনেক খ্রিষ্টানের সঙ্গে আমার পরিচয় হয়েছে, যাদের পূর্বপুরুষেরা খ্রিষ্টের জন্য প্রাণ দিয়েছিলেন এবং যাদের পিতামহেরা সাহসের সঙ্গে মণ্ডলী পরিচালনা করেছিলেন; কিন্তু এখন যেন কিছু একটা অনুপস্থিত। ঈশ্বরভীরু অনেক খ্রিষ্টানের সঙ্গে মেলামেশা করতে গিয়ে মনে হয়, আত্মবিশ্বাস নিয়ে এক ব্যাপক সংগ্রাম চলছে—এমন এক জীবন্ত ঈশ্বরের ওপর আত্মবিশ্বাস, যিনি সর্বশক্তিমান, সর্বজ্ঞ এবং সর্বত্র উপস্থিত।

আজকের পৃথিবীর অনিশ্চয়তার মধ্যে অতীতের প্রকৃত বিশ্বাসীদের মতো আমাদেরও আবার সাহসের সঙ্গে সুসমাচারের বার্তা ঘোষণা করতে হবে। সঠিক ও ভুলের মধ্যে বাইবেলসম্মত স্পষ্ট সীমারেখা টানতে হবে। এই সব জঘন্য ধূসর ক্ষেত্র থেকে আমাদের মুক্ত হতে হবে এবং পাপকে পাপ বলতে হবে। মনে হয়, আমাদের সময়ের পাপের বিরুদ্ধে কথা বলার আত্মবিশ্বাস আমরা হারিয়ে ফেলেছি। ঈশ্বর যা ঘোষণা করেছেন তা যদি আমরা আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে প্রচার করি, তাহলে কিছু লোক আমাদের পছন্দ করবে না। এমন ভাইদের আমাদের দরকার, যারা উপহাসের ভয় পান না এবং কম-চলা পথ বেছে নিতে প্রস্তুত।

আমাদের প্রভু ঊর্ধ্বলোকে আরোহণ করার ঠিক আগে তাঁর শিষ্যদের এক মহিমান্বিত প্রতিশ্রুতি দিয়েছিলেন: …পবিত্র আত্মা তোমাদের উপরে আসিলে তোমরা শক্তি প্রাপ্ত হইবে; আর তোমরা যিরূশালেমে, সমুদয় যিহূদিয়া ও শমরিয়া দেশে, এবং পৃথিবীর প্রান্ত পর্যন্ত আমার সাক্ষী হইবে—প্রেরিত ১:৮।

তোমরা শক্তি প্রাপ্ত হইবে! মানুষের কাছ থেকে শক্তি নয়, এই জগতের রাজ্যগুলো থেকে শক্তি নয়, বরং প্রকৃত, জয়ী হওয়ার শক্তি—যে শক্তি কেবল পবিত্র আত্মা থেকেই আসে! এই শক্তি পাওয়ার পর আমরা নতুন সৃষ্টি হয়ে এগিয়ে যাই, আমাদের মুক্তিদাতার ধন্য সুসমাচার আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে ঘোষণা করি।

ঈশ্বরের ইচ্ছা ও ঈশ্বরের বাক্যে প্রজ্বলিত হৃদয় আমাদের প্রয়োজন। আমাদের হৃদয় আগুনের মতো জ্বলুক!

একদিন দুপুরের খাবার খাওয়ার সময় এক দম্পতি আমার কাছে এসে একটি গুরুতর প্রশ্ন করলেন, “মণ্ডলী কেন মনে করে যে আমাদের নিয়ন্ত্রণ করতে হবে?” ‘খ্রিষ্টে স্বাধীন’ হতে পারা উচিত বলে তাঁরা কী বোঝান তা ব্যাখ্যা করার পর, তাঁদের প্রশ্নের উত্তর দিতে আমি আগ্রহী হলাম। কিন্তু আমার পাশে আরেকজন অভিষিক্ত ভাই বসেছিলেন। তাই আমি অপেক্ষা করার সিদ্ধান্ত নিলাম, আশা করলাম তিনি দম্পতির সঙ্গে কথা বলবেন; কিন্তু তিনি কিছুই বললেন না। আরও পঁয়তাল্লিশ মিনিট কেটে যাওয়ার পর আমি দম্পতিকে বোঝানোর চেষ্টা করলাম যে তাঁদের নিজেদের অস্বীকার করে মণ্ডলীর কাছে সমর্পিত হওয়া দরকার। আর তাঁরা যদি সম্পূর্ণভাবে নিজেদের জীবন সমর্পণ করেন, সবকিছু ছেড়ে দেন, তাহলে মণ্ডলীর কাঠামো নিয়ে তাঁদের আর এমন সংগ্রাম থাকবে না।

দম্পতিকে উৎসাহিত মনে হলো, তাঁরা আরেকবার চেষ্টা করতেও প্রস্তুত ছিলেন। কিন্তু আমার পাশে বসা পরিচারককে খুব সন্তুষ্ট মনে হলো না, তাই আমি তাঁকে জিজ্ঞাসা করলাম, তিনি কী ভাবছেন। তিনি বললেন, বহু বছর আগে তাঁর বাবা তাঁকে বলেছিলেন যে, তিনি যখন তরুণ ছিলেন, তখন ভাবতেন তাঁর কাছে সব প্রশ্নের উত্তর আছে। বৃদ্ধ হওয়ার পর তিনি বুঝেছিলেন, তিনি কিছুই জানেন না, আর মণ্ডলীর সমস্যাগুলো সমাধান করার পক্ষে খুব জটিল। আমাদের শুধু মিলেমিশে থাকার চেষ্টা করা উচিত।

এটাই কি উত্তর—আমরা কিছুই জানি না এমন ভান করে বসে থাকা এবং আশা করা যে শেষ পর্যন্ত সব ঠিক হয়ে যাবে? আমি বুঝি যে আমাদের কাছে সব প্রশ্নের উত্তর নেই। সত্যি বলতে, বেশিরভাগ সময় আমি বুঝতে পারি, উত্তরের চেয়ে আমার প্রশ্নই বেশি। কিন্তু ঈশ্বর তাঁর মণ্ডলীর জন্য কী চান, তা আমি জানি! …খ্রিষ্টও মণ্ডলীকে প্রেম করিলেন, আর তাহার নিমিত্ত আপনাকে প্রদান করিলেন; যেন বাক্য দ্বারা জলস্নানে তাহাকে শুচি করিয়া পবিত্র করেন; যেন মণ্ডলীকে নিজের নিকটে তেজস্বিনী অবস্থায় উপস্থিত করেন, তাহার কলঙ্ক কি বলিরেখা কি তদ্রূপ অন্য কিছুর অভাব না হয়, বরং সে যেন পবিত্র ও নির্দোষ হয়—ইফিষীয় ৫:২৫-২৭।

তেজস্বিনী মণ্ডলী, যার কলঙ্ক বা বলিরেখা কিংবা তেমন আর কিছু নেই; বরং সে পবিত্র ও নির্দোষ! ঈশ্বরের লোক হিসেবে আমরা কি আবার সত্যের পক্ষে দাঁড়াব, জগৎকে অস্বীকার করব এবং মেষের মতো নিজেদের বধ্যভূমিতে নিয়ে যেতে দেব? নাকি আমরা নিজেদের জীবনকে অস্বীকার করার পক্ষে অতিরিক্ত আরামদায়ক করে তুলেছি, সহজ (প্রশস্ত) পথ বেছে নিয়ে সরু ও সংকীর্ণ পথকে অস্বীকার করেছি? আমরা কি পাপের দাসদের সঙ্গে শান্তিচুক্তি করেছি? লিখতে লিখতে আমি যদি কাঁদি, পড়তে পড়তে আপনারাও কি কাঁদবেন?

আত্মবিশ্বাস শব্দটির সংজ্ঞা হলো নিজের ক্ষমতা সম্পর্কে অনুভূতি বা সচেতনতা। আজ অনেকেই আত্মবিশ্বাসকে অহংকার বলে ভুল করেছেন, এবং তার যথেষ্ট কারণও আছে। আত্মবিশ্বাসী অধিকাংশ মানুষ খ্রিষ্টে আত্মবিশ্বাসী হওয়ার বদলে নিজেদের ওপর আস্থা রাখে। এই আত্মনির্ভর আত্মবিশ্বাস আমরা চারদিকে দেখি। পৃথিবীজুড়ে জীবন-পরামর্শদাতা ও পরামর্শকরা মানুষকে নিজেদের ওপর বিশ্বাস রাখতে, নিজেদের সম্পর্কে আত্মবিশ্বাসী হতে বলছেন। কেউ নিজের ওপর আত্মবিশ্বাসী হলে প্রায়ই সে অহংকারী হয়ে ওঠে। মনে রাখবেন, জগৎ অহংকারকে নিন্দা করে না। যেদিকে তাকান, সর্বত্রই জগতের অহংকারের বড়াই শুনতে পাবেন। মানুষ তাদের সন্তানদের নিয়ে গর্ব করে, দেশ নিয়ে গর্ব করে, প্রিয় ক্রীড়াদল নিয়ে গর্ব করে, নিজেদের উঠোন নিয়ে গর্ব করে—জীবনের প্রায় সব ভালো বিষয় নিয়েই গর্ব করে। আমাদের মনে রাখতে হবে, অহংকার পাপ এবং তা স্বর্গে প্রবেশ করবে না। নিজের ওপর বা কোনো কিছুর ওপর আত্মবিশ্বাস অহংকার; কিন্তু ঈশ্বরের ওপর আত্মবিশ্বাস অহংকার নয়!

ঈশ্বরের ওপর আত্মবিশ্বাসকে অহংকার বলে ভুল করা নতুন কোনো ধারণা নয়। দায়ূদের বড় ভাই ইলীয়াব তাঁকে বলেছিলেন, “আমি তোমার অহংকার জানি।” দায়ূদ কি অহংকারী ছিলেন? না, তাঁর ঈশ্বরের ওপর কেবল গভীর আস্থা ছিল।

এমন কি হতে পারে যে মিথ্যা নম্রতার ধারণা মণ্ডলীকে নীরব করে দিয়েছে? এমন কি হতে পারে যে শত্রুর এই কৌশল খ্রিষ্টানদের বিরুদ্ধে শয়তানের বর্তমান অস্ত্রগুলোর একটি? পৃথিবীর সব অঞ্চলে মণ্ডলী যে সংগ্রাম করছে বলে মনে হয়, এর কারণ কি এটিও হতে পারে? বিশ্বস্ত পুরুষেরা যদি আবারও ঈশ্বরের ওপর বিশ্বাস রেখে গভীর আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে এগিয়ে আসতেন, এবং কথা ও কাজের মাধ্যমে পাপে কলঙ্কিত এই জগতকে ঈশ্বরের রাজ্যে প্রবেশের সরু ও সংকীর্ণ পথ দেখাতেন, তাহলে কেমন হতো?!

আমাদের সবাইকে একমত হতে হবে—আমরা এক বিভ্রান্ত জগতে বাস করি, যেখানে কোনটা সঠিক আর কোনটা ভুল তা নিয়ে বিভ্রান্তি রয়েছে। জগৎ যদি মণ্ডলীর দিকে তাকিয়ে আবার এমন একদল মানুষকে দেখতে পেত, যারা ঠিক জানে তারা কোথায় যাচ্ছে—এমন এক মণ্ডলী, যার সঠিক পথ কোনটি তা নিয়ে কোনো সন্দেহ নেই—এমন এক মণ্ডলী, যে আমাদের সময়ের সমস্যাগুলোর উত্তর সাহসের সঙ্গে ঘোষণা করতে পারে—এমন এক মণ্ডলী, যে তার ঈশ্বরের ওপর সম্পূর্ণরূপে আত্মবিশ্বাসী, তাহলে কেমন হতো?

নতজানু হয়ে, বিনত হৃদয়ে, যেখানে আমরা পথ হারিয়েছি তার জন্য প্রকৃত ঈশ্বরীয় অনুশোচনা প্রকাশ করে, আসুন আমরা আমাদের ঈশ্বরের সামনে আসি। নিজেদের জন্য, পরিবারের জন্য, মণ্ডলীগুলোর জন্য এবং প্রতিবেশীদের জন্য আন্তরিকভাবে ঈশ্বরের ইচ্ছা খুঁজি। আমাদের চারপাশের জগতের কাছে কীভাবে তাঁর উদাহরণ হতে পারি, তা দেখাতে ঈশ্বরের কাছে প্রার্থনা করি। প্রভু সদাপ্রভুর আত্মা আমার উপরে আছেন; কেননা নম্রদের কাছে সুসমাচার প্রচার করিবার জন্য সদাপ্রভু আমাকে অভিষিক্ত করিয়াছেন; ভগ্নচিত্তদিগকে সুস্থ করিতে, বন্দিদিগকে মুক্তি ঘোষণা করিতে, এবং বদ্ধদিগের কাছে কারাগারের দ্বার খুলিয়া দিতে তিনি আমাকে প্রেরণ করিয়াছেন; সদাপ্রভুর অনুগ্রহের বৎসর ও আমাদের ঈশ্বরের প্রতিশোধের দিন ঘোষণা করিতে, এবং সকল শোককারীর সান্ত্বনা করিতে; সিয়োনের শোককারীদের জন্য ব্যবস্থা করিতে—তাহাদিগকে ভস্মের পরিবর্তে ভূষণ, শোকের পরিবর্তে আনন্দতৈল, ভারাক্রান্ত আত্মার পরিবর্তে প্রশংসার পরিচ্ছদ দিতে; যেন তাহারা ধার্মিকতার বৃক্ষ, সদাপ্রভুর রোপণ নামে আখ্যাত হয়, এবং তিনি মহিমান্বিত হন—যিশাইয় ৬১:১-৩।

Greetings of Christian love to one and all. This past year and a half have been challenging in one way or another for most people. My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing –James 1:2-4.

We trust that no matter what each of you has faced your inner motivation echoes with the words of Apostle Paul, … for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. –Philippians 4:11-13.

As we are already almost halfway through another year, I stop to consider how time keeps disappearing at an ever-increasing rate of speed. For many, the last 16 to 18 months have been quite challenging as the Covid-19 pandemic and its aftereffects continue to wreak havoc with all that used to be considered normal. For us, some of these aftereffects have hindered us from getting this issue of the magazine out in a timely manner. Our apologies. However, things are back on track to be able to get the next issue out within the next several months, thus allowing us to get back onto our normal schedule once more.

I see the pandemic and the resulting aftereffects as quite similar to one big traffic jam. First, many vehicles are all traveling along quite smoothly at the speed limit. Gradually more and more vehicles join the flow, until the highway becomes quite congested. However, things still continue to flow unhindered until suddenly one vehicle brakes sharply and swerves to avoid some debris on the roadway. Immediately, there is a ripple-effect or domino-effect, as each vehicle brakes to avoid hitting the one in front of them that just applied their brakes. I have seen this type of situation create stop-and-go traffic for a mile or more as traffic slows to a crawl, then once each vehicle finally gets past the offending object they can once more accelerate to their previous rate of speed.

With our world’s economies, both local and global, the same thing seemingly has happened, howbeit on a much, much larger scale. First came the shutdowns, both local and national, causing businesses to lose production and sales. Then as businesses reopened and their workers began to get sick, further production was lost. Suddenly, many manufacturers found themselves behind in their inventory reserve, which graduated into being behind in their ability to supply the demand. Since so much of our world’s businesses have developed trade at a global level, there are many products that are not available for sale as manufacturers wait for the “company overseas” to once more have enough supply to meet the global demand. Another problem that has developed more recently is that due to the major imbalance of supply versus demand on a global level, the cost of purchase for many products has skyrocketed awakening fears among some economists of a global crisis due to inflation.

Where does this leave the church? It seems that the “enemy of our souls” has used this global event to cause churches everywhere to struggle on many levels. I have on my bookshelf a book titled Conscience in Crisis, which is about church history. This book specifically examines the struggle of the “peace” churches in colonial America. One of the key points the book focuses on is that the global events of that time period shook the very foundations of their faith and practice. This caused the collective conscience of the churches to face an unprecedented crisis level, which many individuals never overcame. Some gave up the faith, some quit going to church, some walked away from their church and started going to more worldly churches. And the ones that remained, struggled substantially through many issues until they once more were considered stable.

Our Perspective Matters

When I think of the word perspective, the definition I am using is: a particular attitude toward, or way, of regarding something; a point of view. It is like the prescription of the glasses we have in front of our eyes causing us to see things in a distorted manner or with a clear 20/20 view. Or it is like using a filter in your computer or in your vehicle engine, which only lets through that which is pre-determined should be allowed.

So, our perspective is akin to using a filter or a pair of glasses. Our perspective is shaped by many things: the way we were trained as children, the role models we chose to follow during our formative years, the reading material we absorbed, the spiritual mentors we opened our hearts to, and the peers we embraced throughout our lifetime. Also, our perspective determines how we look at situations, how we interact with God, how we view sin and salvation, and how we respond to both friends and enemies.

In our world today, there are many perspectives, all vying for our allegiance. Many are the “special interest” groups clamoring for our support of their cause. There’s race discrimination on both sides of the matter. There are voices crying “foul” in their effort to gain support and an advantage against their opponents regarding voting rights, honesty of the election outcomes, and desired legislative changes to the judicial system and the Constitution. While there have always been multiple sides to an issue, there has usually been an effort to work together for the good of all. However, in the last number of years it seems that numerous issues have become quite divisive to the point of polarizing the people into two camps. The balance of power in government has been swinging back and forth from the one side to the other. This polarization has been causing bitterness and anger to build, in some instances erupting into violence and vandalism. In other instances, it has caused normally level-headed individuals to lose their cool and make “knee-jerk” reactionary decisions which are totally out of character for them.

In the midst of all this chaos and confusion, what is our perspective as the church? Are we remaining steadfast in allowing God and His Word to mold and shape our perspective to be aligned with His perspective? Or have we allowed the pressure of one peer group or another to start pushing us off-course in our walk as strangers and pilgrims?

I have heard reports of some churches in other parts of the world being pushed by their local government to not meet for fellowship and group worship. There are families whose conscience chooses to obey the government in long-term mask wearing and social distancing. Individuals have become discouraged. Families have become isolated. And churches have struggled through one issue after another in their efforts to maintain peace among the brethren.

As I have interacted with people who are not regular church goers, or those who attend a “dying” church, an “older” church, or a “small country” church, there are numerous things I have heard them testify regarding the churches of the conservative, Anabaptist persuasion. These people are awed by the way we help each other both on a regular basis and when tragedy strikes. They can’t comprehend the large size of our weddings and especially our funerals. They don’t understand how our children are mild-mannered and respectful of others.

Let’s take heed and use wisdom as we continue facing the challenges in the days to come. From my limited vantage point, I believe that long-term mask wearing and social distancing that is practiced at the expense of normal worship as we understand the Scriptures to teach, will eventually have a negative ripple effect on us as believers.

Many years ago, as I was involved in learning from the “counseling model”, it was spoken of as quite troubling and detrimental to interpersonal relationships IF someone had a “mask” on (figuratively). As I have evaluated and considered the long-term effect of a person having a “mask” on (literally), I believe it WILL cause as much and more detriment to interpersonal relationships. There is something about visiting with brothers and sisters of the faith when you can see their whole face. Without even realizing it, we read body language and facial expressions, which aids in understanding and conveying thoughts as we communicate with one another. Thus, it is my personal opinion that long-term mask wearing and social distancing by a local church body will eventually degrade the level of spiritual life and fervor to the point of someday that local body will no longer stand out from all the rest of the nominal Christians around them.

May God bless each one. May we not give up the spiritual fight. May we ever keep our eyes fixed on our Father, our Saviour, and our eternal home.

Curvin L Wenger

Saudações de amor cristão a todos. Este último ano e meio foi desafiador, de uma forma ou de outra, para a maioria das pessoas. Meus irmãos, tende por motivo de grande alegria o passardes por várias provações, sabendo que a provação da vossa fé produz perseverança. Ora, a perseverança deve ter ação completa, para que sejais perfeitos e íntegros, em nada deficientes –Tiago 1:2-4.

Confiamos que, não importa o que cada um de vocês tenha enfrentado, sua motivação interior ecoe as palavras do apóstolo Paulo: … pois aprendi a estar contente em qualquer situação em que me encontre. Sei passar necessidade e sei também ter abundância; em toda e qualquer situação, aprendi o segredo de estar alimentado e de passar fome, de ter abundância e de padecer necessidade. Tudo posso naquele que me fortalece. –Filipenses 4:11-13.

Como já estamos quase na metade de mais um ano, paro para refletir sobre como o tempo continua desaparecendo a uma velocidade cada vez maior. Para muitos, os últimos 16 a 18 meses foram bastante desafiadores, pois a pandemia de Covid-19 e seus efeitos posteriores continuam causando estragos em tudo o que antes era considerado normal. Para nós, alguns desses efeitos posteriores nos impediram de publicar esta edição da revista em tempo hábil. Pedimos desculpas. No entanto, as coisas voltaram aos trilhos, e poderemos publicar a próxima edição nos próximos meses, voltando assim mais uma vez à nossa programação normal.

Vejo a pandemia e os efeitos posteriores resultantes como algo bastante parecido com um grande engarrafamento. Primeiro, muitos veículos seguem todos tranquilamente, no limite de velocidade. Aos poucos, mais e mais veículos se juntam ao fluxo, até que a rodovia fica bastante congestionada. No entanto, o trânsito continua fluindo sem impedimentos até que, de repente, um veículo freia bruscamente e desvia para evitar alguns detritos na pista. Imediatamente, ocorre um efeito de ondulação ou dominó, à medida que cada veículo freia para evitar atingir o que está à sua frente, que acabou de frear. Já vi esse tipo de situação provocar um trânsito de anda e para por um quilômetro ou mais, enquanto os veículos avançam lentamente; depois que cada veículo finalmente passa pelo obstáculo, pode voltar a acelerar até a velocidade anterior.

Com as economias do nosso mundo, tanto locais quanto globais, parece ter acontecido o mesmo, embora em uma escala muito, muito maior. Primeiro vieram os fechamentos, tanto locais quanto nacionais, fazendo com que as empresas perdessem produção e vendas. Depois, quando as empresas reabriram e seus trabalhadores começaram a adoecer, perdeu-se ainda mais produção. De repente, muitos fabricantes perceberam que seus estoques de reserva estavam abaixo do necessário, o que acabou se traduzindo em incapacidade de atender à demanda. Como tantas empresas do nosso mundo desenvolveram o comércio em escala global, muitos produtos não estão disponíveis para venda enquanto os fabricantes esperam que a “empresa no exterior” volte a ter oferta suficiente para atender à demanda global. Outro problema que surgiu mais recentemente é que, devido ao grande desequilíbrio global entre oferta e demanda, o custo de compra de muitos produtos disparou, despertando em alguns economistas o temor de uma crise global causada pela inflação.

O que isso significa para a igreja? Parece que o “inimigo de nossas almas” usou esse acontecimento global para fazer com que igrejas de toda parte enfrentassem dificuldades em muitos níveis. Tenho na estante um livro intitulado Conscience in Crisis, sobre a história da igreja. Esse livro examina especificamente a luta das igrejas da “paz” na América colonial. Um dos pontos principais abordados pelo livro é que os acontecimentos globais daquele período abalaram os próprios alicerces de sua fé e prática. Isso fez com que a consciência coletiva das igrejas enfrentasse uma crise sem precedentes, que muitos indivíduos nunca superaram. Alguns abandonaram a fé, alguns deixaram de ir à igreja, alguns se afastaram de sua igreja e começaram a frequentar igrejas mais mundanas. E os que permaneceram lutaram intensamente com muitas questões até que, mais uma vez, fossem considerados estáveis.

Nossa perspectiva importa

Quando penso na palavra perspectiva, a definição que estou usando é: uma atitude particular em relação a algo, ou uma maneira de considerá-lo; um ponto de vista. É como a prescrição dos óculos que temos diante dos olhos, fazendo-nos ver as coisas de maneira distorcida ou com uma visão nítida, perfeita. Ou é como usar um filtro no computador ou no motor do veículo, que só deixa passar aquilo que foi previamente determinado como permitido.

Assim, nossa perspectiva é semelhante ao uso de um filtro ou de um par de óculos. Nossa perspectiva é moldada por muitas coisas: a maneira como fomos ensinados quando crianças, os modelos que escolhemos seguir durante nossos anos de formação, o material de leitura que absorvemos, os mentores espirituais a quem abrimos o coração e os companheiros que acolhemos ao longo da vida. Além disso, nossa perspectiva determina como encaramos as situações, como nos relacionamos com Deus, como vemos o pecado e a salvação e como respondemos tanto a amigos quanto a inimigos.

Em nosso mundo de hoje, há muitas perspectivas, todas disputando nossa lealdade. São muitos os grupos de “interesses especiais” que clamam por nosso apoio à sua causa. Há discriminação racial dos dois lados da questão. Há vozes que gritam “injustiça” em seus esforços para obter apoio e vantagem contra seus adversários em questões como o direito ao voto, a honestidade dos resultados eleitorais e as mudanças legislativas desejadas no sistema judiciário e na Constituição. Embora sempre tenha havido vários lados em uma questão, geralmente houve um esforço para trabalhar em conjunto pelo bem de todos. No entanto, nos últimos anos, parece que numerosas questões se tornaram bastante divisivas, a ponto de polarizar as pessoas em dois grupos. O equilíbrio de poder no governo tem oscilado de um lado para o outro. Essa polarização tem provocado o aumento da amargura e da ira, que em alguns casos irrompem em violência e vandalismo. Em outros casos, fez com que pessoas normalmente ponderadas perdessem a calma e tomassem decisões reativas, “precipitadas”, totalmente fora de seu caráter.

Em meio a todo esse caos e confusão, qual é a nossa perspectiva como igreja? Estamos permanecendo firmes e permitindo que Deus e sua Palavra moldem e formem nossa perspectiva para que esteja alinhada com a dele? Ou permitimos que a pressão de um ou outro grupo de pares comece a nos desviar do caminho em nossa jornada como estrangeiros e peregrinos?

Ouvi relatos de algumas igrejas em outras partes do mundo sendo pressionadas por seus governos locais a não se reunirem para comunhão e culto coletivo. Há famílias cuja consciência escolhe obedecer ao governo usando máscaras por longo prazo e mantendo o distanciamento social. Pessoas ficaram desanimadas. Famílias ficaram isoladas. E as igrejas enfrentaram uma questão após outra em seus esforços para manter a paz entre os irmãos.

Ao conversar com pessoas que não frequentam a igreja regularmente, ou que frequentam uma igreja “moribunda”, uma igreja “mais antiga” ou uma igreja “pequena do interior”, ouvi muitas delas testemunharem sobre as igrejas de orientação anabatista conservadora. Essas pessoas ficam admiradas com a maneira como nos ajudamos, tanto regularmente quanto quando ocorre uma tragédia. Não conseguem compreender o grande número de pessoas em nossos casamentos e, sobretudo, em nossos funerais. Não entendem como nossos filhos são tranquilos e respeitosos com os outros.

Prestemos atenção e usemos de sabedoria enquanto continuamos a enfrentar os desafios que virão. Do meu ponto de vista limitado, acredito que o uso prolongado de máscaras e o distanciamento social, quando praticados à custa do culto normal, conforme entendemos que as Escrituras ensinam, acabarão tendo um efeito negativo em nós como crentes.

Muitos anos atrás, quando eu estava envolvido no aprendizado do “modelo de aconselhamento”, dizia-se que era bastante problemático e prejudicial às relações interpessoais SE alguém estivesse usando uma “máscara” (figurativamente). Ao avaliar e considerar o efeito a longo prazo de uma pessoa estar usando uma “máscara” (literalmente), acredito que isso CAUSARÁ tanto ou ainda mais prejuízo às relações interpessoais. Há algo especial em visitar irmãos e irmãs na fé quando se pode ver o rosto inteiro deles. Sem sequer perceber, lemos a linguagem corporal e as expressões faciais, o que ajuda a compreender e transmitir pensamentos ao nos comunicarmos uns com os outros. Assim, é minha opinião pessoal que o uso prolongado de máscaras e o distanciamento social por parte de uma comunidade local da igreja acabarão por degradar o nível de vida e fervor espirituais, a ponto de, um dia, essa comunidade local já não se destacar de todos os demais cristãos nominais ao seu redor.

Que Deus abençoe cada um. Que não desistamos da luta espiritual. Que mantenhamos sempre os olhos fixos em nosso Pai, nosso Salvador e nosso lar eterno.

Curvin L Wenger
